cells.date: Śaka 1327, ( nagha-nētra-agni-chandra ) Tāraṇa, Śrāvaṇa-paurṇima, Monday = 21st July, 1404 A.D.
cells.remarks: Two copper-plates with ring in the possession of Gōpālakṛīshṇa-bhaṭṭa. Records that Raṅga-bhūpāla (I) installed his son Narasimha on the throne and with his queen Timmāmbā retired to the forest. Narasimha visited Bēlūru and celebrated there the ulābhāra , on which occasion he set up Sōmēśvara-liṅga and (?) the Channakēśava at of Veṅkaṭāpura and granted the village the Sōmaseṭṭipalli to a Brāhmaṇa named Śrikaṇṭha-vājapēy. Āpastambha-śākhā and Lōhita-gōtra, grandson of Kēśava-bhaṭṭa and son of Śīva yajvas The king is said to be the son of Śriraṅga and grandson of Tirumalarāya. The given date too early. No king of this name is known to be ruling by then. If the given Śaka years is to be equated with 1527, taking agni to stand for the numeral 5, the cyclic year would be Viśvāvasu. Tāraṇa would be Śaka 1506 when the details correspond to 10th August, 1584 A.D. The record is most likely a spurious one. We do not know of any son of Śriraṅga I, by the name Narasimha. In fact, the available evidence indicates that Śriraṅga had no issue. at all.

cells.date: Šaka 1461. Viļambi, Phālguņa šu. 14=1539 A.D., January 3, Friday, The Šaka year was current.
cells.object: On a stone south of the main entrance in the  prākāra  of the Mārkanđēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of two villages, Huṇasevalli in Bidireya-sthaḥa and Kategāra in Hērambi-sthaḥa yielding 280 and 450 khaṇḍugas of rice respectively to gods Janārdana and Mārkaṇdē-śvara of Khāṇḍeya in Eḍavale-nāḍu, belonging to Vasudhāre-sime, assigned to Raghupati rāja-voḍeya, son of Mallarāja-voḍeya, as an amara-māgaṇi . cells.date: Śaka 1313, Śrīmukha, Chaitra śu. 5. The  tithi  fell on 18th March, 1393 A. D., the Śaka year being 1315.
cells.remarks: Copy of an epigraph in the agrahāra . Records the grant of the village Kūduva!!i, in Vasudhāre-sime, converted into an agrahāra named Purushōttamapura, made by Śrī Rāmachandra-bhāratisvāmi, the pontiff of the Śrīngēri-maṭha, to Nīli Nar asimha-bhaṭṭa and other learned men ( vidvan mahā-janas ) of various gōtras (mentioned). The gift village is said to have been originally gifted by the king to the donor's preceptor Purushōttama-bhārati, for the maṭha and to god Vidyāśańkara. Of the vrittis so gifted 3/4 each was for goddess Lakshmi and the Gāyatri-maṇṭapa respectively. One vritti was for god Sōmēśvara.

cells.date: Śaka 1472, Saumya, Śrāvaṇa śu. 1. The  tithi  occurred on Thursday, 25th July, 1549 A.D., the Śaka year being current.
cells.object: On a stone in the Rāmēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of income from taxes like hiṭtu and hugge collected from the township ( pura ) newly built by Hiriya Basavappa, agent of Rāmapayya, with several gauṭa-prabhus (named) of Yamasandi, Koraṭikeṛe etc. of Jēvaṇige-nāḍu and also of Kuṛuvaṅgi (named) for worship, offerings and conducting several festivals (in the temple of) Rāmēśvara-liṅga. The gift was made for the prosperity of the king and of Rāmarāja-vođeya. Malōja of Kuṛuvaṅgi is the sculptor. Kṛīshṇappa, son of Saṅkaradēva of Basavanahaļi wrote the record. The gift was made over as kālāṇji to Mallappa, son of Gaṅgādhara-vođeya of the sthāna . It refers to the car-festival as also karāđe, kausāle ( kaṇsāle ?) and kāle as some of the services to be rendered on the eve of Śīvarātri .

cells.date: Śaka 1537, Rākshasa=1615-16 A.D.
cells.object: On a stone in the Virūpāksha temple (west of the village).
cells.remarks: Damaged. The king bearing the titles mahāmaṇḍalēśvara, rājādhirāja-paramēśvara and virapratāpa , is said to have renovated the temple of god Virūpāksha (formerly) consecrated by Vira Ballāļarāya who had granted 11 villages (named) for the service of the god. It seems to record a grant of the village Beladāļahaļji by Munīśvaradēva of Mutti. But, the lower portion of the stone is said to be under the ground and hence details are lost.

cells.date: Šaka 1464, Šubhakřit, Vaisākha šu. 15, Monday. Irregular. The  tithi  occurred on Saturday, 29th April, 1542 A.D.
cells.object: On a stone near the  karugallu  to the east of the village.
cells.remarks: Records the remission of taxes for the villages Hiriuru, Muktihalli etc. of Āsamdi-nāđu in Ekkaťi-sīma belonging to Hoyisaṇa-nāđu, in the southern region, granted for his chieftaincy ( nāyakatana ) by the king to the donor Aubhaļarāja-mahā-arasu, son of Maļli Aubhaļarāja. The taxes included those on marriage, taļavā xike , setťi-haṇa , nōťa-vaṇa etc. to be paid by the 18 community ( jātis ) of the villages mentioned.

cells.date: Šaka 1452, Vikřitu, Āšhāđha ba. 3, Wednesday=1530 A.D., July 13.
cells.object: On a stone in front of the Prasanna Rāmēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Sirigiripura, a hamlet of Belagūru, for the services of god Siddharāmēšvara-liņga of Belagūru by Sańkarasayya, after making a representation to Simgaṇa-nāyaka of his community ( jāti ) who had received Būdihāla-sīme from the king. The donor, a bāgila-pradhāna of Simgaṇa-nāyaka, is said to have himself received Belagūru in that sīme from the latter. It records the obeisance of Kōnamarasa, agent for the affairs of Samkarasayya.

cells.remarks: Registers a gift of 100 kam̂bas of wet land below the tank of Keřeyasante, a hamlet in Hāranahaļi-sime, to god Viṭhala by mahāmaṇḍalēšvara Sidedēva-mahā-arasa, son of Kalamili Bopparāja Gōparāja-mahā-arasa, for the merit of his parents Gōparāja and Aubhalamma, made over to Veṅkaṭādri, son of abhi šēkada Kāmarasa, of Kauśika-gōtra, the priest of the temple. Hāranahaļi-sime had been received by the donor from the king for his chieftaincy ( nāyakatana .) Bhadrayya, son of Virōja, the blacksmith ( kammāru ) wrote the epigraph.

cells.date: Śaka 1330, Sarvadhāri, Prāthama Vaiśākha ba. 15, Thursday, solar eclipse = 1408 A. D., April 26 ; Virōdhi, Kārttika su. 12, Sunday = 1409 A. D., October 20 ; Virōdhi, Mārgaśira śu. 7 = 1409 A. D., November 14.
cells.object: On a set of 5 copper-plates in the possession of Nārāyaṇa-joyisar.
cells.remarks: The king performed the Tulāpurusha and Brahmāṇḍa sacrifices on the first and second dates respectively and on that occasion made a grant of the villages Hiriya Bāsūru and Chikka-Bāsūru on Sāvayana-hōbaļi within Āsandi(?) of Hoysaļa-nāđu after converting them into an agrahāra named Pratāpadēvarāyapura. Trivēdi Vāmana-bhaṭṭa, the officiating priest of the tulābhāra received 3 vṛittis in the village Pamgulampādi of Mandagiri-nāđu. Barring him, the others participating in both the sacrifices, viz., the brahmas , sadasyas , ṛitviks and kaļaśāchāryas , numbering 55, together received 57 vṛittis and 330 varaha-gadyāṇas . The record specifies the shares received as also the boundaries of the gift land. The gift is said to have come into effect from Kārttika śu. 12 of the year Virodhi for the mahājanas of tualābhāra and Kārttika śu. 12 of the same year for the mahājanas of the brahmāṇḍa-dāna . The last date noted above appears to be the one on which day the copper-plate grant was got written and presented although it is not clearly stated to be so. The names of the composer and engraver are lost.

cells.date: Śaka 1350, Plavañga, Chaitra śu. 1, Thursday =1427 A. D., February 29.
cells.object: Slab set up under the  gōñi  tree.
cells.remarks: It registers a sale of land in Aramvaļi in Sāntaļige-nāđu of Āraga-vēnthe for 85 varahas by the members of the nāđu(samasta-nāđavarunamed), to Hariyaka-nāyakiti of Hebbarađi when Sirigirinātha-vođeya was governing Āraga-rājya. Thereupon, on the same day she gifted that land to Amarēśvara-tīrtha-śripāda , of the (Munivūra)- maṭha for feeding an ascetic and 4 itinerant Brāhmaṇas daily and employing 2 cooks. Both the records registering the sale and grant were written by sēnabova Viṭhaṇna and is attested by several individuals, officers and (ascetics in the later part).

cells.date: Śāka 1371, Vibhava, Vaiśākha śu. 8 Guruvāra =1448 A. D., April 11. The Śaka year was current.
cells.object: On a stone in the Sampige-maśha.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of four villages for feeding 12 Brāhmaṇas in a feeding-house ( satra ) made over to Raghunandana-tīrtha-śripāda of the Mēlu-maṭha of Munivūru in Sāntaļige-nāđu of Āraga-vēnthe made by Kōṭiyappa-heggađe of Nāvalanda in Pađuv-gēri-nāđu when Sirigirinātha-vođeya described as Brahma-kshatriya was governing Āraga-rājya. The mahājanas of Hālumattūru, Munivūru and Chikka Hoļalūru as also the pontiffs of the five maṭhas of Munivūru figure as signatories to the record written by Dēvarasa. The gift villages, yielding, in all, 264 khaṇđugas of paddy, were all purchased by the donor from several individuals before they were together granted. The record specifies the expenses to be incurred upon rice, ghee, green-gram, oil, fire-wood etc. Of the 12 beneficiaries two were cooks, one a store-keeper and the fourth an ascetic who was to manage.

cells.date: Śaka 1325, Svabhānu, Kārttika ba. 14, Tuesday=1403 A. D., November 13.
cells.object: On a stone in the  chandraśālā  of Tripurāntaka temple.
cells.remarks: Registers a sale of 6 villages—Meṇasūru, Mađavađi, Kuđigađi, Huñiseyakere, Volagōđu and Kārabayalu—along with their five hamIets, namely Hātage. Ānegōđu, Hosakoppa, Maṭṭakōđu and Keřeyakoppa along with the temples ( guđi? ), wet lands, dry lands, etc. as also the holeyālū ( holeya ) labourers ?) to Virāṇṇa-vođeya who was governing Āraga-rājya. These villages were situated in Mađvađi-nāđu in Āraga-vēṇthe. The sale price of these was fixed at 500 hons at the rates then carrent. Virāṇṇa was authorised to collect income from taxes like hadike , daṇṇāyakara-svāmya , uđugo xe (presentations) etc. amounting to 150 hons . Virāṇṇa-vođeya, of Bhāradvāja-gōtra and Rīk-śākhā is eulogised as a Brahma-kshatriya , wors shipper of god Triyambaka, discipline of Kriyāśakti-guru and son of Virūpāṁbikā. Madhuvaṇṇa, the sēnabōva of Mānki-seṭṭi of Āraga-paṭṭaṇa wrote the record.

cells.date: Śaka 1325, Svabhānu, Mārgaśira ba 12. Bhaumavāra=1403 A.D., December 11, Monday.
cells.object: On the same stone (whereupon No. KN 458 is engraved).
cells.remarks: Records the sale of land that belonged to the share of Masiga-gauđa valued at 150 hons in Meṇasūru of Mađavađi-nāđu to Viṭṭhaṇṇa-vođeya, son of Bommaṇṇa-vođeya by all the nāđu of the three cities and the eighteen Kampaṇas of Āraga-rājya, after getting it released from the original cultivators. Thereafter Viṭhaṇṇa-vođeya formed it into an agrahāra named Bommaṇṇāpura and dividing it into 54 vrittis granted 50 to vrittis Brāhmaṇas (named) of several gōtras etc., and 4 vrittis to the temples. The record gives the genealogy of Viṭhaṇṇa of Bhāradvāja-anvaya, a grandson of Saṁkapa. This latter, as also his younger brother Rāyapa were ministers. The record is said to have been written by Viṭhaṇṇa who may be probably a different person.

cells.date: Śaka 1322 ( rasa-nētra-guṇa-indu ) Tāraṇa, Kārttika-pūrṇimā, Vidhuvāra, Krittikā-nakshatra. Irregular. The  tithi  occurred on 1404 A. D., October 18, Saturday, the constellation being Aśvini.
cells.object: On a set of three copper-plates in the possession of Bishṭa-bhaṭṭa:
cells.remarks: Records a royal grant of the village Hālumuttūru alias Śakaripura in Bellāra-sthaṭa belonging to Kārakaṭa-sīme of Āraga-rājya dividing it into 52 vrittis , to a number of Brāhmaṇas after setting apart 4 vrittis for the worship of the village deity ( grāma dēvata ). It gives a genealogical account of the king who is said to be the son of Harihara and Pampā, grandson of Bukka and Gaurāmbikā and the third great-grandson of Samgama. The record contains the sign-manual śrī Virūpāksha , The language of the record is very faulty.

cells.date: Śaka 1315, Āmgirasa, Chaitra śu, 10, Bhānuvāra,  The Śaka year corresponds to the cyclic year Śrimukha when the given details may be equated with 1393 A.D., March 23, Sunday, In the year Āmgirasa (Śaka 1314) the  tithi  occurred on Wednesday, 1392 A.D., April 3.
cells.object: On a stone in the  maṭha .

Sābaṇṇa figures as the signatory. The record states that king Harihara bestowed his own name Pratāpa Hariharapura Mādhava to the pontiff.

cells.date: Śaka 1340, Hēmalaṇbi. Māgha śu. 7, Saturday = 1418 A.D., January 14, Friday.  The Śaka year was current;
cells.object: Stone leaning against the north wall of Mādhavēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: The record commences with a reference to the original grant made by Mallanṇa, son of Nāgaṇṇa (and grandson of) Peddaṇṇa of Kāśyapa-gotra to Nāgaṇṇa, son of Nāgappa of Viśvāmitra-gōtra, of land yielding a revenue of 4 haṇas in the haravari (?) of Dēviyakka, in Kuppava!li which had been granted to the donor by king Harihararāya through a copper-plate. This Kuppava!li which had been named Pratápa Hariharapura, an agrahāra , was now granted to Viṭhaṇṇa-vođeya (son of) Rāyappa-vođeya, who had been bestowed the administration of Āraga-rājya by the king vīrapratāpa Dēvarāya-mahārāya. The present donor now made a distribution of lands among the tenants of his own bḥaṇḍā-ra-sthaḥa and the tenants of the agrahāra in such a way that there would be no quarrel among them. Sāvaṇṇa-vođeya who was then administering Āraga-rājya, sent for Arasaṇṇa-heggađe (?) of Neluvāgilu, the mēlubhāgi (?) of Sātalige-nāđu. The record gives details of distribution.

cells.date: Śaka 1495, Śrīmukha, Nija Āshāḍha śu. 10, Sunday. The  tithi  occurred on 1573 A.D., July 9, Thursday.
cells.object: Stone set up to the north wall of the sanctum of Narasimha shrine in the  maṭha .
cells.remarks: States that Narasimhabhārati-svāmi, described as shaṭdar śana-sthāpanāchārya was the pontiff of Simgēri and Bhayirarasa-vođeya was governing at Kārakaḥa when Śamkhara-sarasvati, disciple of Mādhava-sarasvati-vođeya of (the maṭha of) Hariharapura made a grant of land in Kuppava!i, in Kātabayalu-Kuppava!i-nāđu, for the worship of and offerings to god Narasimha as also burning a perpetual lamp and maintaining a feeding house ( satra ) at Hari-harapura. The gift land was purchased from Mādhava-sarasvati-vođeya for 78 hons . The mahājanas of that place, the chief of Kārakaļa, Timmaya-sēnabōva of Bełtore and the nāda-var of Kārabayalu-Kuppavaļi are cited as witnesses.

cells.date: Šaka 1308, Kshaya, Āśvija śu. 10, Thursday=1386 A.D., October 3, Wednesday
cells.object: Stone set up in a field.
cells.remarks: Registers the renewal of a grant of the village Siđiyamani to Vidyāśaṅkaradēva-vođeya, grandson of Aṇṇaiyyadēva-vođeya. The latter person had been the original recipient of the grant made by Hoysala Ballāla, earlier in Šaka 1235, Ānanda, Kārttika śu. 10, Wednesday; the details of this date corresponding to 1314 A.D., October 19, Saturday. The gift village, situated in Keļabhāgi of Sāntaļige-nādu, is said to have been yielding 4 hons . Aṇṇaiyya was the son of Jagadānanda Pempa.

cells.date: Šaka 1202, Virōdbikřit, Kārttika śu. 1, Guruvāra. Irregular. The given cyclic year corresponds with Šaka 1233 when the  tithi  occurred on 1311 A.D., October 13, Wednesday. But the Vijayanagara kingdom had not come into existence as yet. If the Šaka year were 1293, the other details can be equated with 1371 A.D., October 9, Thursday, f. d. t.·39 when Bukka I was ruling.
cells.object: On a (second) stone at the base of the  garuđa kambha  in the Rāmēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: Badly damaged. Records that Jakkaṇṇa, younger brother of Hiriyaṇna made a grant of the paddy fields of Haļļi Hirivūru for god Rāmanātha, to provide for worship and offerings and maintenance of dancing girls and the Brāhmaṇas of Dēvivṛinda. Tippaṇṇa-vođeya confirmed the grant to the gauđas and temple priests. Refers to Teppada Nāgaṇṇa-vođeya, son of Ísvaradēva and Virāmbike, who was probably the mahāpradhāna at whose instance the grant was made. It also records a monetary grant of 169 ga and 4 haṇas . Details are all lost.

cells.date: Šaka 1431, Vaišākha šu. 1, Sunday=1509 A. D., April 20, Friday.
cells.object: Stone set up in a land called  gurulakke gadde .
cells.remarks: Registers a sale of land called gurullike-bedeya-makki , referred to as a grāma by Mallu-heggađe, younger brother of Tammana-heggađe of Kandalabaļi of Hōri-nāđu in Yēļuma-la-nāđu of Kaļasa, to Timmarasa, son of Rāmachandradēva of Kāšyapa-gōtra and Ēik-šākhā described as the aļiya (nephew or son-in-law ?) of Sūrappa-sēnabōva. The amount of 2 gadyā ṇas payable towards siddhāya was paid to god Kaļasanātha for sōniyadharma by Bhay rarasa-vođeya at the instance of the heggađe of Hōri-nāđu. Further, a sum of 5 haṇas had to be paid for this village for osage when the turn for collecting one haṇa for each salage in Hōrināđa-sime was to come. Sēnabōva Hamparasa wrote this 'record. Witnesses are cited. Bhai-rarasa-ođeya mentioned here may be the chief of Kaļasa Kārkaļa.

cells.object: On two sides of (the second) stone, to the north, in the Kaļasēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: Not given. Damaged, Records a grant of 20 ga for worship and offerings and maintaining pātra-bhōga and Pañcha-vādya (i.e. services of dancers and musical instruments) by a mahā-pradhāna whose name is lost. The king (?) bears the titles like Satya Hari-śhandra , dhanurdhara-madhyama-Pāṇḍavarāya , Bayakāra-Pitāmaha Maṅgarājātmaja etc. The record engraved on the backside of the stone is, in all probability, in continuation of the one on the front (noticed by Rice as Mg.58). This records the gift of an income of 170 varahas for services in the temple of Kaļasanātha made by the same māh-prādhana (? name lost) under the rule of Āragada Hariyappa-vođeya, son of Maṅga īāja which was another name for Mārappa, brother of Harihara I. It gives the details of the expenditure incurred for temple services.

cells.date: 1) Śaka 1438, Dhātu, Śrāvaṇa, śu. 15, Sunday, lunar eclipse = 1516 A.D., July 13. The month was Adhika Śrāvaṇa.
cells.object: On both faces of the 4th stone (to the south) in the same temple.
cells.remarks: 2) Iśvara, Jyēshṭha śu. 3, Mandavāra = 1217 A.D., May 23, Saturday When Immađi Bhairarasa-vođeya, son of Bommaladēvi and nephew ( aļiya ) of Hiriya Bhairarasa-vođeya was governing Kaļasa-Kārkaļa-rājya, Bhujabala-mahāráya of Vijayanagara attacked the Tuļu-rājya and camped at Maṅgalūru. The governor having vowed to god Kaļasanātha that he would renovate the temple if the enemy retreated, that army having retreated and he having returned to his country, got the temple renovated through Sūrappa-sēnabōva, described as budadhivant of his chāvađi (court) and arranged for the performance of worship in the mouth of Sōṇa (Śrāvaṇa. the rainy season) by granting 30 gadyāṇas . Details of the grant are given. The inscription engraved on the second face appears to be a continuation and registers a grant of sugar, jaggery etc. for feeding Brāhmaṇas. The record refers to the gift of a village to god Kaļasanātha in the presence of god Chandranātha of the basti at Kaļasa.

cells.date: Šaka 1446, Tāraṇa, Bhādrapada śu. 5, Thursday =1524 A. D., August 4, the month being intercalary.
cells.object: On the 5th stone in the same place.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of 10 honnus , made by Saṅkappa-sēnabōva of Mēgunda ( Mēgundada moda-la-bayilu ) for the daily offerings of god Kaļasanātha, in the presence of the three prabhus of the Thousand villages. The grant was made when Immađi Bhayirarasa-vođeya was governing the kingdom below and above the ghats and his širapradhāna Sūrapa-sēnabōva was holding the pārupatya of Kaļasa. Ummakka, wife of Kaļasappa of Yeđadahālu, took that money in the presence of Sūrappa-sēnabōva for the marriage of her grandson and in lieu thereof gave certain lands. Purushōttamabhāratī-vođeya of Mēlu-maṭha, Dēvarasa-hebārva of Māvinakēri and several other hebārvas are cited as witnesses. Bhānappa-sēnabōva wrote the record.

The grant was made by agreement among the three hebārs of the Kalasa Thousand villages and seven-teen persons (specified) outside the village, and all the elders ( mūligas ) of Nūju. Several hebāruvas are named as witnesses. Sēnabōva Hamparasa wrote the record.

cells.date: Šaka 1290, Kilaka, Māgha šu 10, Budhavāra = 1369 A.D., January 18, Wednesday, f.d.t. .38
cells.object: On a stone south of the enclosure of the Virabhadra temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of 6 gas for a perpetual lamp at the rate of 5 paņas every month probably collected for the maintenance of the tank at Bāleyaha!li in Hońga-nāđu by Bollarasa, son of Mādarsa-vođeya. The latter was ruling Āraga, Sayiđuguťa, Kole-nāđu and other rājyas . The grant was made for the rule to be bestowed upon Virupañna-vođeya, the prince. The epigraph noticed in MAR , is engraved on the same stone to the right. It contains a Sanskrit verse recording the blessings of god Virabhadra on Bollu-bhūpa, obviously the same as Bollarasa.

cells.date: Śaka 1290, Kilaka, Phālguña ba. 10 Sunday =1369 A.D., March 4
cells.object: In the same enclosure near the Viraśaiva-maťha.
cells.remarks: Slightly damaged. Records the gift of some land (details are lost) in Bāleha!li of Sātaļige-nāđu by Mādarasa-vođeya, the mahāpradhāni of kumāra Virupañnođeya, ruling Āraga, for the services of gođ Virēšvara of Bāleha!i. Also seems to refer to the maintenance of a feeding house for Brāhmañas. Mādarasa-ođeya is identified with Mādhava-mantri who ruled the kingdom of Chandra-gutti, Āraga and Końkaña under Harihara II, Bukka I and later Harihara II also. He is said to have been a Śaiva Brāhmaña of the Kálāmukha sect and a disciple of Kṛiyāśakti.

cells.date: Nandana, Māgha gu. 5, Thursday. Probably =1353 A.D., January 10, Thursday f.d.t. .04.
cells.object: On another stone in the same place.
cells.remarks: When Hariyappa-vođeya of Āraga, son of Vira Mārappa-vođeya, described as Hindurāya-suratāla , as also Bommarasa the house-hold officer ( maneya-adhikāri ) of pradhāna Malappa-vođeya were governing, Bommarasa having found the adgubnūhmi-nāđu of Holega mixed np in the tenancy of Bāleyaha!li, resumed that land and granted it to god Virēšvara. Hariyappa vođeya may probably be identified with Harihara II while Mārappa-vođeya was the younger brother of Bukka I.

cells.date: Śaka 1329, Sarvajit, Mārgaśira su. 15, Monday, lunar eclipse = 1407  A ,  D , November 15, Tuesday.
cells.remarks: Copy of the inscription in the possession of Dēvaru-bhaṭta. Records the grant of 5 villages-Sivakaraḍḍi, Karekoppa, Śiramgūru, Śiramgūru, Kadalemmane-attached to (?) Bhānupura-agrahāra, in Sāntaĵige-nāḍu, to god Vidyāśaṁkaradēva. The grant was made by Viṭṭhaṇṇa-voḍeya, of Āraga-eighteen kaṁpaṇas , who was ruling Āraga, Gutti, Bārakūru and Maṅgalūru stretching upto the western sea in Karnāṭaka-rājya by the orders of Bhāskararāya, son of the king in order that he may obtain four-fold merit ( chaturvidha-purushārtha ). On the date of the record Dēvarāya I was the ruling king. There might be some mistake in the copy of the inscription.

cells.date: Śaka 1474, Paridhāvi, Phālguṇa su. 10, Thursday, Punarvasu=1553 A.D., February 23
cells.object: Stone set up on the tank bund,
cells.remarks: It registers the consecration of god Virūpāksha-līṅga and the establishment of a feeding house for feeding five Brāhmaṇas daily therein, by Liṅgaṇa-nāyaka, son of Chennarāya-voḍeya and grandson of Virūpāksharasa, at Dānivāsa-paṭṭaṇa in Dānivāsa-sime, which had been granted to the donor for his hereditary chieftaincy by Hoysaĵa Ballāĵarāya of Haĵēbiḍu. The latter portion which is damaged registers a gift made for the worship, offerings and perpetual lamp for that deity. It also refers to the consecration of god Basavēśvara and a gift of land for worship and offerings of that deity. 36.

cells.date: Śaka 1332 (expressed by the chronogram  yugma-agni-guṇa-bhūmi ), Vikriti, Kārttika śu. 12= 1410 A.D., November 8, Saturday.
cells.object: On a set of copper-plates in the possession of Subbā-bhaṭṭa.
cells.remarks: The king, described as the son of Harihara and Mēlāmbikā, made a grant of the village Vōṭegāru, renamed Dēvarāyapura, in Hebāru-sīme within Āraṅga-vēṇṭhe, to Māyaṇāchārya, son of Dēvarāchārya belonging to Śrivatsa-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra and Bahvṛicha-śākhā, free from all imposts and for hereditary enjoyment as an agrahāra . cells.date: Śaka 1240, Vibhava, Pushya, ba. 5, Makara-saṅkrānti, Sunday. Irregular. The  tithi  occurred on Thursday, 22nd December, 1328 A.D., in the cyclic year cited, the Śaka year being 1250. The  saṅkrānti  occurred on Monday, the 26th.
cells.remarks: Vengere copper-plate inscription in the Śṛingēri-maṭha Vijaya Veñkaṭapatīrāya, described as the terrifier of the minds of Narapati. Aśvapati and Gajapati, son of Virūpāksharāya and grandson of Narasimharāyaraiyya granted a gift of the village Vemgare, to the holy maṭha of Narasimha-bhārati, disciple of Rāmachandra-bhārati and disciple's disciple ( praśishya ) of Gövinda-bhārati, at Śṛimgēri for the services of waving of lamp ( dipārādhana ) to the goddess Śāradāmbā. The gift village is said to be situated in Paramati-sthaṭa to the western gate of the Ūṭatūru-simhāsana. It also registers a grant of Gonegere village inclusive of its tanks and hamlets, situated to the east of Karutana-pālya, east of Pānđya-maṅgala, south of Sirukkenattu-pālya and north of (river) Kāvēri. The record is obviously surpious. The given date is too early and in the cited year Vijaya-nagara had not even come into existence. The genealogy of the king as also of the pontificate is faulty. No disciple of Gōvinda named Rāmachandra is met with among the lineage of gurus of Śrīmṅgēri, nor a king of that lineage in the Āraviđu dynasty.

cells.date: Śaka 1268 (current), Pārthiva, Phālguna ba. 1, Thursday=1346 A.D., March 9
cells.reference: EC., VI, Sg. 1; ARIE., 1953-54, No 41;  ibid. , 1961-62, No. 499;  Selections from the Records of the Sringeri Mutt (SRSM) , No. 1
cells.object: Slab near the western side of the Āūjanēya temple in the Maṭha.
cells.remarks: Commences with an obeisance to Vidyātirtha, the precptor. Records the gift of nine villages Heddase, Homnahole, Babbi, Haravari, Bellūru, Ambalūru, Bełamđūru, Hałaka, Kaimaleya Hosūru along with the hamlets, forming the Kela-nāđu within Mēlubhāgi-1000 of Sāntaļi-ge-nāđu, to Bhāratītirtha-śrīpāda, the pontiff of Śrīnṅgēri-tirtha and his disciples, and also 40 Brāhmaṇas serving them ( parichāraka ) so that they could be performing daily worship etc. Out of the income, 5 hons were deducted towards taxes etc. like umbaļi , dēvāsa , khamđike , damđige , and uđugože and 100 ga for payment to the original tenants. The gift was made, by the king and his brothers Kampaṇṇođeya, Bukkaṇṇođeya, Mārapođeya, Muddapođeya, son-in-law Ballappa-daṇṇayaka, kumāra Sōvaṇṇođeya and others on the occasion of celebrating the victory of the king. A supplement adds that Vira Kikkāyi-tāyi (of the Ālupa family) made a gift of Kaimaleya Hosavūru in Kela-nāđu to the same pontiffe Liṅgōja, son of Chinna Mallōja engraved the record.

cells.date: Šaka 1302, Raudri, Mārgaśira, śu. 1 Monday. In the cyclic year cited there was an inter-calary month of Kārttika, but Mārgaśira had lapsed. The  tithi  may be equated with 1380. A.D., October 19, in Nija Kārttika.
cells.remarks: Copy of a copper-plate grant found in a kađita in the Maṭha. When Hiriya Hariyappa-ođeya (Harihara I) was ruling in Hoysaṇa-dēśa, his younger brother Mārappa-vođeya and the son-in-law Ballappa-daṇṇāyaka granted the village Kesa-nāđu after dividing the lands of original value of 150 gadyāṇas in Keļa-nāđu situated in the upper regions ( mēlubhāgi ) of Sātaļige-nāđu, for the maintenance of the ascetics and disciplines, on the orders of Hariyappa-vođeya to śri Vidyātirtha-śripāda of Śrimgēri on the 1st lunar day of the dark half ( kṛishṇa-paksha ) of Phālguṇa in the year Pārthiva (1346 A. D., March 9). The total revenue value of the lands inclusive of baļi is 502 gadyāṇas and 5 paṇas . Afterwards, Bukkarāya granted Kelava!li-bhāgi in the upper regions of Sātaļige-nāđu and also the following out of the haravāris of Kikunda-nāđu viz. Ginikal, Bōlūru, Mūđanāđu, Ariśinava!li and the haravari named Nārave in Chikka Kođa nāđu. Altogether Bukkarāya granted lands (adding the income of Keļanāđu) at the time of the annual revenue value of 425 gadyāṇas and 5 paṇas to the maṭha (Śrimgēri) on, Tuesday, 1st lunarday of the bright half of Phālguṇa in the year Manmatha. Subsequently Bukkarāya again guaranteed lands altogether amounting to a revenue of 222 gadyāṇas and 4 paṇas , deducting the umbaļi . This was when śri Vidyāraṇya-śripāda, at the request of the king made through emissaries, returned to Śrimgēri from Vārāṇasi, after a short stay at Virūpāksha. The gift was made at the kings instance by Mādarasa, for the maintenance of ascetics The serving Brāhmaṇas, their families and others. Further, the king bestowed upon his son Chikka Bukkarāya granted, the administration over Āraga-rājya in Hulugāru order that his services may continue and also Kikunda-nāđu with 5 haravaris , in among the 30 haravaris , adding with this one haravari of Hariya Kođa-nāđu, altogether the total revenue being 424 gadyāṇas and 9 paṇas , It contains the sign-manuals of Śriṅgēśvara of Kigga, Kōṭēśvara of Kōṭapalli and also śri Virūpāksha . This seems to be partly identical with EC. , VI, Sg. 1 and MAR. , 1933 No. 2.

cells.date: Śaka 1306, Raktākshi, Mārgaśirsha śu  dvādaśi , Śukravāra =1384 A.D., November 25
cells.object: Copper-plate inscription in the Maṭha.
cells.remarks: The record begins with a description of the predecessors of the king, viz., Samgama and Bukka I without mentioning Harihara I. It then records a royal gift of the village Beługuła yieding 120 hons in Chikka Kođa-nāđu in Āraga-věnṭhe to Sūrappa and Kṛishṇadēva, disciples of Vidyāraṇya-śripāda, each getting a portion of 60 hons . Harihara II is described as having gained jñāna-sāmrājya , unattainable by other kings, by the favour of Vidyāraṇya. Sūrappa is said to be the son of Samādhiya Tippaṇṇa of Jāmadagnya Vatsa-gōtra while Kṛishṇadēva was the son of Pemmaṇṇa of Kauśika-gōtra. Both of them were disciples of Vidyāraṇya. The gift was exempt from taxes like suñka , kāruka , hodake , hombali , magame vaṭta and kaṭtige .

cells.date: Śaka 1309, Akshaya, Jyēshṭha ba. 13, Saturday=1386 A.D., May 26. The Śaka year was current.
cells.remarks: Second copper-plate inscription in the Maṭha. This charter records a royal grant to the mahājanas of the village Śringēri in the presence of god Virūpāksha of Pampā kshētra, in memory of Vidyāraṇya who had passed away ( paripūrṇarādalli ). He granted the lands of the annual income of 400 varaha-gadyāṇas situated in Kikkunda-nāđu of Āraga-věnṭhe and also land of the annual income of 100 varaha-gadyāṇas situated in the village Hagađūru in the upper part ( mēlu-bhāgi ) of Sātaļige-nāđu, dividing the same into 100 vrittis , constituting the lands into an agrahāra named Vidyāraṇyapura. Four vrittis were granted to the temple while the remaining 96 were distributed among 106 Brāhmaṇas named. While only one plate is noticed in MAR. , text from the 4 plates is given in SRSM . .41

cells.date: Śaka 1311, Vibhava, Māgha ba. 14, Sthiravāra. The  tithi  fell on Monday, January 25 of 1389 A.D., the Śaka year being current. In the next year (Śaka 1311, Śukla) the details cor respond with 1390 A.D., February 12, Saturday, f.d.t. .64
cells.object: Stone inscription.
cells.remarks: States that Chikka Harihara-mahārāya who went to Śriñgeri to pay respects to śri Bhārati-lirtha-śripāda, made a gift of 30 vrittis of land valued at 225 ga at the rate of 7.5 ga per vritti excluding those that had been earlier gifted, situated in Keļabhāgi of Kikkunda of Sāntaļige-nāđu. The gift was made to Brāhmaṇas in the presence of god Vidyāśamkara.

cells.date: Śaka 1316, Bhāva, Phālguṇa śu. 10, Thursday = 1st March, 1395 A.D., Monday and not Thursday.
cells.remarks: Copy of an inscription in the Maṭha (found in a kađita ). Registers the grant of some lands under the orders of the king to the Brāhmaṇas named Nārāyaṇa-vājapēyi, Narahari-sōmayāji and Pāṇđuraṅga-dikshita in the presence of Vidyāraṇya-śripāda. The granted land was of two haravaris , of the annual revenue of 478 kaṭi-gadyāṇas including the extra income ( mēlāya ) from forty nāđus . This grant was made to those Brāhmaṇas, for having brought out commentaries on the four Vēdas in the name of the king. The date is too late for this pontiff who is said to have passed away in 1386 A.D. CF. MAR. , 1933, p. 144.

cells.date: Śaka 1318 ( vasu-chandra-agni-vidhu ), Dhātu, Māgha śu. 7=1397 A.D., January 6
cells.remarks: MAR. 1933, No. 25 The third (Bhānuvalī) copper-plate inscription in the Maṭha. Commences with a eulogy of the king and his predecessors. Records a grant of the village Bhānuvalli renamed Hariharapura by the king in the presence of god Virūpāksha, to Mādhavēndra of Kausika-gōtra, Yajuś-śākhā and Āpasrambha-sūtra, son of kāraṇikya Mādhavēndra. The gift village was situated in the Āraga-rājya, Māle-nādu, Kārakala-sime. Beļāre division. The donee divided this village consisting of 20 vṛiṭtis to 25 and gave them to Brāhmaṇas (named) well-versed in the Vēdas. The language is very faulty.

cells.date: Śaka 1325, Chitrabhānu, Vaiśākha, ba. 1, Tuesday=18th April, 1402 A.D.
cells.object: On a palm-leaf book in the same Maṭha.
cells.remarks: Toravagāļuva, son-in-law of Nāgā-bhaṇdāri, purchased two plots of wet lands having the sowing capacity of two khaṇdugas , situated in Sindegēri and made a gift of the same to Vidyānātha-adhikāri, son of Kallidēva-adhikāri who was to make over annually 20 khaṇdugas of paddy to Vishṇu-bhaṭṭa or Śṛiṅgēri for the services of god Vighnēśvara. The said Vidyanātha-adhikāri is said to have let out the wet land for cultivation to one Kalānvita-yya on condition that he supplied the above paddy every year as rent and have a part of the lands converted into a garden. Dēvarappa, the sēnabōva , wrote the record while Honnale Jiṇo-heggađe, Būva-hggađe, Chinna-heggade of Annūr etc., figure as witnesses.

cells.date: Śaka 1355, Saumya, Kārttika śu. 1 = 1429 A. D., October 28, Friday. The Saka year was current.
cells.object: Stone inscription (copy).
cells.remarks: States that when Śaṅkarabhārati-vođeya ascended the pontificate after the demise of Purushottamabhārati-vođeya, the king invited him to Vijayanagara and worshipped his feet. On that occasion, he ordered through a rāyasa of his daṇāyaka-vođeya to form a village yielding 250 varahas in Bārakūru-rājya, to be gifted to the pontiff. Accordingly, Bhānappa, son of Channapparasa of Bārakūru made a gift of the village Koṅguva!li yielding 252 varahas annually for a perpetual lamp and offerings to god Vidyāśamkara and for the bhikshā of the ascetic.

cells.date: Śaka 1352, Saumya, Māgha ba. 14=21st February, 1430 A.D., Tuesday. The Śaka year was current.
cells.remarks: Copy of the Andava!li grant found in a kađita book. Hampeyarāya, son of Arasappa-vođeya, governing the Göve-Gutti kingdom, granted a gift to Viśvēsvārāraṇya-śripāda of Kallu-maṭha at Hampe for food-offerings and burning a perpetual lamp for god Vidyāśamkara and feeding ascetics in the maṭha of the village Andava!li in Chinamaha!iya-nāđu of Chandraguttiya-vēṇtheya, renamed Viśvēsvarāraṇya-pura, after due payment to the nāđu and making entries in the register of the karaṇika of Göve-Gutti and after satisfying nānā-mūlis . Details are given of the income of the village which amounted to 47 gadyāṇas and 6 haṇas .

cells.date: Śaka 1354, Paridhāvi, Āāđha śu. 12, Thursday = 1432 A. D., July 10, the month being Nija Āshāđha.
cells.remarks: A set of 3 (Mañjugaṇi) copper-plates in the Maṭha. Registers a royal grant of the village Mañjugaṇi in Kambannalige-dēśa of Saigaha!li-vēṇtheya in Honnāpura-rājya, with all its incomes and free from all imposts, after excluding former grants made to gods in Nādarineyyadi-dēvahađa (?), to Purushōttamāraṇya-yatindra, for food-offerings to god Rāmachandra. Varadapāchārya engraved the record which ends with the sign-manual śri Virāpāksha . Last four lines of the record are in Kannada.

cells.date: Śaka 1353, ( Lakshmilōka ) Virōdhikṛit, Māgha-amāvāsya, Dhanishṭhā-nakshatra, solar eclipse, Saturday=1432 A.D., February 2.
cells.remarks: The fifth (Kaigai) coper-plate inscription. Records the gift, as sarvamānya , of the village Keļagundaṇi in Gutti-12 of Gutti-vēņthe of Gōve-rājya and also the village Kaigai with its 5 hamlets (named) by the king to the pontiff Purushōttamāraṇya-yatīndra for food-offerings to god Rāmachandra, the worship of god Mahābala(of Gōkarṇa?) and maintenance of the maṭha and feeding of the Brāhmaṇa dependants. Varadapāchārya was the engraver. Nāraṇadēri motner of Dēvarāya II is said to be a devtoee of Vishṇu.

cells.date: Śaka 1369, Kshaya, Chaitra ba. 10, Sthiravāra=22nd March, 1446 A.D. Tuesday (not Saturday). The Śaka year was current.
cells.remarks: Copy of a grant found in a plam-leaf in the Maṭha. Mahāpradhāma Rāmachandradēva-vođeya. on the orders of the king, described as gajavēņte-kāra , granted the village Harihaļi situated in the māgaṇi of Sayavaninahaļļi for the service of god Mahābala in Gōkarṇa-kshētra. He appointed Bañki-sabbāyita as the manager of the satra-dharma for free feeding services. It also states that he handed over the management to the guru of the Śriṅgēri-maṭha when it was found difficult to carry on the duties without Bañki-sabbāyita.

cells.date: Śaka 1261, Pramādhi, Śrāvaṇa śu. 13, Sunday. The  tithi  occurred on Wednesday, 1339 A.D., July 21. But this date is too early for Mallikārjuna. cells.date: Śaka 1437, (1438, current), Yuva, Āśvija su. 1=1515 A.D., September 8. Saturday, f.d.t. .06 The Śaka year was 1437 itself.
cells.remarks: Inscription (copy). States that when Vidyāranya-vođeya, the pontiff of Śṛiṅgapuri came to Vijayanagara to give audience to the king and had camped in the maṭha at Hampc, under the orders of Ratnappođeya who was governing Bārakūru-rājya, his son Vijayappođeya made a grant of the village Huyyāru in Kela-nāđu and Honnagalli, a hamlet in Tombattina-sime (a sime of 90 ?) yielding respectively 362 and 150 kāṭi honnu to the pontiff, for god Vidyāśamkara and for offerings and burning a perpetual lamp (in the temple) of god Narasimha at Hālāđi. The gift was made for the merit and prosperity of the king. Mallarasa, probably the kara-ṇika , is mentioned probably as the writer of the record.

cells.remarks: Copy of an inscription in a kađita . Yuva, Mārgaśira ba. 30, Wednesday =5th December, 1515 A.D., the Śaka year being 1437. This is an order addressed to Triyambaka by the king, informing that the villages Baruve and Gavaṭūru in the Mālēnahalli-sime, and the village Maṇdali with its hamlets Harakere, Śivamogge and Sollebayalu in Gājanūru-sime, are granted to the gurus of Śřimgēri-maṭha since long and that no restriction should be imposed on them by him. This is according to the text given in SRSM . But, in MAR it is stated that the gauḍa-prajes of those gift-villages were directed to obey the pontiffs as their masters since they alone, right from the beginning, were entitled to those villages.

cells.date: Saka 1467, Viśvāvasu, Chaitra ba. 10, Monday =1545 A.D., April 6
cells.remarks: (Copy of) an inscription. Registers a gift of the village Bastihalli, in Gājanūru-sime, within Araga-sime, for the morning offerings to god Vidyāśamkara by daļavāyi Honnappa-nāyaka, agent for the affairs of Subali Immađi Parasunāyaka-vodeya. This latter was governing Āraga-sime which was bestowed upon him by the king ruling from Vidyānagari. The recipient was śri Rāmachandra bhārati-vodeya of Śřimgēri. The record ends with the sign-manual of Honnappa-nāyaka.

cells.date: Śaka 1582 ( dva-ashṭa-paṭcha-śaśi ), Śārvari, Pushya ba. 30, Sunday =1661 A.D., January 20
cells.remarks: Copy of an inscription found in a paper manuscript. Registers a royal gift of two villages, Raṇaghaṭṭa and Kalyāṇi Hārōnahalli with its hamlet Siṅgāpētha, near Vēlāpuri (Bēlūru) in Balaga-nāđu to Agnimūrdha Kṛishṇānandasvāmi, the pontiff of Muļuvāyipura-maṭha. The king is said to have been the son of Gōpālarāja and Vēṅgamāmbarā. The donee is described as the disciple of Śachchidānanda and Kshīrasvāmi. Pichchhala-yati and Śrīdhara-yati of the maṭha of Vishṇusvāmi in Muļuvāyipuri are named as the earlier pontiffs. In the latter part of the record it is stated that the king was the son of Raṅgarāja and Timmāmbarā, grandson of Srīraṅga and Raṅgamāmbarā and great-grandson of Veṅkaṭēśa belonging to Atri-gōtra and Āpastambarha-sūtra. The record ends with the sign-manual śri Rāma .

cells.date: Śaka 1582, Plava, Kārttika śu.15=1661 A.D., October 27, Sunday. The Śaka year was 1583
cells.remarks: The (Surapura) copper-plate inscription. The king, Vira Śriraṅgarāyadēva-mahārāya, son of Gōpālarājayya and grandson of Āraviṭi Rāmarāju Raṅgapparājayya of Atrēya-gōtra, Āpastambarha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākhā, made a gift of the village Jalagārāmani Surapuram, to the ascetic Kṛishṇānandasvāmi, disciple of Sachchidānanda, head of the maṭha at Muļuvāyi, for the worship of god Gōpālasvāmi. The gift is stated to have been made while the king was ruling from Vēlāpuri ( i.e. , Bēlūr) in the presence of god Chennakēśava as an act of devotion to god Veṅkaṭēśa. The record noticed in MAR. , 1935 is a copy of the grant written on a palm-leaf.

cells.date: Šaka 1577, Manmatha, Mārgaśira ba. 7, Chandravāra (Monday)=1655 A. D., December 9, Sunday
cells.object: On a set of three copper-plates in the possession of Šāma-jōyisa.
cells.remarks: This registers a renewal of an original grant made in Saka 1571, Virōdhi, Pushya śu. 7. Monday, Makara-saṅkrānti, (29th December, 1649 A.D., Saturday, śu.7, f.d.t. . 21) by Bālagiri-nāyaka, brother of Hire Hanumappa-nāyaka, son of Puvvali Keňgappa-nāyaka of Santhebennūru, to Kōnēri-bhaťta, son of Tirumała-bhaťta and grandson of Koṇdāvajjha of Yaraguła, of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and Řik-śākhā. It is said that this donee's family was erased out due to deaths and the grant was made again, obviously to the present donee—Jakka-bhaťta, son of Tirumala-bhaťta and grandson of Kōnēri-bhaťta and the record of the grant having worn out, a fresh copper-plate grant was now given. The dônor was Sarajyā Hanumappa-nāyaka, son of nichcha-madavaṇiga Hanumappa-nāyaka and grandson of Immađi Hanumappa-nāyaka. The grant was made in the presence of god Virabhadra of Kallatti while he was making several mahādānas before the temple of Basavēśvara. The gift included lands, houses etc. in the 10 sthaļas (Hire Kātūru, Hādikere, Kuṇtanamađuvu, Amřitāpura, Doranahāła, Tarikere, Chikka Kātūru and Dugganahāła—only these 8 are named) in Kātūru-sime.

cells.date: Śaka 1480, Kālayukti, Chaitra śu. 7=1558 A.D., March 26
cells.object: On the second stone to the right side of the temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of land below the tank at Kāmasamudra for offerings to god Virabhadra on the occasion of the lunar and solar eclipses. Both these eclipses did occur in the same month Chaitra śu. 15 and ba. 15 respectively—corresponding to April 2, Saturday and April 18, Monday of the same year. The donor was mahānāyakāchārya Tirumala-nāyaka, son of Koṇḍana-nāyaka of Kundūru who made the gift for the merit of K ṛishṇappa-nāyaka, son of Baipa-nāyaka. This looks like a gift made for a future occasion.

Both these eclipses did occur in the same month Chaitra śu. 15 and ba. 15 respectively—corresponding to April 2, Saturday and April 18, Monday of the same year. The donor was  mahānāyakāchārya  Tirumala-nāyaka, son of Koṇḍana-nāyaka of Kundūru who made the gift for the merit of K ṛishṇappa-nāyaka, son of Baipa-nāyaka. This looks like a gift made for a future occasion.

cells.date: Saka 1481, Siddhārthi, Nija Āśvija śu. 10=1559 A.D., October 10, Tuesday
cells.object: On a stone in the Birēdēvara-guda.
cells.remarks: EC. XI, C1. 54 Mahānāyakāchārya Hoṭteṇṇa-nāyaka, the chief of Harati, son of Chikapa-nāyaka granted the village Chitagoṇḍanaha!li, in Chaṭiyakambha of Mādhvasamudra-sthaḥa, in Doṭdērisime belonging to Kōṭekereya-vēṇthe of Rāyadurga-rājya, to Veṁkaṭādri, son of Liṅgappa of Kāśyapa-gōtra, Bōdhāyana-sūtra and Yajuś-śākhā, the sthānādhipati of god Virūpāksha of Hampe for the services of that god. The donor who belonged to the family of Abbeya-nāyaka Bomme-nāyaka of Kōṭekere and was the agent for the aflairs ( kāryakarta ) of mahā-maṇḍalēśvara Ramarāju Tirumalarājaidēva-mahā-arasa, is said to have received Doṭdērisime (?) as amara-māgaṇi from the latter. The gift was made on the day of lunar eclipse, in Adhika Āśvija month of that year corresponding to 16th September, 1559 A.D., Saturday Obviously the record was engraved later. The epithets borne by the donor, like kapaṭa illada bēḍa , Śivarātre sthira-saṁtōshi etc. are noteworthy,

cells.king: Bukkārāya (I) ruling from Hosapaṭṭaṇa in Hoysaṇa-dēśa
cells.date: Śaka 1277, Manmatha, Jyēshṭha śu. 7, Monday=1355 A.D., May 18, Monday f.d.t. .06
cells.object: On a stone at the entrance of the Sampige Siddhēśvara temple on the hill.
cells.remarks: Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Mallinātha-voḍeya, son of aṭiya Sāyi-nāyaka described as maṇḍaṭika khaṇḍeya-rṇya and the worshipper of the feet of Amaragundadēva, ruling at Bemmattana-kallu raised an upper storey of stone ( kalla upparige ) for god Siddhanātha of Bemmattama kallu, consecrated a pinnacle, and set up a stone swing. He renewed the gift of the village Chikkapura in Bemmattanakalla-nāḍu, formerly granted to that god making it free from taxes like hodake , hadike , koṭṭaṇa , suṁka-haṭṭi etc. Sōvaṇṇa, son of Hiriya Siddaṇṇa, a devotee (priest ?) of that god was the recipient of the gift. The record written by karaṇika Dēvappa and Rēvappa was engraved by Jaḍeya Rāmōja who also did the masonry work of the temple.

cells.object: On a stone in the Hiḥambeśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Vira Mallanṇoḥeya, son of Dēvarāya, described as the devotee of god Triyaṁbaka, made a grant of the village Kuṁchiganahaḥi alias Mallapura, one of the villages to the east of Bemmattanakallu, for the service of god Hiḥimbanātha, so that merit may accrue to his mother Mallāyavve. cells.king: Prauđhapratāpa Dēvarāya (II), son of Vijaya (Bukka III)
cells.date: Śaka 1353 (expressed in words), Saumya, Sahasya, Samkrānti. The corresponding Śaka year was 1351 = 1429-30 A.D. The details cannot be verified.
cells.object: Slab set up to the south of the Kallinātha temple.
cells.remarks: The record introduces Sāļuva Tipparāja, husband of Harimāūgā, the king's elder sister The latter's chief accountant ( karaṇādhpa ) Siṅghaṇa, great grand-son of Bhānu, grandson of Narasimha and son of Virūpāksha of Jāmadagnya-vatsya pravara and gōtra , had the temple of Kallinātha constructed at the village ( palli ) named Goṇđama in Bannūru and made a grant of 39 gadyāṇas and a further grant of land in Puṇđarkīapalli, to Nārāyaṇa for Rudrābhīshēka and offerings on Mondays to god Kallinātha.

cells.date: Šaka 1459, Viļambi, Kārttika šu.5, Thursday. Irregular. The details correspond to 1538 A.D., October 27, the weekday being Sunday and the Šaka year 1460.
cells.object: On a stone to the south of the Dyāmavva temple.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of the village Mallāpura, otherwise called Benakāpura, in Gunṭanūru-sime for the service of god Vināyaka consecrated by Konđarāya, the maternal uncle of hađapada Potti-nāyaka's son Viṭhappa-danāyaka at Gunṭanūru, for the merit of the latter who had received Bematūrakalu-sime, for his chieftaincy from the king. The gift included income from taxes like pasige on the weekly fair ( santhe ) at Gunṭanūru. The record states that Vidyānagarī was established by king Harihararāya, in the name of Vidyāraṇya-śripāda and under the command of god Virūpāksha-linga of Pampā.

cells.date: Šaka 1514 (Kali year 4742) Nandana, Māgha šu. 5, Sunday =1593 A.D., January 27, Saturday. The Kali year was 4693. On this date, however, Veňkaṭapati I was ruling. The Šaka year may be a mistake for 1574 when the Kali year would be 4753 and other details correspond to 1653 A. D., January 23, Sunday. In this year Šriraṅgarāya III was ruling.
cells.object: On a stone near the Āñjanēya temple.
cells.remarks: Mahānāyakāchārya Immađi Madakeri-nāyaka made a grant as a charity of affection ( manaḥ priti ), of Kađalegudu village belonging to Hiregunṭanūru-māgaṇi, in Chitrahaļi-sime as an agrahāra to an individual, name not clear (Rāma-vođeya ?) son of Puṭṭanṇa and grandson of Keñcha-vođeya, described as bhaṭara-bhaguta . The donor Immađi Medakeri-nāyakaraiyya, son of Kastūri Raṅgappa-nāyaka, grandson of Medakeri-nāyaka and great-grandson of Kāmagetti Vōbaṇṇa-nāyaka, was the agent for the affiars of the king. The donee may be Timmappa. The gift was made for the sole enjoyment ( ēka-bhōgya ) and was free from imposts like biṭṭi and Kōmaṭi-kāṇike .

cells.object: On a copper-plate in the possession of  ś yānubhōga  Rāmaṇṇa.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of the village Kađaleguda, with all its incomes, as an agrahāra , as a charity of affection ( manaḥ priti ) to Timmappa, son of Puṭṭaṇṇa, grandson of Keṭchaiyya and great-grandson of Baggūra-bhaṭṭa (who was himself the son of) Kshātra-bhaṭṭa, by mahā-nāyakāchārya Immađi Madakeri-nāyakaraiyya, son of Kastūi Rańgappa-nāyakaraiyya, grandson of Medakeri-nāyakaraiyya and great-grandson of Kāmagetti Vōbaṇṇa-nāyakarai, yya. cells.object: On a stone against the wall of the  gauḍa's  threshing floor.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Yibbeya-nāyaka, son of Buveya-nāyaka got excavated a tank, Būva-samudra, in memory of his father and endowed it with 150 varaha gadyāṇas and also conscerated god Buvēśvara in Halevāla for which lands and 5 gadyāṇas were granted. cells.date: Śaka 1301, ( śasi-kha-śikhi-chandra ) Siddhārthi, Karttika śu,  dvādaśi , (12) Bhāskaravāra (Sunda y)=1379 A.D., October 23.
cells.reference: EC., XI, No. Dg. 34;  HD. , No. 30
cells.object: On a stone to the east of the Hariharēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Mudda-daṇḍanāy aka, foremost of the ministers ( sachivāgraṇi ) of the king established the agrahāra Mudda-daṇḍanāyakapura, otherwise called Chikkahadaḍe in Koṭṭūru-janapada-belonging to Uchchaṅgi-durga and having divided it into 36 vṛittis made over 12 vṛittis to god Harihara and distributed the remaining 24 among as many number of Brāhmaṇas, whose names with gōtras and sūtras are recounted. Dharaṇōja wrote the record. An appendix added at the end states that the king himself made a grant of one vṛitti to Śridhara-bhatṭa of Rīk-śākhā and Vāśishṭha-gōtra, thus raising the number of vṛittis to 37. The record ends with the approval ( voppa ) of the king and the residents of the agrahāra . The sign-manual sri Virūpāksha is appended before the additional matter noted above is added Dharaṇōja wrote the record.

cells.date: Śaka 1332 ( nētra-agni-vahni-indu ) Vikṛiti, Bhādrapada (Nabha) śu. 12, Monday = 1410 A.D., August 11, the month being intercalary ( Adhika )
cells.object: On a stone to the south of the Hariharēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: This record is described vyavahāra-nirṇaya (a deed of settlement of transactions). The mahājanas of Harihara-kshētra, having at their own expense built a dam to the river Haridrā within the boundary of (the temple of) god Harihara and dug a canal through the god's land to Harihara, the king granted two parts of all the lands irrigated by the said canal for god Harihara and the third part was gifted to those mahājanas who got built the canal. The land for the mahājanas was divided in to 111 vṛittis and distributed among several Brāhmaṇas, named, belonging to several gōtras and sūtras . A copper-plate grant concerning this was given by the king. The present record is said to be a copy of the same. The Kannada portion of the record states that the canal passed through the villages of Bannikōđu, Beļuvāđi, Hanagavāđi, Harihara, Guttūru and Gaṅga narasiyakere the lands in which were distributed as shown above. It is stipulated that the donees and the temple were to bear the expenses for the maintenance of the canal and its repair in case of break down etc. in the same proportion. The later portion, in Sanskrit, records that Jagannātha, the minister( mantrt ), son of Maṅgarāja, with the permission of the king through his amātya Nāgapa, entrusted the work of the construction of the dam on the Haridrā to his son Bul!apa who carried it out to the satisfaction of the mahājanas . At the time of consecration, the mahājanas who were vṛitti -holders made a grant of 10 koļagas of land below the canal-5 from the share of the deity and 5 from those of the vritti -holders-to Bharatārādhya, son of Kṛishṇamallāchārya of Gautama-gōtra and ṛik-śākhā. Likewise, 8 kolagas of land, equally from the shares of the deity and the vritti -holder, was gifted to Bāyaṇāchārya, son of Maṭlikārjunāchārya of Chala-sampradāya belonging to Kāśyapa-gōtra and Yajuś-śākhā and 4 kolagas to Śānkara-bhaṭṭa who performed bodily circumambulation ( amga pradakshiṇa ).

cells.date: Śaka 1346, Krōdhi, Karttika śu. 12, Monday. The  tithi  fell on Friday (f.d.t. .01), November 3 of 1424 A.D.
cells.object: On another stone in the same place.
cells.remarks: The strong dam on the river Haridrā earlier built by Buṭlarāja, at the instance of the king and mahāpradhāna Nāgaṇa-daṇṇayaka having breached, this Buṭlarasa met Chāma-nṛi-pāla, the army commender ( samasta sainyādhipati ), son of Boppadēva and persuaded him to get it repaired. He having agreed to bear the cost of repair, the dam was reconstructed by Buṭlarasa. Chāmarāja is eulogised as gaṇḍara-gūṭi and Abhinava Bhōja while Buṭlarasa, son of Jagannātha and Chennāmbikā, is said to have belonged to the Kamme family and Gautama-gōtra. Dharaṇōja, son of Māchidēva, engraved this.

cells.date: Śaka 1453, Khara, Āsvīja śu. 10, Saumyavāra=1531 A.D., September 20, Wednesday f.d.t. .09
cells.object: On a 4th stone in the same place.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of two villages Belūvaḍi and Gaṅganarasi situated in Harihara sime of Uchchaṅg i-vēṇthe, in Pāṇdya-nāḍu for offerings to god Harihara, on tenure ( vartane by Avasarada dikshita, son of Aṇṇājidēva of Gārgya-götra, Āpstaambha-sūtra), and Yajuś śākhā, in order that merit may accrue to Avasarada Dēmarasa. It also records a grant of 5 kuļas of lanes to Tāya Simmaṇṇa's son Savita-bhaṭṭa by the same person. One kuļa ofland in Belūvaḍi village was also granted to Kariya Tippōja, son of goldsmith kasāle ViraVirōja, who wrote ( tiddida ) this incription. Harihara-sime had been bestowed upon the donor for chieftaincy by the king.

cells.date: Śaka 1514, Nandana, Adhika Āshāḍha šu. 1=1592 A.D, May 31, Wednesday.
cells.object: On a stone set up in the shrine of Basavaṇṇa.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Hemmađihāla, in Harati-sthala, belonging to Rāyadurgavēnthe, which belonged to the chieftaincy of the donor Chikka Raņgappa-nāyaka, of Harati for offerings in the maṭha of Hoṭṭe Iśvaraiah. The record recounts the genealogies of both the donor and his pontiff. The latter is associated with epithets Dūshakaragamḍa and Mānava Mahādēva . His lineage : Iśvaraiah of Śāravāḍa → Chenna Dūlēśvara → Hoṭṭēśvara → Basavēśvara → Kemchēśvara → Immađi Basavaṇṇoḍeya → Kemcha Ālaṇṇoḍeya-Isarappa-voḍeya → Hoṭṭe Iśvaraiah. The genealogy of the chiefs of Harati, described as Mahā-nāyakāchārya of Kōṭeyakere : Kāmi-nāyaka → Abbi-nāyaka → Kāmi-nāyaka → Gaḍḍada Brahma-nāyaka → Hoṭṭeṇṇa-nāyaka → Immađi Bīraṇṇa-nāyaka → Iśvaradēvi-nāyaka → Basavināyaka → Mummađi Brahma-nāyaka → Iśvara Dūlappa-nāyaka of Harati → Duṇdappa-nāyaka → Lakshmīpati-nāyaka → Chikka Raņgappa-nāyaka.

cells.date: Šaka 1467, Svabhānu, Mārgaśira ba. 5. In the cyclic year cited corresponding to Šaka 1445, the  tithi  fell on Friday, November 27, 1523 A.D.
cells.object: On the front and left sides of a stone in Narasiraṅga's land below the tank.
cells.remarks: Kāmagetti Timmaṇṇa-nāyaka, son of Hanumi-nāyaka, made a grant of the village Arekere in the Nandana sōma-sthala in the Kuntaṇa-dēśa, which the king had favoured for his chief-taincy, to Vēdamārgapratisthāpanāchārya Mālyavanta Rāmānuja-jiya, in order that merit may accrue to his father, as also Rāmarāju Tirumalarājaya. The gift was made in the presence of god Mālyavanta Raghunātha of Hampe on the utthāna-dvādaśi day occurring in the month of Kārttika. Hr. 75, badly damaged, gives the details of date while Hr. 76, which is better preserved, does not give the date details; but other details of grant etc. are known from this.

cells.date: a) Śaka 1332, Hēmalambi, Mārgaśira śu. 10, Thursday = 1417 A.D., May 18, Thursday, f.d.t. .29; b) Plavamga, Māgha ba 14, Friday, = 1428 A.D., February 13, f.d.t.·46; c) Phālguṇa, śu., Thursday = 1428 A.D., February 19; d) Phālguṇa śu. 15, Monday = 1428 A.D., March 1
cells.object: On a stone in front of the Sōmēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: When the king seized the great city Kāreya-paṭṭaṇa, Kāmāya, wife of Pāyaṇṇa and her sons Jakkadēva etc., altogether 5 persons, were protected by Kandikere Bayire-nāyaka, where-upon, by the order of the family god Sōmadēva of Saurāshṭra, Jakkadēva got excavated a tank on the Meddeṇahalla river to the south of Hiriyūru and consecrated god Sōmēśvara in order that merit may accrue to his parents and his protector Bayire-nāyaka. When his mother Kāmāyi fell ill on the second date and passed away on the third date, he made dēvādāya , brahmādāya grants, in the presence of god Sōmēdēva on the last date. Details of grant are lost. The record obviously came into existence after the last date.

cells.date: Śaka 1449, Kali year 4628, Sarvajit, Āshāḥha ba. 10, Sunday=1527 A.D., June 23, the month being Ādhika Āshāḥha. In Nija Āshāḥha the weekday would be Monday, July 22.
cells.object: Slab leaning against the wall of Āñjanēya temple.
cells.remarks: Rāmaṇṇa-nāyaka, agent of Chinnappa-nāyaka who was himself the agent of the king, gave a charter of guarantee ( nambuge-śāsana ) to the 18 gauḍa-prajes of Dummi that he would not break any of the pledges given by him at the time of bringing back culvators of Dummi who had emigrated from the place on account of the heavy dues exacted from them in connection with the breaches to the tank at the village and other impositions, by the previous pārupatyegāra . He swore by the feet of Chinnappa-nāyaka not to molest the villagers by exactions levied in the previous regimes, consisting of the above impositions. This amounts to a charter of good faith.

cells.date: Šaka 1409, Vibhava, Jyēshṭha šu. 1. These details, not verifiable, are  prima facie  irregular, The Šaka year equated with 1487-88 A.D., corresponds to the cyclic year Plavaṅga, while the cited year Vibhava corresponds with Šaka 1430, the details being equated with 1508 A.D., May 1, Monday. This is too early a date for Sadāśiva. If the Šaka year is a mistake for 1509 = 1587-88 A.D., it is too late a date, for, by then Veňkaťapatirāya I of the Āraviđu dynasty had commenced his rule.
cells.object: On the pillar in the verandah of the  raṅgamaṇṭapa  of Gōpālakrīshṇa temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged and worn out. Mahāmaṇđalēśvara Aļiya Rámarájayyadēva-mahā-arasu having died in the battle with the Muhammadans ( turukara-rājakārya ) and the kingdom havnig perished when Tirumalarājeyadēva-mahā-arasu bestowed Hoļalakere-sīme upon Kāmageti Medakeri-nāyaka, as amara-māgaṇi , the latter made it over to Gulliyapa-nāyaka, his brother-in-law ( mayduna ) as umbaļi . This chief renovated the temple of Madana Gōpālakrīshṇa at Hoļalakere. The later, worn out, portion seems to record some gifts.

cells.date: Šaka 1490, Vibhava, Jyēshṭha śu. 5, Tuesday=1568 A.D., May 31, Monday.
cells.remarks: Copy of a copper-plate record in the Gōpālakṛishṇa temple. Registers a renewal of grant of lands to Veñkaṭāchārya-dikshita of Ātrēyasa-gōtra, Bōdhā-yana-sūtra and āYajuś-śākhā, by Kāmagetti Kastūri Medukeri-nāyaka, through his brother-in-law Gulliyappa-nāyaka. The original grant had been discontinued when, after the Muhammadan invasion, Aliya Ramarājayya passed away and confusion set in. The donor had received the area as amara-māgaṇi .

The inscription was witten by Nāgaṇāchārī of Vidyānagari. The hebārṇvas , gau las sēnabōvas , seṭṭis , paṭṭaṇasvāmius , praje and several svāmis of the Ayyāvol-le-haya-nānādēsi . appear to have carried out the instructions on their part.

cells.date: Śaka 1476, Ānanda, Kārttika ba. 1=1554 A.D., November 10, Saturday.
cells.object: On a stone near the peepul tree in the tank bed.
cells.remarks: States that when Viraṇṇa-nāyaka, agent of Pōtappa-nāyaka's (son ?) Kṛishṇappa-nāyaka was holding the pārupatya of Bāgūru-sime, on the petition of Narasimhayya, the customs officer(?), after holding consultations with Liṅgaṇa-gauḍa, sēnabōva Timmappa and several other prajes (named) rebuilt Hoṛapēṭe which was in ruins, renamed it as Kṛishṇāpura and inviting tenants ( vokkalu ) to reside there made it free from all imposts for one year whereafter the amount of taxes were to be fixed through an agreement.

cells.date: Śaka 1477. Rākshasa, Pushya ba., Sunday, Makara-samkrānti = 1555 A.D., December 29, the  tithi  being ba. 2
cells.object: On a stone in the  prākāra  of Kēśava temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the grant of 3 villages Madure, Araļihaļļi, Hādarikaţte, formerly granted by Gōpaṇṇođeya for the services of god Chennigarāya of Bhāgyapura, by Koṇđarāja, agent of Krīshṇappa-nāyaka, son of haļapada Bomma-nāyaka, in order that merit may accrue to Krīshṇappa-nāyaka. Krīshṇappa-nāyaka and Appamma-nāyaka granted the villages Nāgēnahaļļi, Krīshṇapura. The latter portion records some grants made earlier in the year Šubhakrīt (1542-43 A.D.). It further refers to yet another grant of money for offering to the god. In this connection some dishes to be offeredtuppada laţhi (?) and bellada kajjhāya are mentioned. The slab contains another record dated Paridhāvi, Pushya šu. 12 = 1552 A.D., December 27, Tuesday, wherein it is stated that Erā Krīshṇappa-nāyaka made a gift of the village(name lost renamed Krīshṇa-samudra, for the merit of the king, to god Chennigarāya. It aslo registers the gift of a village as baļuvaļi to Tiruveṅgaļaiyya, Šaţhagōpayya and Lakshmaṇayya who were to be in the service of the deity at Bāgūru while another person was to remain in the gift village ?) as a tenant looking after the lands. If KN. 615 above.

cells.date: Śaka 1308 (elapsed), Kali year 4488, Prabhava, Chaitra šu. 1, Thursday = 1387 A.D., March 21. The Śaka year would be 1309.
cells.object: On a stone under the  garuđakambha  of Kēśava temple.
cells.remarks: Records that by the orders of Vallabharāya-mahārāja, son of mahāmaṇđalēśvara Vira Dēvarasa and Malidēvi, described as Chāļuki-nārāyaṇa and Chāļuki-chakravartti and as the maneya-manneya -of the king, his servant ( manushya ?) Peddarāja set up a lamp-pillar and made a grant of some wet lands and garden for offerings to god Kēśava for the merit of Viradēvarāja. cells.date: Šaka 1455, Vijaya, Kārttika šu. Utthāna-dvādāśi ≡ 1533 A.D., October 29, Wednesday
cells.object: On a set of 5 copper-plates in the possession of Rāmā-bhaṭta.
cells.remarks: EC. XI. Hk. 132 Recounts the genealog of the king and records the grant of the village Kēdaggere, a hamlet of Imāmbikā-samudra, in Nirugunda-sīma within Yakkaṭiya-vaļita in Hoysaṇa-rājya to a number of Brāhmaṇas well-versed in lore, having divided the villages into 34 vrittis . The grant was made on the banks of the TuŹgabhadrā in the persence of god Viṭhalēśvara Ē on the requisition of Tīmma-nāyaka and haḍapada Baiyapēndra . This inscription was composed by Sabhāpati and engraved by Viraṇāchārya, son of Mallaṇṇa.

cells.date: Šaka 1433, Prajāpati, Pushya-ardhōdaya, Sunday=1512 A.D., January 4. The  tithi  was ba. 81, the constellation being Pushya.
cells.object: On a set of 4 copper-plates in the possession of Nērlakere Narasamma.
cells.remarks: The king made a grant of the village Bōbūru, surnamed Krīshṇarāyapura in Maleyanūru-sthaļa of Hiriyūru-sīme, within Kuntaļa-dēśa, converting it into an agrahāra , to Timmā-bhaṭṭa, son of LiŹgā-bhaṭṭa of Šaunaka-anvaya, Āpastambha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākhā. The donee divided it into 32 shares and keeping 16 for himself, distributed (the remaining vrittis ) among the Brāhmaṇas (named). But the details of this are incomplete since the second face of the 3rd plate is left blank for unknown reasons. The inscription composed by Sabhāpati was engraved by Mallaṇa's son Viraṇāchārya, The donee. LiŹgā-bhaṭṭa is said to have belonged to the family of Kāka (Tāta ?)-bhaṭṭa of Vōrugallu.

cells.date: Šaka 1441, Vyaya, Chaitra šu. 15=1526 A.D., March 28
cells.object: On a stone in the verandah of the Āñjanēya temple.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of the village Nibugūru in the Jagaļūru-sīme, which the king had bestowed upon him for his chieftaincy, to provide a satra for feeding 35 Brāhmaṇas and 40 followers of the six darṣanas and the šūdras in order that merit may accrue to the king, by Raṇganātha-rāūta, son of Viśvanātha-rāūta of Kāśyapa-gōtra and Āśvalāyana-sūtra, belonging to Āreya-kshatriya community. The gift was made in the presence of god Kallinātha, on the bank of the Hanatoṛe, where there appears have once existed the residence ( āśrama ) of the sage Jamadagni.

cells.date: Šaka 960, Prabhava, Mārgaśira šu. 5. These are apparently wrong. The Šaka and cyclic years do not tally.
cells.remarks: MAR.. 1925, No. 22 Single copper-plate in the possession of taļavāra Durga, Contains a wrong genealogical account. Mentions Bukkarāja, Dēvarāja, Samgamarāja, Harihararāja, his younger brother Bukkarāja's son Harihara whose son was Vikramarāja, grandson Bukkarāja and great grandson Dēvarāja. It mentions the immigration of shepherds from different regions to this kingdom where they settled and built temples, dug tanks, enjoyed the office of redđi and so on. Clearly, this is a spurious record.

cells.date: Šaka . . . Pimgaļa, Šrāvaṇa ba. 8=1557 A.D., August 17, Tuesday. The Šaka year was 1479'
cells.object: On a stone east of the doorway of Gamgādharappa's house.
cells.remarks: Damaged. In the course of scrutinizing the accounts of the temple of Viṭṭhala, the king got a copy of an epigraph recording the grant of income from taxes— suṭmka, kaḍivāru, maka-ḍivāru (?) (taxes on) amgaḍi, magga, nāḍa-taļavārike, hoṭrabaļi hulubanni, uppinamōļe etc. as also taxes to be paid by the pimjaniga (?), washerman, on loads on bullocks to be paid by the baṇajiga (merchant) etc. of seven villages (named)—formerly made by Kṛīshṇadēvarāya in the year Pramādicha Šrāvaṇa śu. 1 (1519 A.D. July 27), for offerings to god Bairēdēva. Having found it inoperative, the king renewed the same by adding income from some other taxes. The gift was made for the merit of Aļīya Rāmarājayyadēva-mahā-arasu.

cells.date: Śaka 1309, Kshaya, Kārttika śu. 1=1386  A.D. , October 24, Wednesday, the Śaka year being current.
cells.object: On a copper-plate in the Jaṭimga Rāmeśvara temple on the hillock.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of the village Jiyarahaļi in Hāneya-nāđu of Rāyadurga yielding 400 pratāpa ga , which was being credited to the palace, to god Jatāngi Rāmayadēva for worship and offerings etc. by the king. cells.date: Śaka 1356, Ānanda, Āśvayuja ba. 10=1434 A. D., September 27, Monday, f.d.t. .04.
cells.object: On a second copper-plate in the same temple.
cells.remarks: When the king went to Māchēnahaļi for hunting and paid a visit to the temple of Jatāngi Rāmeyadēva, (the temple authorities) having petitioned to grant a village yielding 23 varahas for the temple, under royal orders, and also of Arasappa, land below Saṅgebōva's canal in Hāneda-nāđu, originally held on tenure ( koru ) by Viraṇṇa, was gifted. This gift had come into effect from the month of Āshāḥha śu. 1 of that year (June 8, Tuesday).

cells.date: Šaka 1478, Nala, Jyēshṭha šu. 15 = 1556 A.D., May 24, Sunday, lunar eclipse.
cells.object: On a stone in front of the Hanumanta temple.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of the village Karađipalle otherwise called Harihararāyapura in Rāya-durga-sime bestowed upon mahāmaṇđalēšvara Rāmarāju-Viṭhalarāju-Tirumalaiyyadēva-mahārāju. It refers to the representation made by the mahājanas about some illegal exactions made by maṇiha-gauṇđas whereupon the king exempted them from paying the same and arranged for repairs of temples, tanks etc. from out of such illegal taxes, more specially the fines collected obviously from the erring officers. Cf KN. 644 below.

cells.date: Śaka 1478, Nala, Jyēshṭha śu, 15 = 1556 A. D., May 24, Sunday, lunar eclipse.
cells.object: Stone lying behind the Basava temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. States that mahāmaṇdalēśvara Rāmarāju-Viṭhalarāju-Tirumalaiyadēva-mahārāya having granted to vidvan-mahājanas the village Muravađi, otherwise called Bukka-rāya pura as agrahara free from all imposts, now rearnt that they had illegally exacted some taxes. He now appears to have recovered them (and returned ?) and thereupon re-granted the village with strict instructions not to collect such. The details of the record are lost. The gift village is situated in Rāyadurga-sime which had been bestowed upon him for his chieftaincy, by the king.

cells.date: Śaka 1313, Pramōdūta, Vaiśākha śu. 3, Sunday = 1390 A.D., April 18.
cells.object: Stone near the Chandranātha basadi.
cells.remarks: Mentions Harihara and his general Guṇḍappa-daṇḍanāyaka. Records the renovation of the basadis at Mullūru by Bāhubalidēva, disciple of Vijayakirtidēva. Incidentally refers to the construction of the basadi by Rājādhirāja Koṅgālva, for the merit of his mother Pōchabba-rasi and grant of villages for its maintenance. Harihara appears to have renewed the grants and himself gifted the village Kāragōḍu renaming it Aṇṇaṅgāpura, to god Pārśvanātha through Guṇḍappa-daṇṇāyaka. Goṅkaraḍḍi-nāyaka was in charge of Mullūru-70. Arjuna is said to have written the inscription.

text.remarks: Mentions Harihara and his general Guṇḍappa-daṇḍanāyaka. Records the renovation of the  basadis  at Mullūru by Bāhubalidēva, disciple of Vijayakirtidēva. Incidentally refers to the construction of the  basadi  by Rājādhirāja Koṅgālva, for the merit of his mother Pōchabba-rasi and grant of villages for its maintenance. Harihara appears to have renewed the grants and himself gifted the village Kāragōḍu renaming it Aṇṇaṅgāpura, to god Pārśvanātha through Guṇḍappa-daṇṇāyaka. Goṅkaraḍḍi-nāyaka was in charge of Mullūru-70. Arjuna is said to have written the inscription.

cells.date: Šaka 1301, Siddhārthin, Jyēshṭha, Tuesday, lunar eclipse= 1379 A. D., May 31.
cells.object: Copper-plate set in the possession of the Secretary, Karnataka Historical Research Society Dharwar (formerly in the possession of Sri V.B. Alur, Editor,  Jayakarnāṭaka )
cells.remarks: Records the endowment of 22 villages in Gadaga-dēśa comprising 66 villages and situated in Lakuṇđiya-vēnthe of Toragallu-nāđu, a sub-division of Pampā Hastinavati, for the maintenance of worship in the two temples of Tryambakēśa and Viranārāyaṇa at Gadag, made by the king, in the presence of god Virūpāksha on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadrā, at the instance of his preceptor Vāṇivilāsa Kriyāśakti-guru and the appointment of Sammaṇāchārya, son of Sarvāchārya, a Brāhmaṇa of Kāśyapa-gōtra and Bōdhāyana-sūtra, a resident of Kratupura and sēnabōga of Gadaga-dēśa, to supervise the worship in the temples and manage their property.

cells.date: Śaka 1359, Vibhava, Śrāvaṇa śu. 5, Friday. The Śaka year is wrong for 1370.=1448 A.D., July 5, Friday, f.d.t.·46. The intended date of this record may be 1448 A.D. cells.remarks: Summaries., 1947-48, No. 3; KI , VI, No. 69 It records that Mahalappa-sēnabōva, son of Gōpaṇa-sēnabōva, purchased land from Mahābaladēvarasa, son of Saṅgirāyarasa and Bommidēvarasa, son of Mahābaladēvarasa of Vardhamāna-samtati of Kumbiṭe in Gōkarṇa-kshētra, for building a temple for god Raghunātha and a maṭha attached to it, on that land. It further records purchase of another piece of land in the village Miḍije, a māgaṇi , by the same person from Padumaladēvi-amma. This was made over as a gift for worship and offerings in the temples of Raghunāthadēva, Mahābaladēva and Vināyakadēva. Mahābaladēvi Padumaladēvi-amma was administering Nagire. Haive, Tuṛu, Koṅkaṇa and other rājyas .

cells.date: Šaka 1317, Yuva, Pushya śu.  ċkādaśi  (11), Thursday = 1395 A. D., December 23, Thursday.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1932-33, BK., No. 167; SII., XVIII., No. 274
cells.remarks: Three pieces of a slab in Bastimaṭti. Saṅgama, son of Mallappa, a Jaina devotee and son of Šaṅkhadēva and grandson of Muddapa-śrēshṭhi of Pulikara died by the rite of samādhi whereupon Nēmaṇṇa made a grant of land for offerings to god Pārśvanātha of Saṅgūru for the merit of his father and ancestors. Mallappa is said to be the sēnādhipati of Mādhava ruling Gōve when chakravarti Vira Harihara II, son of Bukkarāja was ruling and Maṅgappa-daṇđanātha was his minister. The village Cheṅgāpura (Saṅgūru) was granted by Mādhava to Mallappa who is said to have died by the rite of samādhi on Monday, ¡Phālguṇa ba, 14 of the year Naļa (1377 A.D., March 9) and was followed by his four wives. His father as well as his three sons died by the same rite.

cells.date: Śaka 1334, Nandana, Chaitra śu. 1, Monday = 1412 A.D., March 13, Saturday
cells.object: Slab in the temple of Virabhadra.
cells.remarks: Pradhāna-daṇḍanātha , Sāvaṇṇa-vođeya, son of Nāgaṇṇa-daṇṇāyaka-vođeya was administering Gōve-rājya. Registers a gift of land in Saṅgūru in Gutti-18 kampana , to Siṅge-nāyaka, Lakhe-nāyaka, Malle-nāyaka and Bhaira-nāyaka as blood-grant nettaru-gođage , by Nēmaṇṇa. Mādarasa, Hampanṇa, sons of Pāđimukhi Jaina Mallapa of Gōve, the grandsōn of Kāva-mūli Baicha-veggađe of Saṅgūru. It is stated that the donees stood by the donors, in the past, in their adversities. The donors were joined by several others, like paṭṭaṇasvāmi Malli-seṭṭi, Goṇasubāya (?) Dēvaṇṇa; sēnabōva Sōmappa. and other potters ( kumbaṇā ) silk weavers ( pāṭresāliga ) etc. named.

cells.date: Šaka 1501 (wrong for 1502), Vikrama, Māgha šu. 15, Friday, lunar eclipse=1581 A.D., January 19, Thursday.
cells.reference: ARIE., 1957-58, No. 304;  Summaries , 1949-50, No. 22;  KI. , V, No. 8; VI. No. 72;  QJMS. , LV, pp. 92-98
cells.object: Slab fixed into the  prākāra  wall of the Šāntēśa temple.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Maddugoņdakoppa alias Hanuma-samudra, for worship and offerings to god Hanumanta of (the temple at) Sātēnahaļli by Lakhe-nāyaka of Hāvasebhāvi, who was an agent of Samķhaṇa-nāyaka, son of Immađi Sadāśiva-nāyaka of Keļadi, who was governing from Ikkēri. The grant was made at the instance of the latter for his welfare as also that of Chinnappa-nāyaka, the father of the donor and also the mother. The gift village was situated to the south of Tiļuvaļli in Nāgarakhaņda-sime within Banavāsi 12000. Penugoņda, the capital, was situated in Hastināvatiya-vaļita. The Kelādinīpia Vijaya states that the title Immañi was conferred on Sadāśivēndra-nāyaka by Kṛishṇadēvarāya while the Śivatattvaratnākara states that Sadāśiva-nāyaka, who had obtained the title of Rāya-nāyaka from Rāmarāya, conferred his kingdom as well as the title Immañi Sadāśiva-nayaka on his own brother Bhadrappa.

cells.date: Śaka 1334, Nandana, Mārgaśira śu. 2, Sunday=1421 A.D., November 2.
cells.remarks: Three sides of a pillar in the Śaṅkha-basti. This record refers to a dispute between Hēmadēvāchārya of the Śaṅkha-basti at Huligeṛe and Śivarāmayya, the āchārya of the Sōmidēva temple of the same place regarding the lands belonging to their temples. It was referred to mahāpradhāna Nāgaṇṇa-daṇṇāyaka who, with the assistance of Saṅgamadēva, the purōhita and the scholars in the palace went through the concerned documents and settled the dispute in favour of Hēmadēvāchārya. It contains the signatures of several individuals who were probably witnesses to the record described as jayapatra .

cells.object: Slab built into the wall of the backyard of the Taluk office.

text.remarks: It registers a deed of settlement of dispute between the Jainas of Šamkha-basti headed by Samkhanāchārya and Hēmanāchārya and Kāļahastidēva and Sivarāmēdēva of the temple of Dakshiṇa Sōmēšvaradēva regarding the use of certain honours (like the flags of  ashṭadik-pālas ) which had been misappropriated by the Jainas for their deity. Two of the disputants Hēmanāchārya and Šivarāmadēva are identical with their namesake that figure in KN 718 Hence the record will have to be assigned to 1418 A.D.

cells.date: Šaka 1283, Šārvari, Āšvija šu. 13, Wednesday = 1360 A.D., September 23, the Šaka year being current.
cells.reference: MAR., 1942, No. 37; EC., V, Hn. 19; VIII (Rev.), Al. 41
cells.object: Stone set up to the south of Janārdana temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the grant of two villages, Chendanahaļli in Manaliga-nāđu and Horada-nūrāpura in Mūga-nāđu, yielding respectively 50 and 30 gadyānas . besides some (garden) lands below tanks like Karađiyakeğe. etc. with all incomes from kexegođage , āxyvaja and banaguttige and free from all imposts to god Janārdana of Seṭtigana-pāļeya by Tippaṇṇa-vođeya (Tippāmātya), son of Ēśvaradēva of the Brahmakshatriya family and Virāmbike and husband of Simgāradēvi. The gift was made for the daily worship and offerings and special worships etc., on specified days, maintaining one lamp-waver ( ārati-juna ). one service man ( pa-richūraka ), two florists, one piper, one drum ( đavaṇe )-beater and one servant ( āliga ). among whom the grant was to be shared. The beneficiaries included Dāmaṇṇa and Jamnakalpa. The donor, a general under Bukkarāya (I), described as his eldest son ( hiriya kumāra ), is said to have defeated a certain Gōpāladēva of Uchchaṅgi and is eulogised as Śriṅgārapurt chakravarti, temkaṇarāya-rāvutara-gamḍa etc.

The record refers to the rule of Achyutadēvarāya.

cells.date: Šaka 1578, Viļambi, Māgha šu. 15, Sōmavāra, lunat eclipse. Apparenaly irregular. Viļambi-1659 A.D., January 28, Friday, when there was no eclipse.
cells.remarks: Basavanahalli Copy of an epigraph built into Rachchekafte . Records the grant of the village Basavanahalli-agrahāra in Arakalagūđu-hōbaļi of Biļuha-nāđu-vaļita, belonging to Bēlūru-sime, which had been bestowed upon the donor's ancestor, Křishṇappa-nāyaka as amaramāgaņi by Yeřa Křishṇarāya, as an agrahāra to 6 Brāhm-āṇas (named) by Veñkaṭādri-nāyaka, for the merit of his parents. The donor, son of Křishṇappa-nāyaka and grandson of Veñkaṭādri-nāyaka, was a chief of Bēlūru bearing the epi-thets like Maṇināgapuravarādhišvara and Smdhu-gōvinda . The original record does not appear to have been examined. The given date is too late for Křishṇarāya, who, surprisingly indeed, is said to be ruling from Ghanagiri. A very unreliable record.

cells.remarks: Sone set up by the roadside near Guṇđagaṭte. Virōdhikṛit , Chaitra śu. 1, Sunday. Probably = 1371 A. D., March 18, Tuesday. Worn out. This is described as an arrangement ( samsthe ) made by the mahājanas of Namja-nāthapura alias Hebbāle about the maintenance of four carts for the tank, Hiriyakeṇe, of the village by Bomma-gauđa and three others (named) of Bōļukētanahaļi, the hamlet. They were allowed collection of certain specified taxes like arurana and binugude xe , and were remitted from some others like alīū , anyāya , kaddāya , solage etc. It was stipulated that the beneficiaries themselves were to meet the expenses of the buffalo ( kōṇa ), wooden implements ( kirumuļū ), iron ( kabbuna ) and oil for the carts. Simganna wrote the record. Ends with the sign manual śrt Vijaya Sōmanātha .
