cells.remarks: A set of two copper-plates in the possession of Puļtasāmayya of Koṇanūru. Refers to the rule of Širaņga, son of Gōpālīrāja and registers a gift of the village Bharata-vaļļi adjacent to the village Kaṇatūru in Vēlāpuri rāshtra of Karṇāṭa-dēša by the king to Šañkara of Kāśyapa-gōtra, son of Šañkara-bhatṭa, The donee, after receiving the village, divided it into 13 vrittis and gifted them to several Brāhmaṇas (named) and a plot of wet land of the sowing capacity of 3.5 khaṇđugas and dry land in the village Kaṇatūru to Šañkaraiyya as an emolument ( prabhu-mānya ) for holding the office of hēbārike of the village. The record ends with the sign-manual śrt Rāma .

Refers to the rule of Širaņga, son of Gōpālīrāja and registers a gift of the village Bharata-vaļļi adjacent to the village Kaṇatūru in Vēlāpuri rāshtra of Karṇāṭa-dēša by the king to Šañkara of Kāśyapa-gōtra, son of Šañkara-bhatṭa, The donee, after receiving the village, divided it into 13  vrittis  and gifted them to several Brāhmaṇas (named) and a plot of wet land of the sowing capacity of 3.5  khaṇđugas  and dry land in the village Kaṇatūru to Šañkaraiyya as an emolument ( prabhu-mānya ) for holding the office of  hēbārike  of the village. The record ends with the sign-manual  śrt Rāma .

cells.date: Śaka 1305 Rudhirōdgāri, Kārttika, śu. 1, Monday, Svāti-nakshatra =1383 A. D., October 26. f.d.t., .64
cells.object: On the outer wall to the north of the inner shrine in the enclosure of the Rāmēśvrara temple.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of the village Rāmanāthapura, and income from taxes like ađedere , tax on looms ( maggadere ), taxes on potters ( kuṇmara ), oil-mongers ( gāṇiga ) and barbers ( nāyiṇda ) collected from the villages belonging to that god, inclusive of tolls on two boundaries ( era-đu gaļiya sumka ) but exclusive of tolls collected on Akshatadige (?) for worship and offerings to god Rāmanātha, by Kariya Máyaṇnaa, the households ervant (? maneya ) of the king, The later damaged portion, seems to record a gift of taxes on the looms. motĵe-sumka , vaļavāru (customs on imports), from out of the above mentioned incomes, to god Gōpināthadēva for the morning offerings, perpetual lamp etc.

cells.date: Saka 1680. Vikāri, Magha šu. 7. The  tithi  = 1660 A.D., January 8 Sunday
cells.remarks: Single copper-plate in the Subrahmanyēśvara temple. Records the grant of the village Yakkaṭi, in Marāvūra-sthala, belonging to Narasimhapura-sime for the service of god Prasanna Subrahmaṇyēśvara of Rāmanāthapura by Narasimha-nāyakā, the chief of Bēlūru. The Narasimhapura-sime had been originally bestowed upon the donor's ancestor Yara Kṛishṇappa-nāyaka, as amara-māgaṇi by king Kṛishṇa-rāya ruling from Vidyānagara. The gift was exclusive of the new village Raṅgāpura newly formed nearby, to the north, by the donor's elder brother Raṅgappa-nāyaka, and included lands in Bhorachikāṭte (?). The donor was the son of Lakshmappa-nāyaka and grandson of Kṛishṇappa-nāyaka of Kāśyapa-gōtra and Āpastambha-sūtṁa.

cells.date: Saka 1217, Durmukhi, Māgha ba. 11, Wednesday. Irregular.  Tithi  = 1297 A.D., 20th January 20. Sunday, the Śaka year being 1218. But, in Manmatha (Śaka 1217), the  tithi  = 1269 A.D., February 1. This is too early a date for Bukka. If the Śaka year is a mistake for 1278, the details correspond with 1357 A.D., February 15.
cells.object: On a stone lying near Timmappa's house.
cells.remarks: States that mahāvaḍṭ abyavahāri Mahadēvaṇṇa, son of Arjubhaṭṭayya, with the king's permission formed the new village-Lakshmipura. Since the royal channel from the tank of this village had to pass through some other villages like Māvanūru and Allālapaṭṭana in Chaṅga-nāḍu governed by the prince Bukkaṇṇa-vođeya, the king Hukkaṇṇa-vođeya (?) issued orders to the prince to see that the sides of the channel be rivetted with stones. Accordingly, at the instance of the prince, Sōvapparasa, the pradhāni , after fitting up the sides with stones, seems to have exchanged lands below that channel for certain other lands. Since the later part of the record is lost further details cannot be made out.

cells.date: Šaka 1291, Kilaka, Chaitra šu. 1. . . . =1368 A.D., March 20, Monday. The Šaka year was current.
cells.object: Stone set up in front of Małe Mallēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of lands in Aguļiya-bayalu for services to god Vūrađiya Mallikārjuna by the mahājīnas and the 1000 o'kcalu of Piriya-paṭtada-mahāgrahāra named Údbhava-sarva-jña Vira Vijaya Ballāļapura alias Arasiyakere who had the temple for the god newly constructed. It also registers a garden cultivated by Viraya, and probably land to the stone masons ( kalkuṭiga ). The gift was made under orders from mahāpradhāna Basavaya-daṇnāyaka when nāyaka Ācharesa, son of Sāūpeya Viṭha was administering. Narasimhadēva (son of ) sēnabōva Jamnaya wrote the record.

cells.date: Šaka 1457, Manmatha, Chaitra šu. 15=1535 A.D., March 19, Friday
cells.object: On a boulder on the sluice of the tank.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Chikka Gamđase in Honnavali-sime, belonging to his chief-taincy, inclusive of the hamlet Vođagarahaļi and exclusive of Hirīyūru and the hamlets Gollahaļli, Bommēnahaļli, Hāsēnahaļli and Vođeyanahaļli of Chikka Ganđese, to a number of Brāhmaṇas, by Rāmappa, son of Timmarasa of Parāśara-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākhā. cells.date: Šaka 1477, Rākshasa, Jyēshṭha śu. 10, Thursday = 1555 A.D., May 30.
cells.object: Stone set up to the right of entrance in the enclosure of Kaṇive Rāmēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: Refers to the rule of Rāmarāja (Rāma-nṇipāla) who is said to have defeated the Sultans, and imprisoned all the kings of Kēraļa-vaṭṭi, and records the construction of the temple of Kaṇuveya Rāmēšvara by Holeyagonđa-gauđa of Kolugunda, for the merit of his parents Chigaṇa-gonđa add Aji-akka. Hiriyaṇa-gonđa and his wife Bammaji were the grand parents of the donor belonging to the family of gauđas of Kolugunda. It also registers a gift to the god, of lands below the Hiriyakeře tank of Kolugunda, and also lands at Beļuvaļļi and Mosaļe by the same donor.

cells.date: Śaka 1560, Īśvara, Phālguṇa śu. 5, Thursday = 1638 A.D., February 8, Thursday, f.d.t. .11 While Veṅkaṭādri-nāyaka, the chief of Bēlūru, bearing epithets like  Maṇinā gapuravarādhi īśvara Sindhugovinda , etc., was ruling Bēlūru-rājya, a dispute arose between the Viraśaivas and the Jainas, when Huchchappadēva marked the pillars of the  basadi  of Vijaya Pāśvanātha-svāmi of Haļēbiḍu with the Viraśaiva religious symbol and Vijayappa erased the same  liṅgamudre . Several leaders of both religious groups like the  mahāmahattu  Basavappadēva of Haļēbiḍu and Paṭṭadadēva of Pushpagiri on the one hand and the Jaina-śeṭṭis of Bēlūru-rājya like P admaṇṇa-seṭṭi, son of Dēvappa-seṭṭi of Hāsana, on the other, met together and the  mahāmahattu  decided to allow the worship etc. in the  basadi  as it was being done from the beginning and that they would not object to it in any way. Kṛishnappayya, son of Kālappayya-mantri, the minister of Veṅkaṭādri-nāyaka was responsible for this amicable settlement of dispute.

Several leaders of both religious groups like the  mahāmahattu  Basavappadēva of Haļēbiḍu and Paṭṭadadēva of Pushpagiri on the one hand and the Jaina-śeṭṭis of Bēlūru-rājya like P admaṇṇa-seṭṭi, son of Dēvappa-seṭṭi of Hāsana, on the other, met together and the  mahāmahattu  decided to allow the worship etc. in the  basadi  as it was being done from the beginning and that they would not object to it in any way. Kṛishnappayya, son of Kālappayya-mantri, the minister of Veṅkaṭādri-nāyaka was responsible for this amicable settlement of dispute.

cells.date: Śaka 1304, Dundubhi, Kārttika ba. 10 ( daśami ) Sunday (Ādivāra)=1382 A. D., November 1, Saturday.
cells.object: On a set of four copper-plates in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Records the conferment of prithvī-śatṭitana (the mayorality) since he was the master to lay down rules of conduct and judgement, and a grant of svāmya to Muddeya-daṇṇāyaka. The nakara parivāra , mummaridaṇḍa , all the receivers of dues ( sakalasvāmyavantaru ), 300 Billa dependants (? kālgāhina billan-mū lūrpibbaru ) including holiyajaṅguli of several places like Vijayanagara, Hastināvati, Dōrasamudra, Gutti, Penugoṇḍa, Ādavāni, Udayagiri Chandragiri, Muļuvāyi, Kañchi, Pađeviđu, Chaduramgapaṭṭaṇa, Bārakūru, Honnāvara, Chandhāvura, Āraga, Chandragutti, Huligeṛe, Aṇṇigeṛe, Niđugallu, Chi (Be?)matanakallu, Taṛi-yakallu, Āneviddasaṛi, Kalleya, Telakalaṁbi and Siṅgapaṭṭaṇa, having assembled together and seated in vajrāsana in the presence of god Virūpāksha, agreed among themselves to pay several dues to Muddapa. The record enumerates in detail the dues : from the leased villa-ges 1 bēļe per gadyāṇa of income in gold ( suvarṇādāya ), 2 bēļes per khaṇḍuga of grains, 2 paṇas per 100 gadyāṇas upon the cost of navaratna (precious stones); likewise stipulated sums upon scenents etc. ( sugandha , kastūri , pachchaklapura etc.), clothes, grains, oils, fruits and vegetables, animals etc, with which the above mentioned bodies dealt. There are 4 lines of writing on the outer face of the first plate, in Kannada, stating that this record kept in the temple of Kēśava is a charter of grant of svāmya to the donee by the halaru of Sāhumūle .

cells.object: On three stones to the south of the  pushkariṇi  in the enclosure of the temple.
cells.remarks: Gives a genealogical account of the king who was the son of Bukka and grandson of Samgama and was ruling from Vijayanagara described as a new capital ( abhinava-mahārṇja-dhāni ) in Pampā. Then it eulogises his minister Vijaya Guṇđanātha. This general, at the instance of the king, got newly built the doorway and the seven-storeyed tower ( gōpura ) the original of which had been burnt by Gamga-śālār of Kaluburage and reinstitued several services and renewed grants to god Chennakēśava of Vēlāpuri, as it had been in vogue earlier in the period of Hoysala Vishṇuvardhana Biṭṭidēva.

cells.date: Bahudhānya, Bhādrapada śu. 10, [Va]. Probably = 1398 A.D., August 20, Tuesday taking  Va  as an abbreviation for Vaḍḍavāra.
cells.object: Stone in the field of Varadarājaiyangar near the Yagachi river.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of kaḍahus of portions of wet land of mālegāya (garland maker) Chauḍappan and Basappa and one kaḍahu in bhaṇagila-bayalu to god Śrī-Rāma and for feeding ascetics in the maṭha of Surēndratīrtha-śrīpāda of Bēlūru by Nāgarasa of Bēlūru under orders from Guṇḍappa-daṇṇāyaka-voḍeya who had himself received orders to the effect by the king. It states that this gift was in lieu of an original gift by Vira Bukkarāya according to which 4 varahas and 8 haṇas were to be spent by the palace to god Rāma and for the yatibhikshe of the maṭha of Surēndrātīrtha-śrīpāda of Bēlūru by Vira Bukkarāya through Teppada Nāgaṇṇa-voḍeya. Nāraṇadēva, the ūra-sēnabōva , wrote the record. The signatory is Nāgarasa.,

cells.date: Šaka 1337, (current) Jaya, Šrávaṇa ba. 10, Friday = 1414 A.D., August 10
cells.object: On the stone lamp-pillar ( dipastambha ) in the middle of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Records the erection of dipti-stambha for the krittikā festival of lights ( dipōtsava ) and a swing ( uyyāle ) for the dōlāmahōtsava of god Chennakēśava, by mahōpradhāna Baicha-daṇṇā-yaka. It seems to refer to the ancestry of the donor and states that Harihara II installed Baicha-daṇdēśa, probably his grandfather, in the office of general and later on, Bukka, Harihara's son took the present donor into service. The meaning of the extant portion is not clear.

cells.date: Šaka 1436, Bhāva, Šarad-ṛitu, śu. 10 = 1514 A.D., September 28 or October 28. The name of the month is not specified. It may be either Āśvayuja or Kārttika.
cells.object: On a slab in the western face of the platform round the flag staff ( garuḍastambha ) in the temple.
cells.remarks: The Sanskrit portion in the beginning records the setting up of a garuḍastambha in front of the temple of god Kēśava in Vēlāpuri, situated in Hoyisaṇa-dēśa, by Jakka-nṛipa, son of Timma, described as a subordinate of the king. The pillar (with the image of Garuḍa) is stated to be of gold; probably it was covered with gold plate. Could Timma be the same as Sāluva Timmarasa the famous minister ? The Kannada portion stops after citing the Śaka year 1436.

cells.date: Śaka 1443, Viśu, Māgha, śu. 15, Sthiravāra=1522 A. D., January 11, Saturday, f. d.t. .29
cells.object: On the first pillar in the left row at the south door.
cells.remarks: Records a gift to god Channakēśava of Vēlāpuri, for the merit of the king, of money income and paddy from three villages—Gaṅgāvara, Mallavaļi and Kūsāvara—situated in Hāvaṇige-nāđu of Gōṇibiđu—sime, by Siṅgappa-nāyaka, son of Maṇchchappa-nāyaka who is described as the 'son' of king Kṛishṇadēvarāya. The last portion, added lateron, states that the four individuals—Akaṇa—hebāruva, Chemnappa—hebāruva, Lakmīpati-ayya and Chemna ppārādhya—would share equally the money and paddy from two villages Gaṅgāvara and Mallavaļi.

cells.date: Śaka 1446, Tāraṇa, Śrāvaṇa śu. 5=1524 A. D., July 10
cells.object: On a stone near the ruined  Teppōtsuva-maṇṭapa  in the garden of the temple behind the Vishṇu-samudra tank.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the villages Nārāyaṇapura and Halumiri in Dēvaṇige-nāđu, belonging to Vastāre-sime, including incomes like suvarṇādāya and bhattādāya and all the income from ṭaṭavārike of Bēlūru and the areas belonging to god ( dēvara simega taṭa-varike ) for food offerings to god Channakēśava, feeding of 40 Brāhmaṇas in the chhatra etc., by Basavappa-nāyaka, son of Jakkaṇa-nāyaka, a servant ( ūlīga ) of the king, for the merit of his parents Jakkaṇa and Tipamma and also of Kṛishṇappa-nāyaka. The Vastāre-sime had been bestwed upon the donor by the king for his chieftaincy. It also records excavation of a pond ( teppakōṭa ) and the construction of the vasanta-maṇṭapa for festivals to be performed in Phālguṇa ba. 10 by the same person.

text.remarks: Records the grant of the village Chikagaddubaļi with its hamlet Govimđanahaļli in Hāsa-na-sīme-sthāļa for conducting the car festival of god Channakēšava during the  Sivaratri-festival , by Chikka Simgappa-nāyaka, son of Hiriya Simgappa-nāyaka, after receiving the same from Krīshṇappa-nāyaka, son of  hađapada  Bayyappa-nāyaka.

cells.date: Šaka 1477, Rākshasa, Māgha šu. 5. =1556 A.D., January 17, Friday.
cells.object: On the second stone, in the same place.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records that when a dispute arose between the pañchāļas and the samastahalaru (cultivators ?) of Chennigarāya-sthāna (temple ?) about the rights and privileges granted to the pañchāļas for their caste observances, Vēdanti Rāmarājayyappa, the 88 śrīvaishṇavas Banadarasayya, agent of Rāmarājayya Tirumalarājayya and Masanaba-setṭi, the agent of Rāmapayya, arrived at some decisions in the presence of Rāmarājayya Tirumalarājayya. Accordingly, the boundary of the locality of the pañchāļas at Bēlūru was demarcated within which they were to build their houses. celebrate ceremonies like marriages as prescribed in their community and enjoy certain privileges (which cannot be clearly made out) during the festivals celebrated at Vidyānagara. The writing to the right of the figure of Añjānēya on the top refers to goddess Kāļikā.

cells.date: Šaka 1491, Šukla, Šrāvaṇa šu. 11=1569 A.D., July 24, Sunday
cells.remarks: Broken stone lying to the left of the mahādvāra main entrance to the same temple, (now kept in kaisāle-manṭapa ) It registers a gift of the village Daṇāyakanahalļi in Jēvaņige-nāđu of Vastāre-sīme, renamed Pāpatimmāpura, for services in the Kēšava temple at Bēlūru by Veňkaťamma, daughter of Pāpatimma-nāyaka, a subordinate ( hađapada ) of the chief. Titles of Belūr chiefs are give here as also some verses in Sanskrit in praise of god Kēšava. The portion detailing the expenses from the total annual yield is slightly damaged.

cells.date: Šaka 1501, Bahudhānya, Šrāvaṇa ba. 8, Sthiravāra=1578,A.D., July 6, Saturday, f.d.t. .20. The Šaka year was current.
cells.object: On a stone set up to the southest of the Rāmānujachārya shrine in the temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Kođaganahaļi alias Rāmānujapura in Kesagōda-nāđu, yielding an income of 31 varahas for the daily offerings and celebrating monthly and yearly holy natal-star days ( tiru nakshatra ) of Rāmānujāchārya. The gift was made for the merit of the parents of the donor described as a devotee of god Chennigarāya of Elāpura, (name lost) his own master Malarāja and also Veňkatādri-nāyaka who had bestowed upon the donor Kesagōđa-nāđu as umbaļi . Veňkaťādri-nāyaka, was the son of Yarra Krīshṇappa-nāyaka, the Bēlūru chief. The record specifies the amount to be spent on several items. 12 varahas were to be given to sthānika Channappa, while the gardener and the attendant at the door were also to get fixed sums. The total amount of 30 varahas does not tally with the expenditure detailed.

cells.object: Stone set up near the peepul tree in the  prākāra  of Chennnakēśava temple.
cells.remarks: Mūrttiyappa-nāyaka and Puṭṭaṇṇa-nāyaka, sons of Pedi-nāyaka and Pedamma and the servants ( ūligas ) of Veñkaṭādri-nāyaka, son of Kṛīshṇappa-nāyaka, (the Bēlūr chief), had the kaisāle (verandah) of 26 squares ( aikaṇa ) constructed in the temple of Chennarāyasvāmi of Vēlāpura for the merit of his parents and grandfather Yarama-nāyaka.

cells.date: Śaka 1581, Vikāri, Kārttika-paurṇima, Śukravāra=1659 A.D., October 20. Thursday, f.d.t. .05. There was a lunar eclipse on that day.
cells.reference: EC., V, XV, Bl. 80; IX(Rev.), Bl. 173
cells.remarks: A set of two copper-plates in the possession of Koṇḍi Nārāyaṇāchārya. Records the sarvamānya grant of the village Kamdāvāra in Tagaranāḍa,-sime belonging to Vēlāpuri, to two Brāhmaṇas-Raṅga-bhaṭṭa and Giri-bhaṭṭa, sons of Viṭhala and grandsons of Datti-bhaṭṭa of Harita-gōtra and Āpastambha-sūtra, as dvibhōgya , each getting half of the village, with all rights and incomes. The gift was made after worshipping god Kēśava of Vēlāpura. The king was the grandson of Rāmarāja Raṅgarāja and son of Gōpālarāja. The grant bears the sign-manual śri Rāma in Kannada characters, at the end.

cells.date: Šaka 1582, (expressed in words), Šārvari, Hēmanta, Mahōdaya = 1660 A.D. The season occurred in Mārgaśira-Pushya months.
cells.remarks: One set of copper-plates in the possession of an individual. It registers a gift of 18, 10 and 5 khāris of lands situated in three villages, vīz., Keragalūru Niđugōđu and Channapuri near Vēlāpuri to a Brāhmaṇa, Veňkaṭēśa, son of Kanaka and grandson of Timmaṇa, of Ātrēya-gōtra and Āpastambha-gōtra (sūtra ?) who prayed for the same for the purpose of feeding the Brāhmaṇas. The donee was hereditarily in the service of the king who made it with a desire to have progeny ( sva-putrādi-sukha-pr ēpsuļ ).

cells.date: Šaka 1586, Šubhakṛit, Chaitra śu. 15. The cyclic year = Šaka 1584 when the  tithi  occurred on 1662 A.D., March 24, Monday.
cells.object: On a single copper-plate in the possession of Sindhuvaļli Gururāyāchārya.
cells.remarks: Hassan Distr'let Records a grant of the village Sindhuva!li in Abbaļige-nāđu, of Pālem-śima belonging to Bēlūru, as an agrahāra , by the king to Kuchchayya, son of Tiruveṅgalaya and grandson of Veňkaṭaya of Šrīvatsa-gōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and Rīk-śākhā in recognition of his having newly instituted the car festival for god Chennakēśava of Vēlāpuri, for meeting expenses to be incurred upon celebrating the car festival. This may rather mean that the gift was made in recognition of his having got a new chariot for the car festival, since it refers to brahma-pratishṭha , obviously of the chariot.

cells.date: Šaka 1588, Šōbhakṛit, Kārttika śu. 15. The  tithi  = 1663 A.D., November 5. The Šaka year was 1585.
cells.remarks: Single copper-plate in the possession of the same person. Registers a gift of 20 puṭlu of wet and dry lands below the channel at Gōrūru by the king to Allāđi Veňkaṭēśayya, son of Kanakappa, and grandson of Timmarasa, of Ātreya-gōtra Āpastambha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākhā, for his having got dug the channel ( kaṭtu kālava ) for the tank. The record ends with the sign-manual śri Rāma .

cells.date: Šaka 1596, Ānanda, Māgha śu. 5, Sthiravāra. The  tithi  = 1675 A.D., January 21, Thursday
cells.remarks: Single copper-plate with Koṇđi Narāyaṇāchārya. Registers a gift of the village Gummanaha!li as an agrahāra to Puṭaiya, son of Vasantaiya and grandson of Narasaiya of Bādarāyaṇa-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākhā by Veňkaṭādri-nāyaka, the chief of Bēlūru, son of Kṛishṇappa-nāyaka and grandson of Veňka-tādri-nāyaka of Kāśyapa-gōtra and Āpastambha-sūtra. The gift village was situated in Lakundada-nāđa-valīta (?) of Bēlūru-śime which had been granted to the donor's ancestor. Yara Krishṇappa-nāyaka, described as Maṇināgapuravarādhiśvara etc., by the then king Krishṇarāya. The record contains the sign-manual śri Veṇkaṭādri .

cells.king: Bukka (II) ruling from Harihara-paṭṭaṇa in Hoyisaṇa-rājya
cells.date: Śaka 1282, Vikāri, Pushya śu. 2, Thursday. Irregular. The  tithi  = 1359 A.D., December 22 Sunday. The Śaka year was current.
cells.object: Slab set up in a garden near the tank.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of the village Cheramanahalli in Tagare-nāḍu of Hoyisaṇa-nāḍa-valīta renamed chandrapura, after the donor's brother chandappa-vođeya, to god (?) Mallinātha of Bēlūru made over (?) to Kōyađe-vođeya, by Teppada Nāgaṇṇa-vođeya, who had received Tagare-nāḍu as uṇbalī from the king. It is stated that the king had camped at Harihara-paṭṭaṇa after achieving victory over his enemies. This is described as a patra-śāsana and attested ( voppa ) by Nāgaṇṇa-vođeya and Vira Bukkaṇṇa-vođeya.

cells.date: Śaka 1367(expressed by the chronogram  adri-shaĵ-guṇabhū ), Krōdhana, Chaitra 9. The fort light is not specified. The  tithi  might have occurred in March-April, 1445 A.D.
cells.remarks: EC.. XV, BI. 305 Copy of a set of three (?) copper-plates in the possession of Sitārāma-bhaṭta. Contains a genealogical account of the king, commencing from Saṅgama. States that the king who was suffering from heart disease ( hṛidrōga ), sent Nāganātha (Nāgā-bhaṭta), son of Masli-dīkshita of Bhāradvāja-gōtra and Yajuś-śākhā, to Kāśi and other holy places to perform religious ceremonies on behalf of the king and for his welfare according to vedic treatment ( vaidiki chikitsā ), and upon his return granted him the village Gövahalli, renamed Dēvarāyapura, as an agrahāra , along with its hamlet Bommahalli.

States that the king who was suffering from heart disease ( hṛidrōga ), sent Nāganātha (Nāgā-bhaṭta), son of Masli-dīkshita of Bhāradvāja-gōtra and Yajuś-śākhā, to Kāśi and other holy places to perform religious ceremonies on behalf of the king and for his welfare according to vedic treatment ( vaidiki chikitsā ), and upon his return granted him the village Gövahalli, renamed Dēvarāyapura, as an  agrahāra , along with its hamlet Bommahalli.

cells.date: Śaka 1308 ( vasu-vyōma-vahni-indu ), Krōdhana, Nabha (Śrāvaṇa)-paurṇami, Monday. =1385. A.D., July 22, Saturday, the Śaka year being current. There was a lunar eclipse on that day Gives the genealogical account of the dynasty from Saṅgama and registers a royal grant of lands in Harihara-mahārājapura in Hoysala-rājya after converting it into an  āgrahāra  on the occasion of a lunar eclipse in the presence ( sannidhi ) of Tuṅga, Pampa and Virū-pāksha.

cells.date: Šaka 1483, Dundubhi, Bhādrapada ba. 13 = 1561 A.D., September 7
cells.object: Stone set up at the village entrance.
cells.remarks: Registers a kalavu ( kaulu -contract ?) according to which the hebāruva of Mudreya Goraūru the gauđas like Virappa-gauđa of Mādihaļļi and others (named) who were prabhus of Mādi-haļi-sīme, converted the village Mulēnahaļi in Mūđihaļi-sthaļa granted for offerings to god Channigarāya into a pēļe renamed Chennigarāyapēļe and gave it to Chennapa-seťti with exclusive ownership and free from imposts like customs taxes on looms sīddhava on houses etc. on the condition that he would pay 30 varahas as kađu-guttige to god Chennigarāya Lakshmipati wrote the record. The record is described as pēļeya-šāsana .

cells.remarks: It records that with the permission of māhāsāmantādhipati Sōvaṇṇa-vođeya, his maneya taļa-vāra Bommeya-nāyaka, son of Maleya-nāyaka had the tower constructed upon the temple of Prasanna Kēšava of Koļatūru aļias Amřitanāthapura-agrahāra belonging to the chieftaincy ( amara-daṇāyakatana ) of his master and as a service for the village, made a grant of wet and dry lands to Brāhmaṇas, after purchase from several individuals paying the then current value. Chauđōja, son of Chauđōja engraved the record.

cells.date: Šaka 1441, Pramāthi., Mārgaśirsha,  Gō-dvādaśi  = 1519 A. D, December 3, Saturday.
cells.object: On a set of 3 copper-plates in the possession of Křishna-śāstri.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Saṇaba surnamed Timmāsamudra as sarvamānya , to Basavā dikshita, son of Raṅgu-yajva, of Jāmadagñya-vatsiya-gōtra, Āśvalāyanā-sūtra and Rīk-śā-khā, the pontiff ( guru ) of both the king as also of Ēśvara and Narasa. The donee divided the gift village into 27 vřittis and keeping 8 for himself, endowed the remaining to several Brāhmaṇas and village deities, besides two vřittis for gods Hari and Hara. The donee is said to have officiated in the sacrifices like Vājipēya performed by Vira Narasimha and later on by Křishnarāya himself, and to have been proficient in Grammar and other sciences. The record, composed by Sabhāpati was engraved by Viraṇāchārya. It contains the signmanual śri Virūpāksha at the end.

cells.date: Šaka 1452, Vikřiti, Aśvija ba. 7, Thursday. = 1530 A. D., October 13
cells.object: On a stone in' front of the Arkēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Dēvaraha!ļi in Kuřavaňka-sthaļa of Sātigrāma-sime with all its incomes, as puravarga , to god Arkanātha for the services of the same god Arkanātha[?] of Dēvaraha!ļi by Liņgaņņođeya of Harihara, the agent for the affairs of mahāsāmantādhi-pati Krīshṇappa-nāyaka, son of Basavappa-vođeya of Sōlūru. Liņgaņņođeya is stated to have been administering Sāti-grāma as a maņiha (a subordinate revenue officer). Pemmaņna-hebāruva, Timmarasayya of Beņnūru, the sēnabōva of the village and sevral gauđas and others (named) figure, probably as witnesses. Viśvanātha, son of Basavāchāri and grand-son of Vođeyappayya, said to have been known as jagadguru (among the Viśvakarmas ?), engraved the record.

cells.date: Šaka 1414, Rākshasa, Mārgašira ba. 10, Friday = 1495 A.D., December 11. However, the Šaka year was 1417
cells.object: On the left side of the  mahādvāra  of Jakkēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records the renewal of the gift of the village Dēyigeře in Diňđugūru-sthala of Sātigrāma-sīme, including income from taxes, as an agrahāra , for worship of and offerings to god Jakēśvaradēva of Jambūru of Hunnalāpura-nāđu and for the maintenance of temple servants like the priests, attendants and cooks. It is said that the gift village had fallen into ruins and was now renovated. The donor was daļavāyi Mallaņna-nāyaka, son of Nāgappa-vođeya on whom Narasaņna-nāyaka, son of Ēśvara-nāyaka, the sēnādhipati of the king, had bestowed the chieftaincy of Sātigrāma-sīme, and the gift had been renewed now for their merit The gift was actually made on the 15th day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika (November 2nd) in the presence of the Brāhmaņas of Diňđugūru and Jambūru. Another grant of the village Jambūru described as southern Kailāsa, was also made for the expenses of god.

cells.remarks: Two stones set up at the entrance of the village. Siddhārthi, Kārttika-paurņami =1499 A.D., October 18, Friday, f.d.t. .15. Fragmentary and worn out. Registers a grant of lands free from taxes on looms, marriages imports, exports, and on grains like rāgi and horsegram( huruļi )etc., in Kariyamāranahaļi for the merit of Krīshņarāya, probably upon request from Siņgappa-nāyaka through Aņn-yappa-nāyaka. It seems to state that the grant was to come into effect from Āśvija. The ruling king appears to be Narasaņna-nāyaka.

cells.date: Ēśvara, Māgha ba. 4, Friday =1398 A.D., February 5, the weekday being Tuesday.
cells.object: On a hero-stone set up in the enclosure of Šambhuliņgēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers the death of Bōrayya-nāyaka, son of some nāyaka (.. biya-nāyaka) in the battle fought at Marayavūru. The hero-stone was sculpted by āchārya Guṇdōja . Mentions Rāmaṇṇa-hemmāđi. The cost of setting up the hero-stone (?) appears to have been 12 gadyāṇas .

cells.date: Śaka, 1290, Kilaka, Bhādrapada śu. 10, Thursday=1368 A.D. August 24
cells.reference: EC., II (IEd.), No. 136; (II Ed.), No. 344; (Rev.), SB 475
cells.object: Stone set up to the east in the Bhaṇdāra-basadi.
cells.remarks: On a perition made by the Jainas of Āneyagonde, Hosapaṭṭaṇa, Penugonđe; Kallehapaṭṭaṇa and other places about the injustice made to them by the Śrivaishṇavas., the king, brought about a reconciliation between the Jainas and Śrivaishṇavas declaring that there was no difference between the two creeds and that Śrivaishṇavas should continue to protect the Jaina creed. Tātayya of Tirumala was to collect one haṇa annually from every Jaina home in the kingdom and with it appoint 20 bodyguards to the god at Bełaguła and with the reminder have the Jinālayas repaired and white-washed. Jainas were entitled to the honour of five great musical instruments and the kałāśa . Basuvi-seṭṭi, son of Haravi-seṭṭi of Kalleha having made a petition, the king sent for Tātayya and had (the charter-śāsana?) vated. Both the samayas , uniting, bestowed the dignity of Samigha-nāyaka on Basuviseṭṭi.

cells.date: Śaka 1437, Yuva, Śrāvaṇa-pūrṇima, Wednesday, lunar eclipse=1515 A.D., July 25
cells.object: On a set of 3 copper-plates in the possession of Kittāne Rāmappa.
cells.remarks: Records the grant by the king, of the village Kittāne, surnamed Tirumalapura, after the queen Tirumaladēvi, situated in Hāsana-sīme, of Hoysaṇa-rājya as sarvamṇnya to several Brāhmanas (named) having divided the village into 28 vrittis . Sabhāpati, wrote the record Mallaṇāchārya, son of Viraṇāchārya engraved the record. It says that the lēkhaka of the record also got one vritti and he might be either Sabhāpati or, more likely, Mallaṇāchārya. Although it says that the boundaries are written in dēśabhāshe i.e., Kannada, the record stops with that statement.

cells.language: Kannada (and one verse in Telugu) in Kannada
cells.date: Śaka 1454, Khara, Vaiśākha śu. 5, Monday=1531 A.D., April 21, Friday, the Śaka year being current.
cells.object: On a stone set up near the  raṅga-maṇṭapa  of Virūpāksha temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Uddūru to the Virūpāksha temple of Hāsana to feed 12 Brāhmaṇas daily in a satra , by Yellappa-nāyaka, son of Tippa-bhūpāla and nephew( aliya santāna ) (as also the agent for the affairs) of Channapaṇṇa, for the merit of Channapaṇṇa and for the prosperity of the king. The gift village is said to be situated in Hāsana-sīme, which belonged to the amaranāyakatana of Channapaṇṇa. The recipient of the gift was Dēvaru-bhaṭṭa, agent for the affairs of the temple of Virūpāksha who was one of the twelve to be fed daily.

cells.date: Šaka 1483 ( guṇa-vasu-amburāśi-indu ) Durmati, Kārttika šu. 12 ( utthānā-dvādaśi )=1561 A.D.. October 20.
cells.object: On a set of 5 copper-plates in the possession of Hariyappa.
cells.remarks: Records the sarvamānya gift of village Kabballi, surnamed Krishṇāpura, in Hāsana-sima, belonging to Sige-nāđu in Hoyisaṇa kingdom, as ēkabhōgya to Narasa-paṇṭita, son of Tippaṇa-paṇṭita and grandson of Ahōbala-paṇṭita of Ātrēya-gōtra. The record refers to the short period of rule of Veñkaṭādri, son of Achyutarāya, after whom Sadāśivarāya is stated to have ascended the throne with the help of Rāmarāja, the amāya who is discribed as Haribhakti-sudhānidhi and whose genealogy is recounted. It states that Krishṇappa-nāyaka, son of Aḍappa Bayyappa obtained the sanction of the king for the grant after having made an application to Rāmarāya. Thus virtually he would be the donor. Sabhāpati Svayambhu was the writer of this incription, which was engraved by Viraṇāchārya, son of Viraṇa.

cells.date: Šaka 1492, Rudhirōdgāri, Šrāvaṇa šu. 13, Monday. The  tithi  corresponds to 1563 A.D., August 2; but the Šaka year is a mistake for 1485.
cells.object: On a stone set up to the west of entrance of the Virūpāksha temple.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Seṭṭihaļli in Hāsana-sime which had been leased on tenure ( guttage ) to the donor, Bukkaṇṇa-nāyaka, brother of Tammappa-nāyaka and son of kandā-chārada Kāchappa-nāyaka, as sarvamānya for conducting the car festival ( rathōtsaya ) of god Virūpākshadēva. The donor was a subordinate (?) of Krishṇappa-nāyaka, son of Bayyappa-nāyaka (of Bēlūr) who had received Hāsana-sime as a fief for his chieftaincy ( amara-nāyakatana ) from Rāmarājayya, the agent of king Sadāśiva who is described as the son of Achyutarāya. The villages Biranahal!li, Āduvalì, Rájaghaṭta, Manđegenaha!i, Guđđanaha!i and Yelagaṇa-gilu, belonging to god Virūpāksha, Hułēnaha!i belonging to god Hałada Rāmēśvara and Hon nēnaha!li belonging to god Vighnēśvara were all exempted from payment of taxes like jōđi, beđige, hi!ṭu, huggi etc. by the same donor. The record, written by Nañjappa Upādhya son of Nañjappa Upādhye of Hāsana, was engraved by āchārya Kallayya, son of Lakhaṇā chārya of Hāsana. An appendix at the end registers some grant of land in Bhīranaha!i in the presence of Virūpāksha, to Kallayya, the sculptor.

cells.date: Šaka 1466, Tāraṇa, Mādhava šu. 3, ( akshaya trītiya ).  Tithi  = 1524 A.D.. April 7, Thursday
cells.object: On a set of 3 copper-plates in the possession of  šānubhōg  Nāgappa of Ramgapura.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Muttatti named Krīshṇarāyapura in Bēlūru-sime of Hoyisaṇa-nāđu, by the king, as ēkabhōgya , to Krīshṇa-dikshita, son of Nāñjinātha, grand-son of Ramganātha, of Kaṇđa-varṇśa belonging to Jamadagnāvatsa-götra and Āśvalāyana-sūtra, well-versed in Vēda, Vēdānta. Purāṇa etc., performer of sacrifices like Sarvakratu , Vājāpēya , etc. and eulogised as kavitārasa-sarvajṇa . The gift was made in the presence of god Virūpāksha on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadrā. The record, composed by Sabhāpati, was engraved by Appanāchārya, son of Viraṇāchārya. On the front faces of each plate on the top, the name Muttatti is engraved.

cells.date: Šaka 1484, Dundubhi, Mārgaśira ba. 2, Saturday = 1562 A.D., December 12.
cells.object: On a stone standing in front of the Virabhadra temple.
cells.remarks: This record registers grant of income from taxes like ānēya (?) sumka , taļavārike , solage , biṭti , alivu , anyāya , samayadavaru (?) in the village Kudurugunđi (situated in the Hāsana-sime) for the service of offering incense, lights and food in the temple of Bayala Virabhadra, by Bukkapa-nāyaka, a subordinate of Krīshṇappa-nāyaka (same as Eṛa Krīshṇappa-nāyaka, the chief of Bēlūr), son of Bayappa-nāyaka. The donor was the younger brother of Tammappa-nāyaka and son of Kāchappa-nā paka. Chief of Bēlūr had received Hāsanada-sime as amara-māgaṇi by Rāmacha-ayya (Rāmarājayya)-mahā-arasu, the kāryākarta of the king. Kuduregunđi had itself been bestowed upon the donor by the chief as svāsthe .

cells.date: Śaka 1483, Dundubhi, Bhādrapada śu. 13, Thursday, Pushya-nakshatra = 1562 A.D. September 10, the Śaka year being 1484.
cells.remarks: Two sides of a stone, south of the dhvajastaṭbha of Rāmēśvara temple. This damaged inscription records the remission of taxes in the hamlets of Niđiviđi, viz., Niđiviđi, Pura, Chiṭtanaha!li and Chilanaha!li in Hāsana-sīme belonging to the vattige of Virūpāksha-nāyaka, son of Basavappa-nāyaka, and younger brother of Timmappa-nāyaka. The grant was made for the prosperity of Krīshṇappa-nāyaka, son of Bayappa-nāyaka (of Bēlūru) who was administering Hāsana-sīme as nāyakatana , received from Rāmarājayya, the agent for the affairs of the king, who is described as the son of Achyutarāya. The record on the second side is badly damaged. It seems to record the consecration of god Rāmēśvara (at ?) Niđiviđiyapura.

cells.date: Śaka 1454, Nandana, Jyēshṭha śu. 5, Monday=1532 A.D., May 9, Thursday
cells.object: Stone set up in the  raṅgamaṇṭapa  of Dharmēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of the village Vogaraha!li in Yeleyūru-sthaļa of Śāntigrāma-sīme to Dēvaru-bhaṭta, the priest of the temple of Dharmēśvara of Śāntigrāma, for offerings to god Dharmēśvara and the processional image of Chandraśēkhara, as also for feeding daily 10 Brāhmaṇas, inclusive of Dēvaru-bhaṭta himself. The donor was Keĵeya Timmarasa, son of Dēma-bhūpāla and grandson of Dhamḍappa. Timmabhūpa was the elder brother of Dēmarasa. The donor had received Śāntigrāma-sīme for his chieftaincy ( amara-daṇṇā yakatana ) from the king.

cells.object: On a pillar at the eastern entrance gateway to the village.
cells.remarks: Records the erection of the stone gateway, ornamented with a tiger face ( huli-mukha ) by Basavarā jad dēva-mahā-arasu of Pūdūru-vamśa, the chief of Nuggiha!li. The genealogy of their chief is given and therefrom we learn that the first member of the family, Tirumalarāja, of Ātrēya-gōtrā, Āpastambha-sūtra, Sāvāśva-pravara and Yajuś-śākhā belonging to the lunar family was the son-in-law ( aļiyandiru ) of Prauđhadēva-māhārāya. The genealogy is given thus : Tirumalarāja→Rāyođcya, the chief of Nuggiha!li→Induśēkhararāja→Basavarāja. Prauđhadēvarāya may probably be Mallikarjuna, since, working backwards the date of Tirumalarāja may be fixed after 1450 A.D., The last portion of the record is damaged and refers to Siṅgaṇa-hebāruva.

cells.date: Šaka 1332, Durmati, Vaiśākha. śu. 1, Bhārgava-vāsara Irregular. The cyclic year corresponds to Šaka 1356 when the  tithi  occurred on 1439 A.D., April 9, Friday, f.d.t.·53. In Šaka-1332 the  tithi  fell on 1410 A.D., April 5, Saturday. On neither of these dates was Harihara ruling.
cells.remarks: Copy of a copper-plate in the possession of an individual. Registers the grant of the village Gubbi, renamed Bukkarājēśvarapura, in Końga-nāđu-vishaya ( vēntheya ) of Hoysala-dēśa, by the king to several Brāhmaṇas (named) on the occasion of the consecration of god Bukkarājēśvara. The total income of the village seems to have been 120 kula-gadyāṇa , Kaṇthirāyi and huṭṭuvaļi-gadyāṇa 300. In all likelihood this is a spurious grant. Reference to Kaṇthirāyi and the unreliable date indicate that this is an unreliable record.

cells.date: Šaka 1317 (reckoned by  rishi-chandra-agni-vidhu ), Yuva, Māgha šu. 7, Sunday =1396.A.D., January 16, Monday.
cells.remarks: Set of 3 copper-plates of Hariharapura-agrahāra. Registers the grant of a village Tavanidhi, renamed Hariharapura along with its hamlets Hosahaļļi, Šigarahaļļi, and Bairahaļļi including Kāchanahaļļi, situated in Kumchika-sthaļa of Nārasimhapura-sime, to Mādhavādhvari, son of Keśava of Kallamāļige belonging to Ātiēya-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākhā. The gift was made by the king on the day of rathasaptami in the presence of god Virūpāksha, on the bank of the Tuņgabhadrā. The boundaries are enumerated in Kannada.

cells.date: Vijaya, Kārttika śu. 1, Wednesday = 1413 A.D., October 25
cells.object: Slab set up in a rice field to the east of the village.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Bekkanahałli renamed Gaurāpura after the name of his mother Gaurādēvi, by Mādaṇṇa, son of Chikka Vijeṇṇa and grandson of Teppada Iśvaradēva upon whom the chieftaincy of Godumale-nāđu had been bestowed. The gift village, which formed a part of the 4 villages in the hill of that nāđu was given to Mallināthadēva, of Rāyasamudra, as maṭha-mānya , with the consent of the inhabitants and with all rights of possession and enjoyment, like incomes from garden, māra , fixed tenure, kođe (?), bālē (?) etc. The record is described as Durgāpurada-śāsana .

cells.remarks: Summaries , 1946-47, No. 6 ; KI., VI, No. 62 This damaged inscription says that Gōvindadēva-vođeya was ruling Haive, Tuļu and Koñ-kaṇa regions. It registers a gift of lands, after purchase from Mahābala-bhaṭṭa, by Virūpāyi, daughter of Mādaṇṇa, for feeding 4 Brāhmanas and also one cook in the feeding house ( satta ) attached to the maṭha at Gōkarṇa. The gift land was leased out free of taxe s like asantāya , biṭṭi and birāđa and the lease-holders were to pay a stipulated sum of money and rice annually to Dāmōdara-bhaṭṭa on condition that he would feed Brāhmanas daily in the satra .

cells.date: Śaka 1312, Pramōda, Chaitra śu. 1, Friday = 1390 A.D., March 18
cells.reference: ARIE., 1957–58, No. 332 ;  Summaries , 1946–47, No. 5; KI., VI, No. 61
cells.object: Slab in the field near the well called  umbu-bhāvi  near Alakki temple.
cells.remarks: This damaged inscription records a gift of land situated in Maleya-nāđu of Haive-rājya made by a chief (name lost) administering Haiva, Tuluva and Koñkaṇa countries. A further gift of land was made for feeding Brāhmaṇas in a satra on the auspicious day of lunar eclipse after purchase from a person whose name also is lost. The record refers to the mahanta of the Gōkarṇa temple and to Timma-nāyaka; The lunar eclipse referred to occurred on April 29 of the same year. The record must have been set up only after this date.

cells.date: Śaka 1337, Manmatha, Mārgaśira ba. 13, Friday=1415 A.D., November 29.
cells.object: Slab in the house of Nagu Tippayya-gauđa.
cells.remarks: Summaries , 1946-47, No. 7; KI., VI No. 64 This badly worn out record refers to Bachaṇṇođeya ruling Haive, Tuļu and Koñkaṇa regions from his capital at Honnāvura. It registers a gift of land by Maduka-nāyaka, Bira-nāyaka and Bomma-nāyaka in the presence of god Mahābaladēva of Gōkarṇa-kshētra. The first part of the record refers to the cyclic year Durmukhi corresponding to 1416-17 A.D. Hence it may be concluded that the record came into existence only during that year.

cells.date: Śaka 1338, Durmukhi, Kārttika ba. 10, [Mandavāra]=1416 A.D., November 14, Saturday.
cells.object: Slab in the field of V.S. Nadkarni.
cells.remarks: Summaries , 1946-47, No. 9, KI., VI, No. 65 It registers a grant of land to Sōma-tārakkura by Mallapa-sāvanta, his aļiya Bommaṇa-nāyaka, Biraṇṇa, son of Bira-heggađe and others. Probably the land was purchased for a token sum, since the same appears to have been gifted in the presence of god Mahābala of Gōkarṇa for running a feeding house, when mahāpradhana Bāchaṇṇođeya was ruling Haive, Tuļu, Koñkaṇa regions from his capital Honnāvura. All the details are lost. The name of the king is lost. But, on the basis of the titles and the date, it may be assigned to Dēvarāya I.

cells.date: Śaka 1352, Sādhāraṇa, Phālguṇa śu. 3 Thursday=1431 A.D., February 15
cells.object: Slab in the field of Subbayya Sannappa Naik Gaonkar.
cells.remarks: Summaries , 1946-47, No. 10; KI., VI, No. 67 It registers an agreement ( vođambađike ) entered into between two dāyādis . In this connection it refers to Sōma-tārakkura, Biraṇṇa-nāyaka of Hosagēri who was an aļiya of Bommi-seťti and his aļiya Bommaṇṇa-nāyaka. A gift of land free from taxes appears to have been made on the occasion, after purchase, probably for maintaining a feeding house, in the presence of god Mahābaladēva of Gōkarṇa. Māhāprdhāna Tipaṇṇodeya was ruling Haive, Tuļu and Koñkaṇa regions from his capital Honnāvura.

cells.date: Śaka 1473, Sādhāraṇa, Āśvija ba. 5, Bhaumavāra (Tuesday) = 1550 A.D., September 30. The Śaka year was current.
cells.object: Slab standing in the field of Kushe Nāyappa-gauṇđa.
cells.remarks: Summaries , 1946-47, No. 11; ARIE.. 1957-58, No. 339; KI., VI, No. 70 States that mahāmaṇḍalēśvara , Sāluva Kṛishṇadēvarasa-ođeya, was governing Nagire, Haive Tulu and Koñkaṇa rājyas . The village Uluvare which was under the control of the Sāluva chief and the lands which were being enjoyed by Bālugeya Dēvapaya and others, were transferred to Sadāśiva-nāyaka, son of Chauḍa-gauḍa of Keĵadi, after purchasing the same for some amount, for the purpose of gifting the same to god Mahābala of Gōkarṇa for daily anointment with Pamchāmṛita , worship and offerings of avasara-kaṭṭaĵe and for maintaining a feeding house. The gift was exempted from taxes like vosage,asantāvya , kāṇike etc. It also records a gift for the bhikshṇ-svāsthe to the pontiff Sarasvati-śrīpāda.

cells.date: Śaka 1356, Pramādi, Kārttika ba. 10 = 1433 A.D., November 6, Friday. The Śaka year was current.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1929-30, B.K. No. 117; KI., I No. 53; SII., XV, No. 247
cells.object: On a slab standing near the Haslara huts.
cells.remarks: Badly damaged. It records a gift of land, free of imposts, by adhikāri Saṇṇu-nāyaru, and the dēśā śamastaru of Bayilūru ? in conjunction with the pontiff Surēśvara-śrīpāda to Nārā yaṇa-maṭha of Gujjāđi, for the exposition of purānas daily in the Mađakēśvara temple and for thirty days in the maṭha in the month of Sōne i.e. , Śrāvana. It was stipulated that he should be invited by the people of the village to attend various ceremonies and festivals like marriages, thread ceremonies, etc. that take place in their houses and that no one should meddle with his other possessions and seek to impose taxes like mane-haṇa , noga-kaṇa , belĵākaraṇe , belūdamṛja etc., on them. Kēśava, son of nāđasēnabōva Gaṇapaṇṇa of Śiriyali wrote the record which was engraved by Išarāchāri, son Kōṭi-āchāri. Nārāyaṇa-chimneya of Sābāle and Nārāyaṇa, (son ?) of Mādhava-jēti and grandson (?) of Sambhu datta approved of this. Mahāpradhāna Purushōttama-vođeya is said to be administering Tulu and other rājyas from Bārakūru, (In ARSIE., 1929-30 and SII., XV this place is said to be in Honavar Taluk.) ARSIE., 1929-30, B K. No. 1I8; KI., I, No. 55; SII., XV, No. 248 On a broken slab lying in the Mārkaṇdēśvara temple. Kannada Saṅgama; Dēvarāya II Śaka 1356, Pramādicha Kārttika ba, 10, Sunday=1433A.D., November 6, Friday. The Śaka year was current. Contents of the record is same as in No. KN 867 above. Purushōttama-vođeya is stated to be governing Tuļu-rājya. Since the stone is broken details are lost.

cells.object: Stone standing near the  basti .
cells.remarks: 1) Śaka 1461, Viļambi, Jyēshṭha ba. 3, Thursday=1538 A.D.. May 16. Śaka year was current; 2) Tāraṇa, divaļige ; 3) Dhātu, Āśvayuja ba 14, Friday=1516A.D., October 24; 4) Viļambi, divalige Refers to the rule of mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Krīshṇadēvarāya-ođeya (the Sāļuva chief?) over Nagire, Haiva, Tuļu and Koñkaṇa. He was the husband (?) of Padmāmbikā, the sister of Sāļuva Dēvarāya and Saṅgirāya, the brothers, born in the family of Māvarasa of Nagire. Narasaṇa-atikāri, son of Saṇṇi-nāyaka of Seṭṭihalli had a chaityālaya constructed at Kannana-balīru and the image of Supārśva-tirthēśvara consecrated therein, and made a gift of lands some of which he received from Bhairādēvi-amma, yielding 208 muđes of paddy, besides money, for worship and offerings and celebrating festivals and rituals like hāladhāre ashṭānnika , jivadayāshṭami etc. and feeding asceties. The charity was to come into force from the 2nd date. The basti was later renovated by Bhairu-heggađe, son of Saṅgu-nāyaka who also made a gift of lands yielding 101 muđes . This was also to come into force on the second date. The record thereafter registers a gift of land yielding 18 muđes by Saṅgu-nāyaka, son of Saṇṇappa-nāyaka of Honnavura to the basti after purchase from mahāmaṇdalēśvara Sālūva Immađi Dēvarāya-ođeya, on the third date. Another grant of land by Sātaṇa-nāyaka of Holeya-balī (born to Saṅga-bhāṇa at Nagire?), after purchase from Kṛishnadēvarāya-ođeya, the governor, is recorded thereafter. This was to come into operation from the last date cited.

cells.object: Inscribed stone in the Pārśvanātha-basti.
cells.remarks: Śaka 1332, Sarvadhāri, Kārttika śu. 10, Monday. Irregular The cyclic year Sarvadhār i occurred on Śaka 1330 when the tithi occurred on 1408 A.D., October 29, Monday. On the death of Māllirāya, son of Haivarasa and younger brother of Saṅgama-bhūpa, the latter ( mahāmaṇdalēšvara Samgirāya, son of Haivarasa and Saṅkamma, the chief of Hāduvalli ?) provided for the ( samudāya ) congregation of the whole town which had the nišidi set up in memory, in the heart of Baṭṭakaļa. Samgirāya is described as Hāduvaļlipuravarādhīšvara .

cells.remarks: This long but yet probably incomplete record introduces the king as the son of Raņgarāya who was the son of Krīshṇarāya, and grandson of Išvara-bhūpa. He was served ( architah , by Rāmarāja. Chennamāmbā, same as mahāmaṇdalēšvara Chennabhairādēvi governing Saṅgitapura, Vrīttapura etc. is introduced thereafter. It records several grants made for ahāradāna and other religious purposes. A certain seṭṭi , son of Dēvu-seṭṭi, the private secretary ( narma-suchiva ) of Dēvarasa-vođeya made a grant of land on the second date noted above. One grant refers to the shops of Ambala once granted by the halaru-seṭṭi-kāra-samastaru for the worship of Pāršvanātha of Hirebasadi, in the name of Dēvarasa-vođeya, grandson of mahāmaṇdalēšvara Dēvarasa-vođeya. This is said to have been made at the expiry of the month Krittike (Kārttika) of the year Piņgaļa. The editor of the record (Sri R. S. Panchamukhi) has equated this date with 1557 A.D., But this would be nearly 5 years later than the year Paridhāvi (= 1552 A.D.,) on which date Chennabhairādēvi herself made a grant, with the consent of the local body of traders to the effect that they would undertake to safeguard. There is also a reference to the provision made for the golden prabhāvaļi . Some of the lands granted were purchased or held on rental basis vāra or antarāruvāra ) and some female donors-like Nāgarasi-adhikārti, Bommarasa-adhikari and daughter of Bommaṇa-seṭṭi, Saṅkama-nāyakiti, the daughter-in-law (or neice sose ) of Nagappa-seṭṭi-also figure herein making grants of land or money ( hiriya nija-varaha ga; hiriya guļige nija ga varaha ). On the fifth date, 1545A.D., we find Dēvasēnadēva, discipline of Guṇabhadra-bhaṭṭāraka of Kārampje making a grant for god Pāršvanātha of Hiriya-basadi. Nāraṇadēva-nāyaka, son of Guđiliņga-nāyaka made a gift, in the name of his younger brother Yemkappa-nāyaka, for anointment with milk ( hāla-dhāre ) of the sāhasra-pada Chandranāthasvāmi in the upper storey ( nele ) at Bidare and also a gift for the Brāhmaṇa who maintains the water-shed ( aravatṭige ) near the hero-stone set up in memory of that Yeṁkappa-nāyaka. The inscribed stone appears to have been set up after the latest date mentioned above, viz. 1557 A.D.,

cells.date: Śaka 1471, Naļa, Kārttika śu. 5 = 1556 A.D., October 8.
cells.object: Slab standing in the compound of Baṇṇa-basti.
cells.remarks: The first part of the record upto line 29, in Sanskrit, is said to be the composition of the poet Vard'hamāna-muni. This refers to Chennabhairava-mahādēvi, daughter-in-law of Kṛishṇadēva (and daughter of Bhairādēvi) and her minister Jeṭṭi-nāyaka. Nāraṇa-nāyaka, son of Viraṇa-nāyaka, a general of Bhairādēvi and Timmarasa got a chaityālaya for Vardhamāna-jinēndra erected and made a gift of lands for worship etc., after purchase from mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Chennabhairādēvi. The gift was made also for celebration of several festivals like Karttika-pūje , Śivarātri , Jivadayāshṭami . Yugādi , Śruta-pañchami , nalu batu ( hālina-abhishēka ) in the month of Śrāvaṇa, ashṭāhnika daśala-kshaṇa-pūje . It refers to several dishes to be served every day of the week like sojige-tuppa on Sunday, sōvalike-pāyasa on Monday, uṭada-dadhige (?) on Tuesday, yeṇne-ghārige on Wednesday, kaṇike-ghārige on Thursday, muditige (?) on Friday and hārasukki (?) on Saturday. The record mentions the donor's wife Lingammā and his sister Saṅkamāmbā whose daughter Mallarasi had married Timma.

cells.date: Śaka 1465, Šubhakṛit, Kārttika ba. 15, Monday=1542 A.D., November 6, Monday, f.d.t.·29
cells.object: Hero-stone near the Pārśvanātha basti.
cells.remarks: The Śaka year was current. Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara , Saṅgitapuravarādhiśvara Chennādēvi-amma, daughter-in-law of Dēvarasa-vōđeya was governing Hāđuvaļi, Baṭakaļa and other kingdoms under the orders of the king. It commemorates the death of Emkappa-nāyaka, brother of Nāraṇadēva-nāyaka and the aļiya (nephew ?) of Liňga-nāyaka who stopped the paraṅgadavaru at the gate of the palace when Kapitamēra, the Paraṅga, laid seize to Baṭakaļa and having burnt the city marched on the palace. The hero who fell in the fight after killing the enemies, was attached to the service of Gururāya-vođeya.

cells.date: Šaka 1465, Šubhakřit, Kārttika šu. 15, Monday=1542 A.D., October 23.
cells.object: On the hero-stone near the  basti  containing KN.875 above.
cells.remarks: PRKRI.; 1939-40, No. 76; K I., III, No. 13 Mahāmaṇdalēšvara Chennādēvi-amma, daughter-in-law of Dēvarasa-vođeya, was governing Hāđuvaļi, Bhaṭakala and other rājyas from her capital Saṅgitapura. The record refers to the death of Emkappa-nāyaka, brother of Nāraṇadēva-nāyaka, the son-in-law (nephew) of Liňga-nāyaka, the servant ( ūļiga ) of the queen, in a fight against the paraṅgadavaru (Cf. KN, 875 above) and registers a grant of land of the sowing capacity of 10-1/2 muđis of paddy to Nāraṇadēva, after having detenanted it ( kuļava kađidu ) from the previous tenants. This land, granted in memory of the hero, was to pass to the female descendant as gift ( henṇiṅge-dāna ) and to the male descendants by right of succession ( gandiṅge-mūla ). Nāraṇadēva, in turn, made a grant of 60 muđis of paddy for feeding and 12 muđis for hāludhāre (milk anointment) in the Hiriya-basti, to be performed in the name of his brother Emkapa-nāyaka.

cells.date: Śaka 13[4]5, Śōbhakṛit, Mārgaśira ba. 10, Vađđavāra=1422 A.D., December 8, Tuesday,
cells.object: Hero-stone standing near the Maṭhada-basti
cells.remarks: Damaged. When mahāpradhāna Virupaṇṇa-ođeya, governing from his capital at Bāraha-kanyāpura, was camping at Bayidūru with the ballālus (soldiers ?) of the hattukēri of Bāra-kūru, mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Saṅgirāya-vođeya of Hāđava!lì seems to have attacked him. The epigraph records the death of [Kōṭi]yaṇṇa-nāyaka. Mābaṇṇa-nāyaka and Bāṇki-nāyaka set up the hero-stone prepared by Yisarāchāri, son of Kēśava-āchāri and his son Māṇiyāchāri. Details are lost. It refers to the servant [ baṇṭa ] Nāraṇa-nāyaka of Chaturāvalì, Timmaṇa-nāyaka, probably the aliya of Bammaṇa-nāyaka and others.

cells.date: Śaka 1352 (expressed by the chronogram  akshi-śara-śikhi-indu ). Saumya, Śrāvaṇa śu. 1, Manadvāra=1429 A.D, July 2. Saturday.
cells.object: Stone standing at Hire-basti.
cells.remarks: This record in Kannada prose and verse contains a description of the Tułu country and Saṅgītapura therein. Saṅga-bhūpa, son of Bhairalarāṇi (of Vēṇupura ?) and Haiva of Nagire, had two sons Haiva and Maṅga. When Saṅga was ruling, his preceptor Māṇikasēna, discipline ( suta ) of Jayasēna desirous of observing sallēkhana , fasted for 33 days and died. The importance of sallēkhana is described in the record. Saṅga-bhūpa set up the nišidi stone after performing paṭṭaṇa-samudāya . Yisarāchāri, son of Kēśavāchāri made (engiaved) the stone.

cells.date: Śaka 1300, Durmukhi. Irregular. Śaka 1300 corresponds with the cyclic year Durmati = 1381-82 A.D. If Durmukhi it would be 1378-79 A.D.,
cells.object: Hero-stone near the Jaina basti.
cells.remarks: States that haṇapada Nāgaṇṇa-oĵeya who was governing Haiva, Koṅkaṇa and other provinces from Honnāvura led an expedition agaigst mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kēśavadēva-voĵeya of Nagire, when Jakaṇṇa-nāyaka, son of Vodisara-nāyaka and grandson of Bommaṇṇa-nāyaka fell in the battle (fought on behalf of Kēśavadēva). Bommaṇṇa-nāyaka's son (hero's father ?) set up the hero-stone. Kēśavadēva is described as siddha-siṅhāsanādhiśvara . On the date of the record Dēvarāya (I ?) was yet a prince. The king bears epithets like Rāya-rājaguru and vādi-pitāmaha .

cells.date: Bahudhānya, Pushya śu. 1, Thursday. The  tithi  = 1398 A.D., December 10, Tuesday. The Śaka year was 1320.
cells.object: Hero-stone near Jaina Basti.
cells.remarks: The king is described as rāya-rājaguru and rāya-vādi-pitāmaha . Maṅgappa-daṇṇāyaka, the mahāpradhāna having attacked the Tuĵu-kingdom camped at Bidire and overwhelmed it the Chauṭas and himself proceeding father, left behind an army led by mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Haivarasa-oĵeya. The Chauṭa having attacked them Tamma-nāyaka and his father rājaguru Jakkaṇṇa-nāyaka of Gāvaṇigara-baĵi attacked the enemy and in the fierce encounter lost their lives. Tamma-nāyaka, the uncle, and Bommaṇṇa-nāyaka, the younger brother of the hero Tamma-nāyaka set up the stone, Sri Panchamukhi says that he joined the Chauṭas. But it appears that he fought against the Chauṭas and on behalf of Maṅgappa. Cf. KN 882 below of the same date and from the same place.

cells.date: Śaka 1337, Manmatha, Jyēshṭa śu. 3, Sunday = 1415 A.D., May 26, if the  tithi  were ba. 3.
cells.object: Hero-stone standing near the Jaina-basti.
cells.remarks: When mahāpradhāna Saṅkharadēva-ođeya was camping with his Tułu army at Baṭakaĵa in an expedition (? rājakarya ), mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Saṅgirāya-ođeya, son of mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Haivarasa-ođeya encountered them with an army at Bhaṭṭakaĵa. cells.date: Šaka 1340, Hemaļambi, Phālguņa šu. 5, Sunday. The  tithi  corresponds regularly with 1417 A.D., February 21, Sunday of Šaka 1338, Durmukhi.
cells.object: Stone in the Parśvanātha-basti.
cells.remarks: Šańkara-kshitipāla, the king's minister was administering the Tuļu country in which Kaikiņi was situated. Pāyaņpārya, a devotee of Vidyānanda, described as traiyidya-chakrēšvara of Balātkāra-gaņa and Sarasvatī-gachchha, had a basadi of Pāršvanātha with gōpura , maņṭapa , prākāra etc. built at Kaikiņi for the worship of Pāršvanātha therein and made a gift of land of 30 hānes after purchase. It also registers gifts by others like Saņgirāya-arasa of Nagire, the seven jananis of Kāyikaņi and others. Kōṭiyaņņa-nāyaka of Sōde also made a gift of land purchased by Saņgirāya-arasa who stipulated that 12 muđes of paddy was to be given to each of the bastis at Kāyikaņņi, Širāli and Mańki.

cells.date: Šaka 1349, Plavamga, Dvitiya Vaiśākha śu. 5, Thursday=1427A.D., May 1.
cells.object: Hero-stone near Jaina-basti.
cells.remarks: Mahāpradhāna Timmaṇṇa-vođeya was governing Haiva, Tuļu and Koñkaṇa from the capital Honnāvura. Ummala-marakāla, the chief of the Hañjamāna merchants left Honnāvura and settled at Kāsarakōđu, with his followers due to his differences with the governor Kanara North Distric, Later, he sought the intervention of mahāmaṇdalēśvara Saṅgirāya-vođeya of Nagire to arbitrate. Saṅgiaya deputed his minister Saṅgava Kōtīśvara-nāyaka of Davutara-baļi, born at Kūruseyapura, and 1000 soliders to Kāsarakōđu. Timmaṇṇa-vođeya accompanied by the mūḥuchāvađi warriors of [Kem]guti Honnāvura treacherously attacked Kāsarakōđu and behaved roughly with the females of the Hañjāmāna. Kōtīśvara-nāyaka now opposed the king's forces and rescued the men and women including Ummara-marakāla, transported them through ferries to safe places and in the fight that followed fought bravely and died-Anṇu-nāyaka, younger brother of Kōtīēśvara, set up the stone made by Māniyāchāri, son of Rāmāchāri.

cells.date: Śaka 1353, Virōdhikrīt, Chaitra śu. 5, Wednesday=1431 A.D., March 29, Sunday. Regular for 1430 A.D., March 29, if the year was Śaka 1352, Sādhāraṇa.
cells.object: Hero-stone in the same place.
cells.remarks: When mahāmaṇdalēśvara Lakhaṇṇa-vođeya was governing Honnāvura-rājya, Bhairavadēva of Asakaļi disassociated himself from mahāmaṇdlēśvara Saṅgirāya-ođeya of Nagire and joined Saṅgirāya of Hāđuvaļļi. They together met the enemy along the boundaries of Kōṭa, near Kaikipi when Yaga aya ka, son of Bommaṇṇa-nāyaka of Haļivāni fell fighting on behalf of his master Bhairavadēva. Lakhaṇṇa then joined Saṅgirāya of Nagire in an effort to capture Hāđuvaļļi. In a battle fought Kasuva Isaraṇa-nāyaka, son of Bommaṇa-nāyaka fell fighting on behalf of Bhairavadēva. Kēśava-nāyaka and Māļu-nāyaka, brothers of the hero set up the stone. The first battle was fought within Nagire kingdom while in the second the offensive was taken by Lakhaṇṇa, as a revenge.

cells.date: Šaka 1394, Khāra, Āśvayuja śu. 5, Ma = 1471 A.D., September 19, Thursday. Šaka year was current.
cells.object: Hero-stone leying under a mango tree near Kaikiñi bridge.
cells.remarks: When mahāmaṇdalēśvara Bhairavadēva-vođeya of Nagire was governing Nagire and Honnāvura rājyas in conjunction with his younger brother Mallirāya-vođeya, serious differences between them led to quarrels and mahāmaṇdalēśvara Indaradēva-vođeya who was governing Hāđuvaļļi encountered the forces of Mallirāya-ođeya, Bemme-nāyaka, son of Desiga-nāyaka and aliya of Sivadēvati-nāyaka, born at Hēļumbe, a servant of Mallirāya-vođeya died in the battle. Kellake-nāyakiti, younger sister of Chelima-nāyaka, set up this stone, prepared by Baichāchāri, son of Kōti-vōja, of Mūđakkarisi in memory of her brother.

cells.date: Śaka 1404, La(Pla)va, Chaitra ba. 4, Monday=1481 A.D., March 19. The Śaka year was current.
cells.object: Hero-stone near the Jaina basti.
cells.remarks: When mahāmaṇdalēśvara Dēvarasa-vođeya, aļiya of Sāļuva Mallirājēndra was governing Nagire, Tuļu and Haive rājyas and Raṇagabha-nāyaka, son of Āju-nāyaka was administering Haive-rājya under his command, and gōpradhāna Kēsarikhān was governing Gōve at the instance (?) of the Sultān of Bedire (Bidar), Nizamuddin Mulk along with many ministers ( Vajilaru ) attacked Miđije from Gōve. Kallaṇṇa-nāyaka, Bhayiru-nāyaka and Tammaṇṇa-nāyaka, sons of Kallu-nāyaka of Sōde, having heard that their master Gabhi-nāyaka and Dēva-nāyaka had been captured, fell upon the muslim force ( turuka-daļa ) and died in the battle.

cells.date: Śaka 1404, Plava, Chaitra ba. 4; Monday=1481A.D., March 19.
cells.object: Hero-stone in the same place.
cells.remarks: Kanaada Damaged. Mahāmaṇdalēśvara Dēvarasa-vođeya of Nagari was governing Tuļu and Haive rājyas while under his orders Raṇagabhi-nāyaka, described as Ađakeyakuļya-puravarādhtśvara was administering Haive-rājya. A Mohammedan ormy ( turika-pāya-daļa ) led by Kēsarikhān appears to have attacked the Haive country through Gōve when Raṇagabhi-nāyaka and his younger brother Dēvu-nāyaka fell upon the enemy and after killing several, themselves got killed. Kathāri Sāļuva Mallirājēndra is mentioned in the record. Probably Dēvarasa-vođeya was his nephew ( aļiya ). See KN 896 below.

cells.date: Šaka 144[3], Vishu, Phálguṇa ba. 3=1522 A. D., February 13, Thursday.
cells.object: Hero-stone near Pāršvanātha-basti.
cells.remarks: Slightly damaged. When mahāmaṇđalešvara Immađi Dēvarāya-vođeya governing Nagire-Haive, Tuļu aud Koūkaṇarājyas, fell upon the army of the Portuguese(?) captain of Gōva ( Gōveya Paṇangada kapita ) at Māđagōve, several heroes died after piercing the horses and killing the enemies. Tammi-nāyaka was one of them and in his memory his brothers set up the hero stone which was engraved by Timmaya, son of Peṭala Timma-nāyaka, servant ( baṇṭa ) of Tammu-nāyaka of Gōvurakōṭiya Kaļuva. The brothers of the hero, Tammu-nāyaka, Timmanāyaka, Vira-nāyaka, and Dēvarasa-nāyaka are described as his senior mothers ( hiriyatāyi ) sons.

The brothers of the hero, Tammu-nāyaka, Timmanāyaka, Vira-nāyaka, and Dēvarasa-nāyaka are described as his senior mothers ( hiriyatāyi ) sons.

cells.date: Šaka 1465, Šubhakřit, Bhādrapada ba. 10, Monday = 1542 A.D., September 4. The Šaka year was current.
cells.object: Slab standing in Pāršvanātha-basti.
cells.remarks: It refers to mahāmaṇđalēsvara Křishṇadēvarasa-ođeya as the governor of Haiva, Tuļu and Koñkaṇa countries and records several gifts, by several persons. One of them is a grant of land by Nēmichandradēva of Balātkāra-gaṇa, after purchase, for the milk anointment ( hāla-dhāre ) of god Pāršvanātha of the basti of Kāyikaṇi while another is by his disciple Pārišva-dēva. A third of them is a renewal of a gift of land originally made by Immađi Dēvarāyaođeya the māvāji (uncle or, father-in-law ?) of Krīshṇadēvarasa for feeding, which had, however, lapsed as a result of foreign invasion. The sēnabōva of Kođakaṇi was enquired of the same with reference to village documents in his custody and the grant was renewed after excluding the grants of land made by Nēmichandradēva and his discipline. It also registers gifts by Gommaṭadēvi-nāyatī, daughter of Kōṭi and Yisaraka-nāyakiti. daughter of Sātuseṭti of Tolahara-baļi, besides several others. The record gives details of transactions concerning these gifts, and also refers to silver hons ( beļļiyas homnu ), chi.ga ( chikka gadyāna ?) measures like side , hađāļu (?) etc.

cells.date: Śaka 1470, Plavamga, Jyēshṭha śu. 10 = 1547 A.D., May 29, the Śaka year being current.
cells.object: Slab in  homnehakkalu .
cells.remarks: Refers to Sāļuva Krīshṇadēvarāya-vođeya as governing Nagire, Haive, Tuļu and Końkaṇa from his capital at Gerasoppe. Maļu-nāyaka, son of Mallarasa-nāyaka and Saṇṇakka, got a new chaityālaya built at Māvaļļi of Kāyakaṇi in the site purchased from Sambudēva-nāyaka and others, grandsons of Sirugu-heggađe of Siriyana-baļi of Māvaļi, installed the image of Pushpadanta-tirthańkara and made a gift of lands for daily worship and occasional special services accompanied by musical instruments like đoļu , jēghaṭe and šańkha . It further records grants by others like Haivaṇa-nāyaka, Saṅgirāya-nāyaka, son of Pārśvadēva-nāyaka etc. mainly for hālu-dhāre . Saṇṇakka, mother of the chief donor and her four brothers (named) were all born to Mallidēvi of Nagire and her husband Saṅga-bāṇasiga of the Siriyana-baļi of Kāyakaṇi.

cells.location: Mūđa Bhaṭkaļ · Bhatkal Taluk · Kanara North
cells.date: Šaka 1449, Sarvajit, Mārgašira šu. 15, Saturday, lunar eclipse=1527 A. D., December 7.
cells.remarks: Broken stone standing in the Śankaranārāyaṇa temple. Gururāya-vođeya, son of Sañgirāya-vodeya was governing Baṭakaĵa and other rājyas from his capital at Samgitapura. Kalpa-joyisa, son of Siriyaṇa-jōyisa of Vaśishṭha-gōtra had caused an Ľśvara temple and a maṭha attached to it, to be built at Baṭakaĵa and made grants of land for feeding therein. This grant is renewed by Dēvappa-jōyisa of that family after getting it detenanted ( kuĵava-kađidu ) by mahāmaṇdalēśvara Gururāya-vođeya. It further renews gifts of one mūđe of paddy made earlier by Yindarasa-vođeya to Kallapa-jōyisa, and also of money income. The gift lands were inclusive of the water ( nirū-dari-canal ), house site, amgōđu , dry land, trees, fruits beṇa , bi ļrru etc.

cells.object: Slab standing in Ambālkaṭti.
cells.remarks: This is a composite record put on stone after the first date noted(1550 A. D.) Mahamāṇda-lēśvara Chennādēvi-amma made a gift of land at Mūđa Baṭtakaĵa, after detenanrting it for the service of paṇchāmrita to the Chauvisa-tīrthamkara basti built by her grandmother ( ajjiyamma ) Virādēvi, wife of mahāmaṇdalēśvara Gururāya-vođeya. The indra (priest) of the basti was to receive the gēṇi (annual rent) of 60 muđes of paddy and maintain the gift. Three earlier grants also are recorded. On the second date a gift of land was made after purchase for 850 varahas from Dēvappa-jōgi and Sāṇṇadēvappa and their parents Indaga-ṇa-adhikāri and Nāgarisi, by Virādēvi-amma, queen of Gururāya-vođeya, son of Sañgirāya administering Baṭtakaĵa and other regions from sañgitapura. The gift was made for celebrating several festivals like jtvadayāshtami , Śrutapaṇchiṭmi , śrāvaṇa , śōđasśa-bhāvane-puje and hāladhare . On the last date mentioned, which in fact, is the earliest date-1511 A. D.,-Mađi-šeṭti, younger brother of Kāsiyaṇa-seṭti made over some lands to Queen Virādēva-mma. But the record here is damaged and details are lost. Chennādēvi-amma, queen (daughter-in-law (neice ?) of Dēvarasa-vođeya made another grant of land on the 3rd date to her grandmother Vidārēvi who appears to have made it over to the basti . The later pare of the record is damaged.

cells.object: Stone in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Mahĉpradhāna Ācharasa-vođeya who was governing. the Tuļu country from Bārakūru, made a grant of 12 hons to Purushōttama-bhaṭta. son of Vāmana-upādhyāya of Muṇđavalli in Baṭakaĵa, for reciting Dēvimahālnyā during the four months of chāturmāsya in the temple of Durgā, every year for the merit of the king. text.remarks: This badly damaged record gives a genealogical account of the Vijayanagara kings, in the course of which Bukkarāya, Harihara, Vijaya-bhūpati and Dēvarāya are mentioned. cells.date: 1. Šaka 1503, Vikrama, Māgha. šu. 5, Monday=1581  A.D..  January 9. The Šaka year was current; 2. Šaka 1510, Sarvajit, Chaitra šu. 1=1587  A.D.. , February 28, Tuesday, the Šaka year being current; 3. Šaka 1515, Nandana, Prathama Āshāđha šu. 10, Friday=1592  A.D.. , June 9. The Šaka year was current.
cells.remarks: Slabs leaning against the wall in the Ratnatraya basadi . Records the construction, by Raṅgapparā jođeya, of the Ratnatraya-basadi, of the maṇđapa munivāsa , chandrašāla , etc. and the installation of the images of Nēmiśvara, Pārśvanātha, and Vardhamāna by his son Ghaṇṭēndra on the advice of Bhaṭṭākalam ankaŭ on the date cited first and records also the grants of 443 varahas , 1 haṇa and 3 visa derived from the incomes from nine villages and lands yielding 300 khaṇđuga of paddy and several other gifts, made for the worship and maintenance, by the latter, on the dates cited first and second. It is further stated in a postscript that on the date cited third. Rāmādēvi, the queen of Ghaṇṭēndra constructed a gandhakuṭi-basti for Šāntiśvara and granted lands to provide for worship and Ghaṇṭēndra granted the siddhāya income from Koppala near Haļeya-Biļigi, for the milk-bath of Nēmiśvara. Cf. PRKRI., 1939-40, No. 88.

cells.location: Hāru Maskēri · Kumta Taluk · Kanara North
cells.object: Slab in a field near the house of Ananta Gaṅgādhara Hegđe.
cells.remarks: Summaries , 1946-47, No. 7; KI., VI, No. 63 It refers to a chief of Sōde whose name cannot be made out. But he is described as a pādapadmōpajivi . It registers a gift of land, after purchase, by Bommaṇa-seṭṭi, son of Madi-seṭṭi to god Mahābaladēva of Gōkaṇa. The gift land was given on lease to Kāmana-seṭṭi, son of Vajra-seṭṭi, the seṭṭikāra of Sayiganaha!li free of several taxes. The lease-holder was to make over a specified amount of paddy and money to the temple in the month of Mārgaśira every year. Other details are lost.

cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land by Arasādēvi and the son (not named) of Immađi Arasappa-vođeya of Kaušika-gōtra and Āpastamba-sūtra, the mahāprabhu of Sōde, for the temhle of Narasimhadēva at Banavase, at the instance of Raṅgapparājayya, son of mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rāmarājayya. The gift land was situated in Varadākopa, renamed Narasimhapura, an agrahāra on the bank of the Varadā in Jeđe-sīme.

cells.remarks: While Basavaṇṇa-vođeya was governing Bārakūru-rājya under orders of the king, Mādaṇṇa-seťi, the seťikāṭa of Basurūru, son of Tammaṇṇa-toľadhāri of Bārakūru made a gift of land, house, well, house-site, tippe , makki , mekke , bayalu , kaļe , mekki , mara , nekki etc. with all rights, to Singaṇayya, son of Chakravarti-upādhyāya, the vidvān of the Śrīmaṭha of Simgēri under the stipulation that the donee should present 9 mūđes of rice annually at the rate of 1 hāne measured in nāđa-hāne for the daily offerings to god Nandikēšvara in front of the temple of Nakharēšvara at Basurūru and pay one hon annually to god Uļļūradēva. cells.date: Śaka 1356, Pramādi. Kārttika=1433A.D., October-November. The fortnight is not mentioned.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1929, No. 414; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 444
cells.remarks: Another slab in the same prākāra . When mahāpradhāna Chandarasa-vođeya was governing Bārakūra-rājya, Ēsara-setīti of Gōļara-baļi, son of Bālū-setīti, the setītikāra of Kakkeye-baļi of Pađuvakēri in Basarūru made a grant of land called keṇchanake re , to god Nakharēśvaradēva for a perpetual lamp and feeding one Brāhmaṇa daily and 2 Brāhmaṇas on occasions like dvādaśī , pradōsha and amāvāsye . It also refers to arrangements made for the livelihood of Dēvakka of the family of Mañju-sāvanta, Kōtīyakka of the family of Dēsinga-setīti, and the children of Yisarālūva of the family of Beṇmaṇṇālūva. In this connection it refers to the grant of a house as kanyādāna to the bride Dēvakka, It stipulates that rice must be supplied as laid down without offering explanations as bānagēđu and baṅagēđu (lack of rain or famine).

cells.date: Śaka 1363, Durmati, Phālguṇa śu. 10, Tuesday = 1442 A.D., February 20
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1928, No. 407; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 448
cells.object: Slab in the outer  prākāra  of Mahālingēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Mahāpradhāna Chandarasa-vođeya is stated to be governing Bārakūru-rājya. Registers a gift of land and cocoanut garden to god Mahādēva at Pađuvakēri of Basarūru for offerings during rudrapūje , raṅgapūje etc. on the eve of divaļige , etc., by Koļiyama-setļi, aliya (son-in-law ?) of Saniyama-setļi of Moratañke. The gēnīkāras , i.e. the lease holders of the land were to supply to the god the stipulated amount of rice and one hāne of ghee without fail, or else, they were to vacate the lease. The gift was to be protected by the several setļikāḥas of Pađuvakēri and the donor and after him, his son-in-law and others. Šañkarasa wrote the record, for which halaru setļikāḥas and goddess (?)Sahādēvi were the signatories.

cells.date: Śaka 1366, Raktākshi, Āshāđha śu. 10, Thursday = 1444 A.D., June 25
cells.remarks: ARSIE ., 1928, No. 417; SII., IX, pt. I, No. 449 Another slab in the same place. Timmaṇṇa-vođeya was ruling Bārakūru-rājya, when several setļikāḥas of Pađuvakēri in Basarūru sold 18 muđes of land and a house etc. to Nāraṇa-seţi of Kuđeyara-baļi, son of Šańkara-seţi of Anyamṭara-baļi who made a gift of the same for offerings and other services to god Mahādēva in the Nakharēśvara temple. Part of the land was given to ađigaļ (priest) who performed šantidēvapūje, rudrapūje etc. The seţiķikāras deducted taxes and 4 ga of jita from the sale-price of the land, and it was stipulated that they would discharge claims upon the land from outsiders. The gift consisted of 27 muđis and 2 kāti ga hons and 20 muđis of paddy for rudrapūje . Brahmas of Tomhattina hultarike also figure as signatories.

cells.date: Šaka 1366, Raktākshi, Pushya šu. 5. Monday = 1444 A.D., December 14.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1928, No. 404; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 450
cells.remarks: Yet another slab in the same place. Timmanṇa-ođeya was governing Bārakūru-rājya. The record states that the nakharas of Dharmapatṭaṇa agreed to pay to the temple of Mahādēva a portion of toll income raised in the village (at the rate of 1 hon towards every 10 kāti ga that was to be paid to the patree) and use it for replacing the copper covering of the pinnacle ( chambina ođilu ) with gold ( henna-kalaśa ) and to use the balance amount, if any, for the service of the god and no other purpose. The gift was made to expatiate the tin committed by them in having mundered two men (Tiruma-hađavaļa of Anyamṭara-baļi, son of Honneya-hađavaļa and Bemma-seţi of Atimuddana-baļi, son of Māde-seţi) of their community. The grant was made under instructions from the seţiķikāras of Pađuvakēri. God Mahādēva of the Nakharēśvara (temple), the nakharas of Dharmapatṭaṇa, seţiķikāra of Pađuvakēri figure as signatories.

cells.date: Šaka 13[7]3, Pramōda, Vaišākha šu. 13, Friday = 1450 A.D., April 24.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1928, No. 429; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 452
cells.object: Slab lying in a house site south of Dođdakerekaṭte.
cells.remarks: While Lingappa-vođeya was governing Bārakūru-rājya a gift of land and money was made for the worship of the gods and feeding Brāhmaṇas in the maṭha at Pađuvakēri by Kōṭiyaka kitti belonging to Upinakuļeyara-baļi of Namduhaļi and her son Meravaṇpa-seṭti. It refers to the loan of 200 kāṭi gadyāṇas borrowed by the seṭṭikāras of Pađuvakēri from her in the summer month ( bēsageya ti mgāļu ) of the year Āngirasa upon which they were to pay 13 muđes of rice as annual interest, at the current rates at Bārakūru ( Bārakūrā parivarttanake saluva ), which also she donated. Nāraṇa of Hosamane was to supply 10 muđes of rice from all the lands he cultivated. Likewise, one kāṭi ga was to be paid towards perpetual lamp in the month of Kārttika from out of the yield of garden and one muđe of rice and one muđe of mungo ( uddu-a pulse ) on amāvāsya (new moonday) and dvādaši (12th day of the fortnight) days for cakes ( dose ), from out of the yield of land called akaļiya-bāļu .

cells.date: Šaka 1377, Bhāva, Māgha šu. 5=1455 A. D., January 23, Thursday.
cells.object: On another slab in the same  prākāra .
cells.remarks: ARS1E., 1928, No. 405; SII, IX, pt. II, No. 457 Records that when mahāpradhāna Pamđaridēva was ruling over Bārakūra-rājya, an agreement was effected between the šeṭṭikāra of the two streets Pađuvakēri and Mūđakēri in Basarūru regarding the boundary and the rights of their respective localities and the paths through which the seṭṭis of each locality had to take sheep and arecanut trees to the temple. of Dēvi on festival occasions. The interest of the inscription lies in the amicable settlement made by the people themselves to avoid bloody religious feuds. The dispute was placed by both the parties, in the presence of god Vishṇumūrti, of Chiruligumḍa before the pontiffs ( ayya ) of the four maṭhas of Basuṣūru and the villagers of Kandāūra. The original endowments of the temples of Nagareśvara, Tuṭuvēśvara, the Dēvi and the basti were enquired in to by both the parties whereupon the varttane of the temple land ( dēvasva ) of Kuṇḍaṇeśvara was made over to god Tuṭuvēśvara and some other rearrangements also were made. This record was wrttten by Aṇṇappa-sēnabōva.

cells.reference: ARSIE.,  1928, No. 406; SII., IX. pt. II, No. 459
cells.object: Slab set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: Records that Pamḍaridēva-oḍeya ruling the Bārakūru-Tuṭu-rājyas under orders from mahā-pradhāna Rāmachandra-daṇāyaka-oḍeya, made a gift of 150 kāṭi-gadyāṇa honnu , for amṛi-lapaṭli , offering curd-rice and burning perpetual lamp to god Mahādēva at Paḍuvakēri on the occasion of lunar eclipse. It is stated that the haṇijamāna (merchant community) was not in a position to pay the income from haṭlike to the palace and hence made over the paṭi-mariyāde (levy collected on weekly fairs etc. ?) to the palace and this amount was to be now collected from customs levied upon merchandise by the local accountant ( taṭada sēnabōva ) from the weekly fairs.

cells.remarks: Records that while Viṭṭharasa was ruling over Bārakūra-rājya, Duggaṇa-seṭṭi of Ballā-baṭi, son of Śavaṇṇa-sēnabōva of Paḍuvakēri at Basurūru and his three nephews Sōvaṇa-seṭṭi, son of Akka-seṭṭiti, Nāgaṇa-seṭṭi, son of Bāliyakka-seṭṭiti, and Dēṭ-seṭṭi, son of Sāvakka-seṭṭiti, agreeing among themselves, made a grant of lands, garden and house to Siriyappa, son of Tirumalenātha-seṭṭi of Javarupāli, who had been to Vāraṇāsi on a pilgrimage and had brought with him the image of god Viśvanātha. The gift was made on the occasion of a solar eclipse, for worship and offerings to the deity. It was stipulated that the gift lands were not to be sold or alienated. And that in case of any difficulty the donee would report it to the setṭikāṭas of Paṭuvakēri through the donors and that they would arrange for the management of the gifts. The record was written by Saṭkara-senabōva, the sēnābōva of the setṭikāṭas of Paṭuvakeri, son of Vishṇurāvāṭi.
