cells.date: Śaka 1403 (expired), 1404 (current), Pramōdūta, Vaiśākha śu. 1. Irregular. The Śaka year corresponds to the cyclic year Śubhakṛit in which year the details given will be equivalent to 1482 A.D., April 19, Friday.
cells.reference: ARSIE.,  1928, No. 421; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 471
cells.object: On a slab in the  prākāra  of Veñkaṭaramaṇa temple.
cells.remarks: When Mallappa-nāyaka, younger brother of Sōmaṇṇa-nāyaka of Kuṛugōđu was governing Bārakūra-rājya, the halaru and seṭṭikāṣas of Pađuvakēri of Basarūru and several other individuals made gifts of land and money for the services of god Tirumaladēva at Pađuvakēri. Uđupa-bhaṭṭa and Kommeya-bhaṭṭa appear to have taken a loan of 82 dođđa varaha ga from Timmayya and developed clay land ( kaļi ) and later sought to own the land where-upon Timmayya laid down certain aconditions according to which they were to pay certain specified sums which was also gifted to god Tirumaladēva. This is one of some such transactions pertaining of gifts recorded in the epigraph.

cells.date: Śaka 1428, Prabhava, Kārttika śu. 15, Saturday=1506 A.D., October 31. The cyclic year would be Kshaya.
cells.reference: ARSIE.,  1928, No. 423; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 476
cells.object: On a slab set up in the  prākāra  of the Veṭkaṭaramaṇa temple.
cells.remarks: Records that Basavarasa-vođeya made a grant of money to god Tirumaladēva of Bāđākeṛe in Kandāūra which belonged to the bhaṇđāra-sthaḥa of the palace for burning a perpetual lamp, offering curd rice and for daily expenses, from out of the interest of the sum. The grant was made for the p'osperity ( śatru-kshaya mitrōrjjia ) of the king. The record was written by Mallarasa, the karaṇika . It records a sub-grant of 25 gadyāṇas being the rental on tenure of a garden, by some seṭṭis , for the services of the same god. Another grant of 2 gadyāṇas of income from gēṇi for burning a perpetual lamp on the divaḥige festival, a fourth grant, by the halaru of Bāđākeṛe, of 7 gadyāṇas fearned as interest from the Brāhmaṇas of the place on a certain sum outstanding on them as a loan( Brāhmara mēle maisālada baḥdi ) for the same god are also recorded. It also states that the seṭṭikāṣas of Pađuvakēri confirmed the management of the temple, dēvālya-sthānada Sōmana dharma-pārupatyā )upon Nalḥla-chakravarti Ananta-ayya.

cells.reference: ARSIE., 1928, No. 410; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 479
cells.object: On a slab in the outer  prākāra  of the Mahalingēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records that Mallapa-nāyaka, brother of Sōvaṇṇa-nāyaka of Kurugōđu ruling the Bārakūru-rājya, collected as contribution ( kāṇike ) from the merchants ( seṭṭikāras ) of Pađuvakēri in Basarūru and made a grant of the village Pađuva Belatūru in Hāṣa-nāđu and Mūđa Belatūru (after purchase from the collected amount ?) for offerings and other services (like paṭchamṇita ) of god Mahādēva. An appendix added later states that on Tuesday, Chaitra ba. 8, of the year Īśvara(=1517 A.D., April 13, Monday), Saṭkamma-mudaliti, daughter of the grand-daughter of Aṇṇu-bhaṇđāri Bemmaṇa-bhaṇđāri belonging to Toḥahara-baḥi of Koṅga-baḥi made a gift of 60 dolđa varahas for copper work ( chembina-kelasa ) from the interest of 4.5 varaha gas on the hon current at Belatūru, an yearly grant of a fixed quantity of rice was made for offering curd rice to god Mahādēva. This record was written by Mallarasa, son of Nāyappa, the karaṇika of Bārakūru, with the approval of the sāmastas of Hāṣu-nāđu and the Jamnis of Belatūru.

cells.object: Slab in a private building site to the north of Dođđakerekaţte.
cells.remarks: Records that while Vijayappa-vođeya, son of Ratnappa-vođeya, was ruling over Bārakūra-rājya which had been bestowed upon his father by the king, Tirumaka-seţtiti of Seţiya-baļi, wife of Kōchi-seţti Nāraņa-seţti and daughter of Joki-seţti, the seţikāya of Pađuvakēri of Basarūru, caused the construction of a maṭha in Pađuvakēri of Basarūru and endowed it with lands and gold. The record gives details about the lands, house etc. she took over, belonging to Vāsudeva-mūđakare, son of Gōvinda-mūđakare on tenancy described as biđā-ruvāra and gave it on ađha-āruvāra (i.e. half of the āruvāra tenancy ?) for a fixed sum. Similarly, the record refers to other lands also and refers to amtarāruvāra (type of tenancy?) and to coins like dođđa-varaha , kumđige-varaha (?) and other payments.

cells.object: On a slab in the outer  prakāra  of the Mahaliṅgēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Aļīya Timaņna-ođeya, of Araga, was ruling over Bárakūra-rājya under the orders of the king. Samķara-setļi, son of Sōvaņņa-setļi built a maļha within the temple of Nakharēšvara Mahálinga of Pađuvakčri in Basarūru. Mallappa-setļi, son of Samķara-setļi's eldest wife granted some lands, probably after purchase. Vāmana Nārāyaņa-bhaťta of Avaļatti wrote this record, witnessed by several individuals (named). Eļavura Aņnu-setļi (?) the patrakāra (?) was responsible for this transaction. Samķama-nāyakiti and Dēku-ađeyati (the two other wives) also granted lands from out of the lands(?) that came to their share after entering into a tenancy ( aņtarāruvāra ) with the sons of Talāka-hegađiti. Madhyasta Nārāyaņa-bhaťta wrote this record. It mentions Rāma-sēnabōva as the representative of the vođeya (pontiff ?) of Simģēri. Dēku-setļiti made a grant of money from out of the tenure amount. This part of the record was written by madhyasta Šridhara-bhaťta. It further records a grant of lands by Mallappa-setļi for the offerings of god Mahálinga. Several hebāras figure as witnesses.

cells.date: Khara, Márgašira šu. 1, Thursday. Probably = 1531 A.D., November 9, Thursday.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1928, No. 424-A; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 540
cells.object: On a slab on the building site north of Dođđakeřekaťte.
cells.remarks: Lajjeya Sadānamda-setļi and Dēvu-setļi made gifts of land and money for the service(offerings, supply of flower, oil for bath, etc.) of the goddess Durgādēvi, consecrated by the former near the temple of god Mahādēva and also for the service of god Mahādēva. The gift was made for feeding Bráhmaņas and muttaides ( sumaņgali ) who were also provided with sarces and cloth ( hachađa ), and for the worship of the goddess Durgādēvi during the nevarātri festival. For this purpose lands were purchased and leased out on tenancy also, the details of which are given.

cells.date: Saka 1457, Vijaya, Āshāḍha śu. 11=1533 A.D. July 2, Wednesday, the Śaka year being 1455
cells.reference: ARSIE , 1928, No. 422; SII., IX. pt. II, No. 555
cells.object: On a slab in the  prakāra  of the Veńkaṭaramaṇa temple
cells.remarks: The king appointed Sumkaṇṇa-nāyaka as governor of Bārakūra-rājya and at the latter's instance Koṇḍa-vođeya was ruling over the province. Sumkaṇṇa-nāyaka made a gift of the village Haṭiya Kuduru in Bhaṇḍāra-sthaḥa for offerings and perpetual lamp of god Tirumaladēva of Pađuvakēri of Basarūru for the prosperity of the king. Koṇḍa-vođeya was ordered to get a document ( paṭe ) in this regard. The income from the gift village is stated to be 23 varahas and 6 haṇas which appears to have been equivalent to 59 kāṭis .

cells.date: Śaka 1468, Parābhava, Kārttika śu 1=1546 A.D., October 25, Monday
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1927, No. 394; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 620
cells.object: On a slab in a house-site to the south of Halavanakere.
cells.remarks: When Achchappa-vođeya was ruling over Bārakūra-rājya under the orders of the king, Sa-ńkaraliṅga-seṭṭi of Atimarana-baḥi built a charity-house ( maṭha? ) and granted certain lands after purchase, and a tank for the worship of god Viṭhaladēva and when, in course of time the charity-house had fallen down, Kuppaṇa-seṭṭi Sūri-seṭṭi of Udare got it renovated and endowed it with more lands and money. It registers other grants made by some others for properly conducting the same charity. Further grant of land by Sūri-seṭṭi of Udare for the conduct of festivals like raṅgapūjé on the eve of sikharada-humṇave , in the month of Kārttika and during śtvarātri in the temple of god Tirumala.

cells.date: Šaka 1471, Kilaka, Kārttika šu. 1=1548 A.D., October 2, Tuesday, the Šaka year being current.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1926, No. 432; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 632
cells.object: On a slab in a private house south of the tank Sannakerekaṭte.
cells.remarks: Records that Bemmacha-setīti of Ārusantaya-baļi renovated the maṭha built by Kallu-setīti of Haṭakaļab-aļi, and endowed it with some plots of land and money income on loans (at the rate of 5 varaha ga upon 50 varaha ga as recorded). cells.date: Šaka 1476, Ānanda, Kārttika šu. 1=1554 A.D., October 27, Saturday
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1928, No. 433; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 655
cells.object: On a slab set up on the road side to the west of the same tank.
cells.remarks: When Mallappa-vođeya was administering Bārakūru-rājya, under the orders of Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka (of Keļadi) who had been appointed governor of the Tuļu-rājya by the king, Timmayya-setīti, nephew ( aļiya ) of Hosabu-setīti of Toļahara-baļi, purchased a plot of land from the setītikāras of Paṭuvakūri, constructed a maṭha thereon and having acquired land on lease ( bidāru-vāra ) from Aṇṇa-uṭupa, the grāmiṇi of Kamdāvara a brahmādēya land, made a gift of the same for the maintenance of the chhatra attached to the maṭha . cells.date: Prajōtpatti = 1571-72A.D., [?)]
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1928, No. 409; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 683
cells.object: On a slab in the outer enclosure of Mahālingēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka and Bārākūru-rājya and records that Timmaṇna-setṭi, nephew of Tiruma-hegađe, belonging to Tombhatina Kavađicha-baļi and his elderbrother Chemmaṇa-heggađe lent 350 varahas to the residents of Ānegaļi village, the interest of 35 dođđa varaha ga per annum upon which they gifted for the worship and offerings to the god for 14 days from Kārttika šu. 1 to šu. 14 every year, commencing from the year Ksa ya. It is stated that 30 varahas of interest amount upon 300 varahas lent by Chammaṇṇa-hegađe, was to be used for rangapū je, paṇchāmrita (anointment), Sahasranāma (worship by reciting the 1000 names of god) and burning lamp and the balance of 5 varahas upon 50 varahas lent by Timmaṇṇa-seṭṭi was for offering rice of one hāne daily. It was stipulated that in case the interest amount was not duly received from Ānegaļi village the seṭṭigāras were to conduct the same by advancing (? pare ) the sum. Thimmaṇa-seṭṭi donated a copper drum ( bhēri ). The record was written by Nāgayya-sēnabōva, son of Hari-sēnabōva.

cells.date: Śaka 1347 (expired), 1348 (current) Viśvāvasu, Chaitra śu .. Tuesday = 1425 A.D., March 27, the  tithi  being śu. 8. But Śaka year would be 1437 itself.
cells.reference: ARISE., 1925, No. 365; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 441
cells.object: Slab in the  prākāra  of Kundēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. States that formerly Dēvaṇṇa-sēnābōva of Kuđākūru had, under the leadership ( addika ) of the vūru-jagattu made a grant of land in the presence of god Kundēśvara of Kuṇdāpura, which had, however, lapsed. Now Narasimhadēva-vođeya who was governing Bārakūru-rājya at the command of the king and Hariyappa-daṇṇāyaka-vođeya, having enquired the grāma, jagattu and mukkālaṭṭi of Kuṇdāpura who had assembled at his instance, measuring the purōhita-sthaļa restored the grant, without diminishing the fixed revenue ( siddhāya ) to the palace. The lower portion of the slab is built in and the details lost.

cells.date: Šaka 1311; Vibhava (wrong for (Šukla), Kārtṭika śu. 5 Sunday=1389 A.D., October 24)
cells.remarks: Slabs kept in the Chandranāthasvāmi basadi . Mentions Iruggappa-daṇṇāyaka, son of mahāpradhāna Baichappa-daṇṇāyaka as ruling over Bārakūru-rājya. Records that, at the instance of Ubhayāchārya, he restored the record which was stated to have been destroyed by fire some time in the past by getting it engraved in a concise form, on small stones, to be preserved in the central shrine. The grant which is said to have been made by Jinadattarāya, gives a detailed account of the benefactions of lands assigned for various services to the deity Chandranāthasvāmi of the basadi at Hatṭiyaṅgaḍi. On the date of this record Bukka II was still a prince and Harihara II was ruling.

cells.date: Šaka 1438, Year 9, Dhātu, Mārgaśira šu. 15. Probably=1514 A.D., December 9, Tuesday. The regnal year can only be 6, not 9.
cells.object: Slab in a field called  kallu tođame .
cells.remarks: Srates that when Vijayappa-ođeya, son of Ratnappa-ođeya, was governing Bārakūru-rajya, a grant of twenty varaha-gadyāṇas , equivalent to 60 kāṭi-gadyāṇas , was made by him, towards the amjītupađi service and burning of a perpetual lamp for the deity Chandranāthasvāmi, for the welfare of the king. The amount was to be realised from the siddhāya tax from Kambhadakōne, a hamlet of Keragāla, a village belonging'to the palace treasury.

cells.date: Šaka 1280, Viļambi, Šrāvaņa šu. 1, Saturday =1358 A.D., July 7, f.d.t. .07
cells.remarks: Two sides of a slab in front of the Hakre-maṭha. This damaged and worn out inscription states that when mahāpradhāna Maļeya-daṇnāyaka was ruling over Bārakūru-rājya, Vissaṇṇa, son of Viraṇṇa, made a gift of land called āneyabāļu after purchase at the then prevailing rates, to god Kirumandilēšvara, for the welfare of the king. It stipulates the feeding of 14 Bīāḥmaṇas and the burning of some lamps out of the income from the land granted.

cells.date: Šaka 1404, Plava, Māgha šu. 15, Sunday. If the  tithi  were ba. 15, the details correspond to 1482 A.D., February 3. The Šaka year was current.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1928, No. 403, SII., IX, pt. II, No. 470
cells.object: On three pieces of a slab lying in the choultry attached to the Mūkāmbikā temple.
cells.remarks: Commences with an invocatory verse of goddess Durgā. Records a gift of land made by Baṁmacha-sāvanta Baṁkiarass and Honnakambaļi for offerings to the goddess Mūkāmbika at Kollūru, while Pamđaridēva was governing Bārakūra-rāya under the orders of mahā-pradhāna Siṁgaṇa-daṇnāyaka. Siṁga-ođeya, the sthānakarta of the temple is praisde for his ascetic qualities. It refers to grants made for śribali thrice a day to the goddess [ mēlu-śāntī kīļu-śānti bali ) and the three priests ( aļigaļu ) including the Brāhmaṇa that carries the (imageĵof) the god. The beneficiaries include the temple instrumentalists ( vādya, maddaļe, haļage ).

cells.date: Śaka 1295, Paridhāvin, Kārttika śu. 5, Thursday.  Tithi  = 1372 A.D., November 1, Monday, the Śaka year being current. But in the next year Pramādin, the details correspond to 1373 A.D., October 20, Thursday, f.d.t. .55
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1927, No. 375; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 415
cells.remarks: Another slab set up in the same place. While mahāpradhāna Gōparasa-voĵeya was ruling Bārakūru-rājya, Gaṇakumāra-heggađe the mahanta (Viraśaiva piest) of Tāyi-sthaļa of Bārakūru purchased land yielding 12 muđe of rice, as also a house, well and house-site, for 100 gadyāṇas and made it over to Divākara-daniya for feeding two (ubhaya) jaṅgamas in the temple of Kōṭiśvara during the festival called kaṭiya-habba , annually. The record was written by sēnabōva Paramēśvara. A supplement adds that in case of shortage ( koṭate ) 8 hāne of rice out of 40 hānes of Koṭhthāriguđi may be used.

cells.reference: ARSIE., 1927, No. 377; SII, IX, pt. II, No. 451
cells.remarks: Fourth slab in the same place. cells.date: Šaka 1469, Parābhava, Kārttika šu. 15 = 1546 A.D., November 7, Sunday, the Šaka year being current.
cells.object: On a slab to the west of the  vōlaga-maṇdapa  in the same temple.
cells.remarks: ARSIE. 1927, No. 373; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 621 Records that Veňkaṭadri-rāja-mahārāya-arasu, governor of Bārakūra-rājya, placed Achchappa-vođeya in charge of that province. This latter made a grant of 50 varahas for the services of Koṭēvaradēva in the month of Kārttika ( puñchāṇrita, dipā-ādhane, naivēdya, phalep 'je, vītydīvanapūje ). The grant was made for the prosperity and long life of the king and for the merit of Rāmarāja Veňkaṭadri-rāja-mahā-arasu. This record was written by Timmarasa, the karanika of Bārakūru. It records another grant by Ekabaļakhāna-vođeya, ruling over the Bārakūra-rājya under the orders of Veňkaṭadri-rāja, who made a gift of 35 varahas for performing the rite of putification of the Kōṭēvara temple. The gift was made for the well-being of Veňkaṭadri-rāja. The putification was needed to remove the pollution caused by the death of Brāhmaṇas and Šūdras and the killing of cows in a religious feud on the occasion of tuđiya-habba , on account of which the door of the temple had been closed and the worship of the god discontinued for about 6 months.

cells.date: Śaka 1484, Dundubhi, Chaitra śu. 10 = 1562 A.D., March 15, Sunday
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1927, No. 385; SII., IX, pt. II, No. 673
cells.object: On a slab on the right side of the entrance into the Kōṭēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: When Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka was governing the Tuṛu-rājya under the king's orders and Kalleya Yellapa-ođeya was ruling over Bārakūru under the latter's command, Chitu-seṭṭi of Holeya-bali, son of Gaṇapa-seṭṭi of Pađuvakēri in Basarūru, caused the construction of a maṭha and granted land for the service of god Umāmahēśvara in the maṭha , for feeding 6 persons daily in the feeding house ( nityachchatra ) and for the service ( rudrābhiśeka , śiva-rātri , raṁgapūje etc.) of god Kōṭēśvara, in whose presence the gift was made. Lands were purchased for this purpose from several individuals.

cells.remarks: Kaleya Elapa-vođeya, who was ruling over the province of Bārakūru under the orders of Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka of Keļadi who had been appointed governor of the Tułu-rājya by Rāmarāja Veňkatādrirāja-mahā-arasu, remitted the tax on those plots of land which Mahābalalinga-sēnabōva of Chōļiyakeri granted to the choultry ( chhatra ) in the maṭha attached to the temples of Umāmahēśvara and Lakshminārāyaṇa in Kumbhāśi, built by him. The halaru also made gift of lands, which were also exempted from taxes, for the service of amriapađi and nandādtpa .

cells.date: Śaka 1485, Dundubhi, Jyēshtha śu. [7], Ādivāra = 1562 A.D., May 10, Sunday. The Śaka year was current.

cells.object: On another slab in the same place.
cells.remarks: The king granted as amara-māgaṇi to Yeđavamurāri, Kōṭekolāhala, Pađuvaṇa-samudrādhi ś-vara Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka of Keļadi, son of Chauđa-gauṇđa of Keļadi, the districts of Āraga, Gutti, 36 kampaṇas , Tuļu-rājya and 26 gāvudas (in length) of Bārakūru and Maṅga-lūru. Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka constructed a maṭha for Virūpākshadēva and having purchased for 200 varahas some land called gorute in the village Kuppāṭa from Kēśava-hebāruva, son of Aṅṇi-hebāruva of that village, made a gift of the same for bhikshā in the maṭha . The gift was made in the presence of god Šaṅkaranārāyaṇa, a sacred place in Tuļu-rājya, for the final beatitude of the parents of Sadāśiva-nāyaka (viz. Chauđappa and Tirumamma). cells.reference: ARSIE., 1901, No. 55; SII., VII, No. 229; TS., No. 56
cells.object: In a field one mile south-east from the Traveller's Bungalow.
cells.remarks: Mentions Maṅgarasa-vođeya as governor of Maṅgalūru-rājya and Mañjaṇṇa-adhikāri as the officer ( adhikāri ) of Bidireya-sthala. During the period of Vikru-chauṭa, Maimđa, son of Vudiyara Neletantri Kēśava-seṭṭi and others inclusive of the five horahinavaru created a dēvasya grant of land to god Chanđōgra Pārśvadēva of the basadi and the pontiff ( guru ) of Bidire, for worship, offerings, for maintaining 2 kaṇapāṭikas for 4 months of chāturmāsya for cocoanut oil for perpetual lamp for the kāpāṭi etc. The gift was made with all its incomes, rights etc. like kiḥu, mēlu, duḥkha, vosaga, naṭju, biḥu, kuṅdāji and keṅgoṅđa . The gift was made with the consent of the ballāṭus and in the presence of Abhinava Chārukīrti-paṇṭita, obviously the pontiff of the basti at Mūđabidare.

cells.date: Śaka 1351, Saumya, Māgha śu. 5, Thursday = 1430 A. D.. January 29, Sunday.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1901, No. 33; SII., VII 202, TS., No. 63
cells.object: On the north wall of the  Gaddige-maṇḍapa  in the Hosa-basti, left of entrance.
cells.remarks: The king is described as turuka-mahā-haya-prabalasainya-vidāri . He is said to have inaugurated the Tribhuvana-chūḍāmaṇi-chaityālaya at Bidire in Nagire-rājya and consecrated the image of Chandraprabha-tirthaṅkara in bronze and made arrangements for worship (śṛi bali ) in the basadis at Gērasoppe, Beļuguļapura, Chandragutti, Honnāvara and Vēņupura at the instance of his preceptor Virasēna, had a copper covering to the 3rd nilaya , supplied silver vessels, etc. to the Tribhuvana-chūđāmaņi-chaityālaya. His wife Nāgaladēvi had a māna-stambha erected and daughters Lakshmi and Pančitadēvi arranged for feeding. The genealogy of Bhairava is given as follows: Tāyapparasa was the chief of Tiļivalļipura in Chandragutti-kampaņa. Bhairava, son of Tāyapparasa, married Māņikadēvi, daughter of Samgama and also Nāgaladēvi, daughter of Bommarasi, sister of Tayapparasa. The record is of literary merit, being in prose and verse.

cells.date: Śaka 1398, Durmukhi, Māgha śu. 10. Friday=1477 A.D., January 24.
cells.object: On a slab built into the wall of the Kshētrapāla shrine in the same basti.
cells.remarks: States that while Viṭṭharasoḍeya was governing Maṅgalūru-rājya, during (the administration of) Siṅgappa-daṇṇāyaka, [Mellamṭa] Sauṭire-seṭṭi of Pērala Karaṇamtata-bali and his alīya Kēchiya Dēvaru-seṭṭi of Chittipāđi supplied ṭhāṇa-divige, dēhāra etc. and made a grant of land for worship in the two gandhakuṭis of the middle storey ( naḍuvaṇa-nele ) of Chandraprabhsavāmi of Tribhuvanachūḍāmaṇi-chaityālaya and also donated a house for the priest to live in. It states that they donated lands, after purchase, for 400 saṅṇa-pratāpa (coins) from Saṅkara-[vojōṭti ?] a Brāhmaṇa of Kemmutemaru, one of the four ūrs in Mūḍillara-dēśa and those lands were leased out. This charter was given (to the donor ?) by the samasta halaru and emṭu-praje seṭṭikāṇas of Bidire at the instance of Chārukīrti-paṇḍitadēva.

cells.date: Śaka 1437, Yuva, Vaiśākha śu. 5, Thursday=1515 A.D., April 19.
cells.object: On another slab in the Gurugala-basti
cells.remarks: While Ratnappa-oḍeya belonging to the family of Baicha-daṇḍādhipa was governing Maṅgalūru-Bārakūru-rājya, at the instance of Munibhadradēva (disciple of ?) Abhinava Chārukīrti-paṇḍita and with the īpermission of the eight seṭṭikāṇas and four eļames of Bidire, 33 individuals (named) donated 660 doḍḍa varahas at the rate of 20 doḍḍa varaha gas , each out of which land was purchased after recording the purchase on copper-plates. It is stipulated that from out of the income from tenure from those lands paddy worth 100 varahas gifted for the daily worship and the remaining set apart for Śāstra-dāna . Varddhamāna Śrī Avve of Sēna-gaṇa, Ajila Pāmḍi-seṭṭi, Chauṭa Sāṭtaya-seṭṭi are some of the donors named. Ratnappa-oḍeya is eulogised as sapta-saptati-durgādhiśvara , Jaina-param-āgamōddharaṇa. dattāvadhāna etc.

cells.remarks: This incomplete record in verse and prose highly eulogises the Nagire chief mahāmaṇḍalē-śvara Jinadāsa Sālūva Malla, son of Śāṭkarāṭbā and Bayyaṇēṭdra belonging to Sōma-vaṭ śa and Kāśyapa-gōtra who was governing Haiva and Koṇkaṇa-rājyas and gives a list of his ancestors commencing from Sālūva Nāraṇa and Nāgaṇa of Kshēmapura. They are: Hom-na, Kāma-nṛipāla Māvarasa, Haive-rājēndra, Kēśavarāja, Saṭgamēṭdra, Bhairava, Immaḍi 1 Bhairava and Aṭbirāya. His nephew Jagadēva, son of his elder sister Mallidēvi had been 1 installed as the crown-prince ( yuvarṇja ), The record stops abruptly.

cells.date: Śaka 1282, Plava, Mēsha 5, Sunday. Irregular. The  tithi  = 1361 A.D., March 30, Tuesday, the Śaka year being 1283.
cells.remarks: Two sides of a slab set up in front of the well called Pustaka-tirtha. Much damaged. Records an endowment of land made by Mādarasa, the governor of Maṅgalūru, for burning a perpetual lamp before the deity enshrined in the maṭha at Kaṭlavāđi, a hamlet of Nayirāđi. In a panel on the top of this slab is cut in relief a liṅga in a shrine flanked on one side by the sun with a devotee in kneeling posture while on the other is found a crescent moon and a bull.

cells.date: Šaka 1333 (current), Viřōdhikřit, Márgašira šu. 5, Sunday =1431 A.D., November 10 Saturday.
cells.object: Copper-plate in the possession of N. Krishnayya'
cells.remarks: While Ampnappa, son of Dēvarāja was ruling Mampgaļūru-rājya, on the orders of prādhāna Hariyappa-dampāyaka-vođeya, his subordinate Kriyāratidēva administering Tiļunādi, during his visit to Puttūr made of a grant of a brahmādāyā land to Pādamūlīka Natĵoji Subbampna who was one of the brothers hailing from the bank of the river Pulinā. The donee is stated to be worshiping god Mehādēva installed by himself. The grant was made at the request of Senameya when the image was buried in the earth probably owing to a disaster. The brahmadāya land which was purchased from Pađyapa-arasa of Bamga for 223 varahas at a place called kambāļatimāru is stated to have been given in perpetuity with the condition that the taxes are to be paid within the prescribed time.

cells.date: Prabhava, Pushya ba. 3 Makara[-saṅkrānti ?] = 1387 A.D., December 27, Friday, f.d.t. .38
cells.object: On a stone near the north wall of the  prākāra  of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary and much damaged. Mādhava-mantri, the famous ruler of Gōva and Āraga who defeated the Muslims, appears to have granted some lands for the worship of the god and for free distribution of food to the Brāhmaṇas at Kukke. The record is in verse and pose. The verses at the commencement seem to record the tradition about the settlement of Kumārasvāmi and Śēsha in this place. The extant portion refers to Kaḍala.

cells.date: Śaka 1329, Vyaya. Chaitra śu. 1 = 1406 A.D., March 21, Sunday. The Śaka year was current.
cells.remarks: Set of 3 copper-plates in the same temple. Bāchappa-vođeya of Gōve was governing Maṅgalūru-rajya under the orders of the king. It registers a gift of charities to the god of Kukke in Kaḍaba-sthala. It consists of money paid by the four pādamūligas of the place from the lands belonging to the god, and other gifts by others for offerings etc. Bāchaṇṇa wrote the record. Some details of money incomes paid are: 16 haṇas of kulada haṇa , 160 kāṭi gadyāṇas per annum; 54 kā ga from the kilōk-kal , 40 kā ga . from jōđi ; 11 kā ga for muđes of paddy 5 kā-ga . for kaṭṭha kāṇike together 270 kā ga described as the charity of Bukkarāya. Details of expenditure are also recorded.

text.object: On one copper-plate in the same temple.
text.remarks: Mentions the father and grandfather of the king namely Gōpālarāju and Āraviṭi Rāmarāju. Rańgaparaju. Records the grant by the king of the villages Haļebēlūru in Maļali-hōbaļ and Dođanāgara, a part of Bayikēri in Keibboṭtu-nāđu of Bēlūru-sthaļa, and a field in Kogađuvaļli in Kebbeṭtu-nāđu for offerings to the god in the Subrahmaṇya temple and for feeding(pilgrims). The record was written by  rāyasada  Vābaṇṇa (an officer under?) Lakharse paṁta. Poṭtibattu (son of?) Mākabattu engraved it- Cf. KN, 1073 above

cells.date: Śaka 1631 (mistake for 1621), Bahudhānya, Āśvija śu. 15=1698 A.D., October 9, Sunday.
cells.remarks: ARSIE; 1928-29, No. 5; MAR., 1943, No. 51 On copper-plates in the Subrahmaṇya temple. Registers gift of the village Subbarāyapura in Māgaḍi-sīma to the Subrahmaṇya temple for daily worship, offerings, and burning of lamps, by Immaḍi Doddavirappa-gauḍa, son of Mummaḍi Kempe-gauḍa and grandson of Immaḍi Kempe-gauḍa of the Sadāśiva-gōtra, the lord of Elahamkā-nāḍu. This gift is said to have been made by the donor in gratitude for the birth of a son to him called Kempavira-gauḍa. The king Śriraṇga, had lost all his powers by the time of this record.

cells.date: Šaka 1281, Vikāri, Pushya ba. 30, Sunday=1360 A.D., January 19
cells.object: On a slab built into the wall of Padmanābha-bhaṭṭa's house, in Mūđakēri.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land, after purchase, by Kālimarasa 6 son of Bamkarasa of Hubbalĵi to the satra attached to the maṭha of god Sōmanātha of Tambulagere for feeding 12 Brāhmaṇas therein as also the cook. This maṭha was got built by the 3 seṭṭikāras of mūxukēri and 150 eļame and others after purchasing (the site belonging to the temple?). Gifts for the carpenter, potter etc., also are recorded. Bārakūru-rājya was being governed by ma-hāprādhāna Malleya-daṇṇāyaka.

cells.remarks: Under orders from the king, mahāpradhāna Malleya-daṇṇāyaka was governing the Bārakūru-rājya. cells.date: Šaka 1282, Šārvari, Mārgasira śu. 15, Sunday, lunar eclipse = 1360 A.D., November 23. Monday.
cells.object: On a slab in Paramēśvara-bhaṭṭa's house.
cells.remarks: When mahāpradhāna Malleya-daṇṇāyaka was governing Bārakūru-rājya, Nāgaṇṇa-seṭi made a gift of paddy from the land jointly owned by him and Hiriya Allāla-seṭi at Basurūru and also 8 ga along with the income from tax on garden for the feeding house attached to his maṭha 18 Brahmaṇas were to be fed in the chhatra . To this several others also made gifts. The sweeper-woman ( besavitti ) of the chhatra was also gifted paddy. This was to be maintained by Nāgaṇṇa-seṭi and in case (after him ?) his family members could not the hataru of Mūḥukeri were to see that they maintain.

cells.date: Śaka 1293, Virōdhikṛit, Āśvija ba. 30, solar eclipse=1371 A.D., October 9. Thursday.
cells.object: On the fourteenth slab close to the west wall of the Sōmēśvara temple at Mūḍakeri.
cells.remarks: Mahāpradhāna Gōparasa-oĵeya was governing the Bārakūru-rājya. A gift of land in Tantrāḍi was made by Duggu-biṁnāṇiti of Huvabbeya-baļi on the death of herĵson Narasimga-biṁnāṇi to feed a Brāhamṇa daily in the temple of Sōmanātha of Mūṛukēri. The gift land was purchased, and made over to Kṛishna-maṁḍacha who was to supply 30 mūḍas of paddy (or its equivalent 10 muḍes of rice) without offering any excuse of draught or famnine. After thejdecease of the donor, it was stipulated that her progeny were to maintain the gift.

cells.date: Śaka 1294, Paridhāvi, Vaiṣākha śu. 10, Monday=1372 A.D., April 13.
cells.reference: ARISE., 1901, No. 181 A; SII., VII, No. 387
cells.object: Slab in a garden to the left of the road leading to Chauļikēri,
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land for feeding 12 Brāhmaṇas and 1 cook in the maṭha within his garden at Kellamgere of ChōJiyakēri by Māji, mother of Ayyappa, son of Iśānya-bhaṭṭa, after purchase from Kōṭeyappa, son of Tammaya-sēnabōva, Mādiyakka, daughter of Chāvakka and others, Details of 13 tāras (money) spent per day-amounting to 55 ga hon per annum are given. cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land yielding 15 muđe of rice in votada hāne , after purchase from the temple, for arranging for the recital of Purāṇa in the Vināyaka temple of Kellamgere, with the consent of the seṭikāras and halaru of Chauļiyakēri by Sriraṅga-seṭṭi, aļiya of Balladēva-seṭṭi of Ariya-baļi, when mahāpradhāna Bācharasa-vođeya was administering Bārakūru-rājya A futher gift of land belonging to Hoṅagaṇa Brahmanātha (temple) (after purchase) for rudrapāje by the same donor is also recorded.

cells.date: Saka 1301, Kāļayukta, Dvitiya Jyēshtha śu. 15, Friday, lunar eclipse=1378 A.D., June 11, the Śaka year being current.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1901, No. 126; SII., VII, No. 316; TS., No. 57
cells.object: On the eleventh slab close to the west wall of the Sōmētvaia temple,  Māđakrēi
cells.remarks: Mahāpradhāna Bommarasa-vođeya is said to be governing Bārakūru-rājya when Kuđinira Hari made a gift of land for burning lamps in the sanctum, the circumambulatory wall, nandi-maṇṭapa etc. on every full moon day. Two brothers, Vishṇu-holļa and Vāsudēva-holļa made a gift of land of the sowing capacity of 20 mūđes to the deity. The tenant of the land was to make over 5½ mūđes of rice to the temple. One mūđe towards tax was exempted from payment by Chavuđappa-ayya, the chief of the ūru , the aya of the temple and Chavuđappa-ayya of Mamgalūru, with the consent of the six of the ūru . Bommarasa wrote the record.

text.object: On the eleventh slab close to the west wall of the Sōmētvaia temple,  Māđakrēi
text.remarks: Mahāpradhāna  Bommarasa-vođeya is said to be governing Bārakūru-rājya when Kuđinira Hari made a gift of land for burning lamps in the sanctum, the circumambulatory wall,  nandi-maṇṭapa  etc. on every full moon day. Two brothers, Vishṇu-holļa and Vāsudēva-holļa made a gift of land of the sowing capacity of 20  mūđes  to the deity. The tenant of the land was to make over 5½  mūđes  of rice to the temple. One  mūđe  towards tax was exempted from payment by Chavuđappa-ayya, the chief of the  ūru , the  aya  of the temple and Chavuđappa-ayya of Mamgalūru, with the consent of the six of the  ūru . Bommarasa wrote the record.

cells.remarks: Mentions mahāpradhāna Bommarasa-ođeya as governor of Bārakūra-rājya. Records gifts of money for rudrapīje , feeding 3 Brāhmaṇas burning lamps of ghee, offering paṭchānīrita , supply of garlands of tulaši etc. in the temple of Sōmaidēva of Maṇigārakēri by Nāgave. wife of Rāmaṇṇa-seṭti, (son of) Kavili-seṭti. The three seṭṭikāras and all the halaru of Maṇigārakēri of Bārakūru were to protect this.

cells.date: Śaka 1302, Raudri=1380-81 A.D.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1901, No. 135; SII., VII, No. 325; IS., No. 53
cells.object: On a slab near the well in the Gōpālakṛishṇa temple.
cells.remarks: Mentions mahāpradhāna Bommarasa-ođeya as governing the Bārakūru-rājya and states that Kumāra Mādhavasvāmi set up the image of Gōpinātha in the Bārakūra-maṭha. The money income from haḍike of the village belonging to Bhaṇḍiya-maṭha formerly granted by his master ( svāmi king ?), Dēvarāya, was to be divided into 3 shares, one of which was to be utilised for feeding Brāhmaṇas on specified days and for study of Vēdas in the temple of Saumyadēva, the second for the daily performance of rudrapūje to god Temkkadēva of Bhaṇḍiya-maṭha and the third for god Gōpinātha. A water shed was to be maintained in the Gōpinātha temple for which unalienable land was gifted.

cells.remarks: ARSIE. 1901, No. 156; SII., VII, No. 353; TS., No. 57 ©n another slabi n the Sōmanāthēśvara temple at Maṇigārakeri. When Mallappa-ođeya was governing Bārakūrarājya under orders from the king, Bemma-ṇṇa-seṭti and Māda setṭi, sons of Kaṁkaṇiti of Dōrājara-baḥi, made a gift of land for rudrapūje and feeding four Brāhmaṇās in the temple of Sōmaiyadēva of Maṇigārakēri, from out of their brahmadāya . cells.remarks: While Śamkaradēva-vođeya was governing Bārakūra-rajya Kēšava-nāyaka, son of Vijaya-nāyaka made a gift of land in damđebeĵtu in Ayirađi for charity on amāvāsve and dvādaśi in the temple of Sōmanātha of Mañigáđakēri. At the request of Chikkaṇṇa. the sthānapati of the Hattukēri of Bārakūru, the king sent mahāpradhāna Bāchaṇṇa of Göve, to enquire into the dislocation caused by Mahābaladēva who took away the aṇya-māṇya-samaya-saṁkēta (?) of the seṭitana of the halaru of Hattukēri, the nakhare, hamjāmāna etc. of Bārakūru. Bāchappa made some adjustments and at the instance of the king granted lands as maṇṇna māṇya honna jāvaḥi (?) The income was to be used also for pātra-bhoga of god Nāraṇadēva made over to Dēvasvāmi(?) parivāraka , and the gifts made over to Maṭha Dēvaṇa.

cells.date: Śaka 1338, Manmatha, Jyēshṭha, śu. 12, Monday = 1415 A.D., May 20, the Śaka year being current.
cells.object: On a slab in the same temple.
cells.remarks: States that Śāṭkaradēva-ođeya was governing the Bārakūru-rājya. Amṛitaprajñā and Nārāyaṇagiri, disciples of Amṛitēndra-tīrtha, who was himself a disciple of Ānandasarasvatī made a gift of 17 mūđes of paddy in the three villages of Muga for feeding Brāhmaṇas on the occasion of the anniversary ( guru samārādhana ) of Ānandsarasvati of Mugilahaļi. It is stated that Nārāyaṇagiri gave up his claim over paddy, to Amṛitprayña for a consideration and the later, in turn handed over (the management ?) of Pejavogara-maṭha and the land belonging to it, Cf. KN 1111 above

cells.date: Śaka 1343, Śārvarin, Summer month ( bēsigeya tiṅgalù ) = 1420-21 A.D.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1901, No. 160; SII., VII, No. 357; TS., No. 61
cells.object: On the sixth slab in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Śaṅkaradē[va]-ođeya was governing of Bārakūra-rājya, when Dēvaṇṇa-ayya, son of Nāgaṇṇa-ayya, the younger brother of Hariharadēva-ayya and six others made a gift of oil for dipōtsava in Sōma-maṭha of god Sōmanātha of Maṇigāragēri. It is said that the originally taxes on houses, lands, Brahmapuri etc., in Bārakūru had now been taken back and in lieu of it Hariharadēva-ayya made a gift of oil as saṅrakshā-bhōga (in lieu of ?) lands in Hosakeře in Bārakūru to the uļāru of Kanyāna. Chavuđappa-ayya, Narahari-bhaṭṭa, the ārādhyas who were royal pontiffs ( rāya-rāja-guru ) etc. figure as witnesses.

cells.date: Śaka 1347, Krōdhi, Phālguṇa śu. 15, Bhaumavāra. !The Śaka year was current. The  tithi  = 1425 A.D., March 4, Sunday.
cells.object: On a slab near the tank in front of the Pañchaliṅgēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Mahāmantrin Narasimhadēva-ođeya, the governor of Bārakūra-rājya made a gift of land for feeding Brāhmanas on the Nīvarātī day in the presence of Pañchaliñgēśvara and mūla-sthāna Mārkandēśvara of Kōṭeyakēri in Bārakūru in the maṭha established by him to the north of the tank of Mārkandēśvara temple, and also for offerings to ĝods Pañchaliñga and Vi hpumurti of Madhya-sthāna. It is stated that the nāḍavas of Paṭuvakōne illegally occupied the land adjacent to theirs, which had fallen fallow and the governor having enquired into it took that land from them and donated that land to the temple. The nāḍus of Kamdāvura, Kōṭa, Brahmūru and Nīruvāra and Paṭuv.kōna figure as witnesses to the record written by the ārādhya of Koṭaganūru.

cells.date: Śaka 1353, Sādhāraṇa, Bhādrapada ba. 10. Monday=1430 A.D., September 11, Monday f.d.t. . 4. Śaka year was current.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1901, No. 119; SII., No. 309; TS., No. 65
cells.object: On the first slab close to the west wall of the Sĵmēśvara temple, Mūṭakēri.
cells.remarks: Records the settlement of a dispute between the Mūṭukēri and Chauļiyakēri of the hattu-kēri of Bārakūru in regard to business dealings in sugar. Mahāpradhāna Chamṭarasa-ođeya who was governing Bārakūru and Tuļu-rājyas invited both the parties, advised them suitably whereupon the five and the halaru of Mūṭukēri of Chauļiyakēri and the three seṭṭikāṭas and 150 eļames together agreed to share equally rice, wheat, gram, green gram, back gram, sugar cane etc., imported from above the ghats and that sugar should be stocked in the godown ( maļige ) and sold to customers when prices improved, and that they would settle any dispute between themselves. Aļhavane Nagarasa, the pajika of Rēvođeyappa, the karaṇa , wrote the record. It would appear that this person drafted the record since it also states Mayaṇkona baraha i.e. writing (engraving?) of Māyaṭka (?).

cells.date: Śaka 1353, Virōdhikṛit, Summer month ( bēsageya tiṭṭgalū =1431 A.D., April-May)
cells.object: On the fourth slab in the same place.
cells.remarks: Damaged. States that Chamṭarasa-ođeya was governing Bārakūru-Tulu-rājyas and records a gift of land to god Sōmanātha of Mūṭukēri by Vishṇu-bhaṭṭa and Saṭkara-bhaṭṭa belonging to Kāśyapa-gōtra and Yājuś-śākhā, sons of Śīidhara-bhaṭṭa of Sānāti, brother ( vođavuṭṭiduvaru ) of Baṇkēsa-hayiva, the mahāprabhu of a village (Kaṭagi?) The gift land was situated in the village Ānagali which the donor had received from the king on the occasion of a lunar eclipse. Also registers a gift by Jātaka-bhaṭṭa, for several services, offerings etc. to god Sōmanātha. A number of individuals are cited as witnesses. Details are not clear.

cells.object: On a pillar in the outer enclosure of the Pañchaliṅgēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: ARSIE. 1901, No. 177; SII., VII, No. 382 Mentions Perumāle-daṇṇāyaka as administering the kingdom along with the king and mahāpradhāna Chomḍarasa-vođeya the Bārakūru-rājya. It st ipu ates that rice unused on ēkadāśi day was to be gifted to the Brāhmaṇas along with oil, every Saturday, Kannapa, the sculptor wrote the record.

cells.date: Śaka 1362, Siddhārthin, Vaiśākha śu. 3, Thursday=1437 A.D., April 16
cells.object: On the thirteenth slab in the same place.
cells.remarks: While Lakhanna-daṇṇāyaka was managing the kingdom at the instance of the king, Anna-ppa-vođeya who was governing Bārakūru-Maṅgalūru-rājyas made a gift of 59 kāṭi ga to jōyisa Rāmaṇna, son of Hemmāđi-jōyisa of Maudgalya-gōtra and Rik-śākhā (residing at) Haṭṭiyakuduru on the occasion of the newmoon day, a Monday. This tithi occurred on April 13, Monday, Chaitra-amāvāsya. It further records a gift of 2 hons to god Sōmanātha of Mūṛukēri for a day's worship on Mahānavami , by Rāmaṇna annually, as a rakshābhōga of Chanđikādēvi of Haṭṭiyakuduru. Aṅṇappa wrote the record with the approval of the 3000 of Bārakūru.

cells.date: Śaka 1372, Śukla, Chaitra ba. 10 = 1449 A.D., April 17, Thursday, f.d.t. .09. The Śaka year was current.
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1901, No. 145; SII., VII, No. 337; TS., No. 72
cells.object: On the third slab in the Gaṇapati temple.
cells.remarks: Rāyarasa-ođeya who was the governor of Bārakūra-rājya made gift of 68 kāṭi gadyāṇas for specified worships and offerings, to god Vināyaka of Chōļiya Kellamgere, so that the danger that had been annoying the king be cleared. The gift was made on the solar eclipse day, on the sea-shore. This eclipse occurred in Adhika Bhādrapada month, 1448 A.D., August 29. Several witnesses are named.

cells.date: Śaka 1375, Śrīmukha, Māgha śu. 10, Wednesday = 1454 A.D., January 9.
cells.object: Slab lying in the compound of the old Jaina-basti opposite Sōmanātha temple.
cells.remarks: Dēmaṇṇa-vođeya who was governing Bārakūru-rājya under orders from mahāpradhāna Siṅgappa-daṇṇāyaka, made a gift of 11 ga due as tax to the palace from Keļakoppariya-ūru in Mughu, with the consent of the 14 jananis , for the pātrabhōga of god Sōmanātha and hāladhāre of Ādiparamēśvara (each deity getting equally 5½ hons ). The record refers to the burning of the dharmasthaļa of aḥavaṇṭeya haravari gifted earlier by Virupaṇa-daṇāyaka to Chārukirṭi-paṇḍita of Beļuguļa. The present gift appears to have been made in that connection. Karaṇika Sāypa wrote the record. A supplement added later states that janni Śivaṇṇi-nāyaka, his younger brother Ēśvara-sēnabōva and son Dēvaṇṇa-sēnabōva, gave land on tenure ( biḍāruvāra ) which amount was made over to god Ādidēva.

cells.date: Śaka 1380, Bahudhānya, Āśvija śu. 1, Friday = 1458 A.D., September 8. The lunar eclipse occurred in the previous month of Bhādrapada, August 24, Thursday.
cells.object: On the tenth slab close to the west wall of the Sōmēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: ARSIE. 1901, No. 125; SII., VII, No. 315 While Siddappa-daṇṇāyaka was managing the affairs of the kingdom. under his and the king's orders, Guruvappa-vođeya was governing Bārakūru-rājya. At the instance of the king and the daṇṇāyaka as also of Aṇṇapa-nāyaka, Gururāya made a gift of money income from kuļa-upachāra of the village Kūrāḍi in Kela-nāđu as also part of sēnabōva-varttane , hostina-kāṇike etc. to god Sōmanātha of Mūḥukēri, on the occasion of a lunar eclipse. The gift was made for the merit and prosperity of the king.

cells.date: Śaka 1380 (expired), 1381 (current), Bahudhānya, Mārgaśira ba. 13, Sunday = 1458 A.D., December 3
cells.object: On another slab in the Gaṇapati temple.
cells.remarks: States that when Guruvappa-ođeya was the governor of the Bārakūra-rājya, Vallabhadēva of Kāmavaṭṭa, (an officer) of the big palace ( hiriya aramane ), of Vijānagari who had received from the king the village Rājādi-Kaṅnyāna, made a gift of money of 70 kāṭi gadyāṇas from out of its income to god Kallamgaṛe Vināyaka of Chōlīyakēri for dipōtsava during three days of dipāvaļi festival. It cites the 12 jananis of nālu ūru of Rājādi Kaṅnyāna, the horahinavaru and fifty two okkađlus , besides other individuals as witnesses. The five halaru of Chōlīyakēri and (?) Vāsudēva (sold ?) a house to Vallabhadēvarasa.

cells.date: Śaka 1421, Siddhārthi, Śrāvaṇa śu. 1, Tuesday = 14 69  A.D., July 9.
cells.object: On a slab at the entrance into the same temple.
cells.remarks: Sādhāraṇadēva-vođeya who was governing Bārakūru-rājya under orders from mahāpradhāna Narasaṇa-nāyaka, made a gift of (1 nd yielding 44 do ṭa varahas ?) in Chittapāyi within Kōṭa-grāma of Bārakūra-sime, on the da of solar eeļipse, in Mārgaśira ba. 30 of Kālayuk-tākshi, (1498 A.D., December 13) to Nāraṇadēva, son of Sōvaṇṇa-sūtra. The donee made a gift of money (30 dođa va ga per annum) accrued as interest upon 300 dođa va ga received which he borrowed from the halaru (lay disciples) of Māṇika-basti, for rakshā-bhōga and Kārttikapūje , in the temple of Sōmanātha of Maṇigāragēri, and for nandādipti to god Vishṇumūrti of Huruṇitta-madhyastara-maṭha at Chītrāpīđi. Karaṇika Mallarasa wrote the record.

cells.object: On a slab on the outside close to the west wall of the Sōmēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: States that under the orders of Rāmarāja-nāyaka, grandson of Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka of Keladi, Achchappa-vođeya was governing Bārakūru-rājya. Nāraṇa-seṭti of Kaluđichi-bali, son of Nārasimha-seti, with the approval of the halaru of Mūrūkēri, in the presence of god Sōmanātha, got a maṭha built to the west of the rājāṅgaṇa of the temple and for feeding 6 Brāhmaṇas daily therein made a gift of land, after purchase from the halaru .

cells.date: Šaka 1358, Rākshasa, Mārgaśira śu. 14, Sunday=1435 A.D., December 4, The Šaka year was current.
cells.object: Copper-plate set in the possession of Nagendra Toļara.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land called Ampāra-haravari in Mumga-nāđu included in Bārakūru-rājya and of certain incomes from tolls, made by mahāpradhāna Aṇṇappa-ođeya to Toļahara Sampkara-nāyaka who was administering Yeļre, in return for which the latter was to build a maļha attached to the temple of Hattara Nāiāyaṇadēva at Bārakūru and feed there in six brāhmaṇas daily. Annappa-ođeya is stated to have been governing the Bārakūru-rājya.

cells.date: Śaka 1359(current), Nala, Chaitra śu.10, Friday. The  tithi  occurred on 1436 1 A.D., March 27, Tuesday, f.d.t. .08
cells.object: Slab built into the north wall of Kṛishṇa-maṭha.
cells.remarks: ARSIE. 1901, No. 109; SII., VII, No. 296 Under the orders of the king and Siṅgaṇa-daṇṇāyaka who was administering the whole kingdom ( pāripatyā ), Aṇṇappa-vođeya was governing Bārakūru-rājya. This latter raided Śiva!li in the year Ānanda and consequently there was dislocation and disorder. The hattukēri and those of kaṭṭaĉe of Bārakūru consoled the people of Siva!li and under instructions from Aṇṇappa-vođeya, Siṅgarasa-vođeya made a gift of land, to set in order the temples at Śiva!li. Karaṇika Purushōttama wrote the record. The villagers of Muḍila Niḍumbūru and Aṇṇappa-vođeya, figure as signatories.

cells.date: Šaka 1397, Manmatha, Pushya šu. 5 = 1476 A.D., January 1.
cells.object: On a slab built into the wall surrounding the tank near the same  maṭha .
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions Viṭharasa-ođeya of Bārakūru as governing when Dēvarāđiya Kumđa-heggađe, Mardda-heggađe, Kimṇika-heggađe of Yēļimja and another came to some agreement among themselves and undertook to protect each other's interests and settle their differences amicably. But the details are not clear. It is stated that if Kumđa-heggađe attacks Mardda-heggađe lending ears to unfriendly people, he has to pay rice to Kāppinadē va(?)for having committed the sin of Brahmēti . Similar stipulations are spelt out for other members also.

cells.date: Šaka 1536, Pramādi, Vaišakha šu. 12=1613 A.D., April 21, Wednesday, the Šaka year being current.
cells.object: Slab built into the wall of the Krīshṇa temple.
cells.remarks: The king's subordinate, Veñkaṭappa-nāyaka of Keĵadi, is stated to be administering Tulū and Male-rājyas. The Kṛīshṇa temple in Uđupi which was originally built in wood was now got reconstructed in stone by Vēdavēdya-tirtha-śripāda, disciple of Vādirājātīrtha-Śripāda a devotee of god Hayagriva, who had been the pontiff of the maṭha and the temple, in his turn parvāya . The sanctum and the maṭha in front was got constructed in stone and covered with copper in two layers( yerađuneles and pinnacles consecrated. Rāmakṛīshṇappa-vođeya son of Vōbarasayya, the mudre (seal bearer ?) of the Chinna-bhaṇdāra (treasury) of the Keĵadi chief, while governing Bārakūru, with the permission of the Keĵadi chief and the king made a grant of the village Keĵagaṇa Hūvinakere in Nālvattu-nāđu of Bārakūru-rājya in the month of Kārttika, śu. 15, lunar eclipse day(1613 A.D. October 18, Monday, on the occasion of the reconsecration of god Kṛīshṇa, in the presence of god Murugēśvara. Vyāsappa an officer was deputed to set up stones bearing the marks of Śaikha and Chakra on all the four boundaries of the maṭha . The pontiff himself made a grant of money-income for worship and offerings to the god. This gift was made in Makara 4, Māgha śu. 1, Sthiravara, of the same year (1614 A.D., January 1, Saturday). The record was obviously set up after this date. It states that the expenses incurred by the maṭha over and above the donations received from out side was considered (by the pontiff) as charity.

cells.object: Slab in the  prākāva  of Janārdana temple.
cells.remarks: Basavaṇṇa-ođeya was governing Bārakūru-rajya. It registers a gift of land for feeding a Brāhmaṇa daily in the temple of god Janārdanadēva of Yermmāla by Lakhkhappa of Kaļalige, son of Gaṇapaṇṇa, after purchase, with the permission of Māraṁma-verggađe the ājanti (?) of theplace, the 24 praje and janani of the place and the pādamlūis of the temple. Vishṇu-nelli, Nāraṇa-nelhi and Kēśava-nelli, the pādamlūis sold the land, which was made free of imposts. Cf. KN 1222 below.
